## Setting up
1. After adding weight plates to the machine’s weight sleeve, straddle the machine as you are facing toward the weights.
2. Place your feet onto the foot plates and your chest onto the chest pad such that your whole body is inclined forward.
    1. You will be most stable when the entirety of the soles of your feet are in contact with the foot plates.
3. Depending upon your height and leg lengths, you may want to bend your knees somewhat or keep them extended to determine where your torso is situated on the chest pad.
    1. How you position your knees will be based on what feels most comfortable and stable to you, but you can initially see how you feel when positioning your knees to allow the uppermost aspect of the chest pad to be approximately level with your collarbone.
    2. Individuals who have longer legs will typically feel more comfortable when using a somewhat more bent knee position, while those with shorter legs will typically feel more comfortable with extended knees.
4. After determining which degree of knee bend places you in a comfortable position, firmly grasp the inner handles that are angled outward and backward such that your palms are facing at an angle in toward each other and backward (which is a hybrid between a neutral grip and overhand grip).
    1. Certain T-bar row machines have a pair of inner parallel handles (which allow a neutral grip) and outer handles directed straight out to the sides (which allow an overhand grip), but lack handles angled outward and backward.
    2. If your T-bar row machine does not have handles that are angled outward and backward, you can perform the [chest-supported neutral grip machine T-bar row](Chest-supported%20neutral%20grip%20T-bar%20row%201a15c6f170d880e58105e80545e3f035.md) or [chest-supported overhand grip machine T-bar row](Chest-supported%20overhand%20grip%20T-bar%20row%201a15c6f170d880a2ac20d8a1281d1d37.md) as an alternative.
5. Lift the bar up off the machine’s stopper, center the bar so that it no longer lies above the stopper, and lower it until your elbows are extended.
    1. In this bottom position, allow the weight to pull your shoulder blades apart from one another, which will likely prompt you to feel a stretching sensation in your upper back.
## Exercise technique
1. Pull the bar upward and back toward your torso by driving your elbows simultaneously upward and backward while progressively bending your elbows and pulling your shoulder blades together.
    1. Move your elbows through a path of motion that feels comfortable to you, which will typically involve flaring them out moderately away from your sides, such that your upper arms form close to 45-degree angles with your torso toward the end of the lifting phase.
    2. Keep your torso in contact with the chest pad throughout the set rather than arching your lower back to lift your chest up off the pad.
    3. Pull through your available range of motion, which will typically result in your elbows being level with your torso or slightly behind your torso at the end of the lifting phase.
    4. As a cue for training your upper back muscles, you can think about squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the pull as if you were trying to pinch a pencil with your shoulder blades.
2. Reverse the movement by lowering the bar in a controlled manner by allowing your elbows to move downward and forward until your elbows have finished extending and the bar has returned to the starting position.
    1. During the lowering phase, your shoulder blades will naturally move apart from one another, but you can exaggerate this motion by intentionally allowing the weight to pull them further apart than your resting position at the bottom, which will stretch your upper back muscles.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set and are ready to return the bar back onto the machine’s stopper.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop your [lats](../Muscles/Latissimus%20Dorsi%201905c6f170d880109e73f99ab91d4d47.md), [teres majores](../Muscles/Teres%20Major%201905c6f170d880dbba32f6bd22e3abe6.md), [rear delts](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Posterior%20Head%201905c6f170d880a29e5ec26f4d257c01.md), [traps](../Muscles/Trapezius%201b95c6f170d880bebf89c759b592e81f.md), and [rhomboids](../Muscles/Rhomboids%201b95c6f170d880c8a84de94f5232a509.md), which are assisted by your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md).

## Setting up
1. Approach a surface (e.g., hand rail, wall, power rack) where you can place one hand to assist with maintaining your balance while performing this exercise.
2. Place your hand onto the nearby surface for balance assistance.
    1. Maintain this hand contact throughout the set.
## Exercise technique
1. Raise your heels into the air through the available range of motion of your ankles while keeping your knees straight and your trunk upright.
2. In a controlled manner, allow your heels to descend toward the ground while continuing to keep your knees straight.
3. After your heels touch the ground, alternate between raising and lowering your heels until you have completed your set.

This exercise offers you a convenient way to train your [gastrocnemius](../Muscles/Gastrocnemius%201b95c6f170d880b59622dd4a8639aa2f.md) and [soleus](../Muscles/Soleus%201925c6f170d88052bbb6c59dc04f2e1a.md) in nearly any environment.

## Setting up
1. Lie down with your abdomen contacting the ground (i.e., in the prone position) and your head lifted slightly off the ground as you maintain a tucked chin position with your face directed toward the ground
2. With straight elbows, raise your arms outward so that they form a “Y-shape” with your torso while resting on the ground.
3. Rotate your arms so that your palms face at an angle toward each other and a little forward.
    1. If you make a thumbs-up gesture in this position, your thumb should be pointing up toward the ceiling.
## Exercise technique
1. Lift your arms up off the ground through your available shoulder range of motion while maintaining the “Y-shape” and keeping your chest in contact with the ground.
    1. Your shoulder mobility will affect how high you can raise your arms.
    2. Most people will not be able to lift their arms particularly high before reaching the end of their available range of motion.
    3. If you notice your chest lifting up off the ground during this movement, that indicates that you most likely are dynamically extending your lumbar spine, which can occur as a compensation pattern instead of lifting your arm only with your shoulder girdle muscles.
2. Reverse the motion by lowering your arms in a controlled manner until your hands lightly contact the ground while maintaining the “Y-shape.”
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise trains your [traps](../Muscles/Trapezius%201b95c6f170d880bebf89c759b592e81f.md) along with your [serratus anterior](../Muscles/Serratus%20Anterior%201955c6f170d880a8b8b9e712f2ec58e0.md), [front delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Anterior%20Head%201905c6f170d8805da59fc8f9dc0a59e4.md), and [side delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Lateral%20Head%201905c6f170d8804b9b6ef12253eec774.md).

## Setting up
1. With a cable station positioned to its lowest height, select your weight with the loading pin, and clip in a straight bar attachment or a multi-grip curl bar attachment.
2. While standing directly in front of the middle of the bar, squat down with extended elbows to grasp the bar firmly with approximately a shoulder-width grip as your palms are directed back toward you (i.e., an overhand grip).
    1. When squatting down, keep your lower back near a neutral position, like you have when you are normally standing upright, rather than meaningfully rounding your lower back.
3. By extending your hips and knees, stand upright with the bar while continuing to keep your elbows extended and your lower back near a neutral position.
    1. When upright, you should feel resistance from the cable, so take a step backward if you do not initially feel any resistance.
## Exercise technique
1. Shrug your shoulders upward through your available range of motion while keeping your elbows extended, which will lift the bar upward.
    1. While doing so, keep your neck in a neutral position, like you have when you are normally standing upright and looking straight ahead.
2. Reverse the motion by allowing your shoulders to descend in a controlled manner through your available range of motion, which will lower the bar.
    1. At the end of this motion, your shoulders should ideally be positioned a little lower than where they are normally situated while standing at rest due to the downward stretch that the weight can provide.
    2. If you lose resistance from the cable machine when your shoulders are fully depressed, you can take a step backward and resume your set with resistance throughout the full range of motion.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise primarily trains your [upper traps](../Muscles/Upper%20Trapezius%201925c6f170d880009e2cf04b5b29b467.md) and [levator scapulae](../Muscles/Levator%20Scapulae%201955c6f170d880048119fd4b2c6c5737.md).

## Setting up
1. Select your weight with the loading pin and adjust the seat to a height that allows your chest to rest comfortably against the chest pad.
    1. While you can initially adjust the seat to a height that situates your shoulders approximately level with the horizontal handles, the seat height that is best for you depends on the specific machine you use, and trying out different positions may be helpful.
2. If your machine has an adjustable chest pad, adjust it to a position that allows you to grasp the horizontal handles when your arms are fully outstretched forward in front of you with extended elbows.
    1. To row through your full range of motion, ideally place the chest pad far enough back that you have to push your shoulder blades forward and apart to grasp the handles with your elbows fully straight.
3. Sit down with your chest resting snugly against the chest pad and your feet flat on the floor.
4. Reach fully forward with straight elbows to grasp the horizontally directed handles firmly with your palms facing down (i.e., an overhand grip).
    1. If you were able to grasp the handles with any amount of elbow bend, you could let go of the handles and adjust the chest pad before grasping the handles again.
## Exercise technique
1. Pull the handles back toward you by driving your elbows backward while simultaneously bending them and pulling your shoulder blades together.
    1. Allow your elbows naturally to flare out away from your sides in a manner that feels comfortable to you, rather than trying to keep them tucked close to your sides (which is typically more comfortable with a closer underhand or neutral grip).
    2. Keep your chest in contact with the chest pad throughout the set.
    3. Pull through your available range of motion, which will typically result in your elbows being level with your torso or slightly behind your torso at the end of the lifting phase.
    4. As a cue for training your upper back muscles, you can think about squeezing your shoulder blades together at the end of the pull as if you were trying to pinch a pencil with your shoulder blades.
2. Reverse the movement by allowing your elbows to move forward in a controlled manner, progressively straightening until they are outstretched in front of you.
    1. Your shoulder blades will naturally move apart from one another, but you can exaggerate this motion by intentionally allowing the weight to pull them further apart than your resting position at the bottom. This will stretch your upper back muscles and may help you train them more effectively.
    2. While you do not have to perform this step extremely slowly, you should avoid letting the weight abruptly yank your arms forward in an uncontrolled fashion.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This row primarily trains your [lat](../Muscles/Latissimus%20Dorsi%201905c6f170d880109e73f99ab91d4d47.md), [teres major](../Muscles/Teres%20Major%201905c6f170d880dbba32f6bd22e3abe6.md), [rear delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Posterior%20Head%201905c6f170d880a29e5ec26f4d257c01.md), [traps](../Muscles/Trapezius%201b95c6f170d880bebf89c759b592e81f.md), and [rhomboids](../Muscles/Rhomboids%201b95c6f170d880c8a84de94f5232a509.md), which are assisted by your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md).

## Setting up
1. Add your desired weight to an adjustable plate-loaded EZ bar on top of the preacher curl bench, or place a fixed weight EZ bar on top of the preacher curl bench.
2. Adjust the seat to a height that allows you to rest your elbows and most of the back of your upper arms (i.e., triceps) on the sloped arm pad when sitting on the seat.
    1. The proper setting will typically result in the top of the pad being close to your armpits.
    2. Some trial and error may be needed to find the ideal seat height.
3. Sit down on the seat, and position the back of your upper arms and elbows on top of the arm pad with your feet on the ground.
4. Firmly grasp the bar with approximately a shoulder width semi-underhand grip (AKA semi-neutral grip) such that your palms are directed at an angle that is facing forward and inward.
    1. With the zig-zag-like shape of the EZ bar, you may have to rotate it initially before a near shoulder width semi-underhand grip is accessible on the bar.
    2. If the bar is a little out of your reach, you could slightly stand up and lean forward to reach the bar before sitting back down after you have grasped the bar.
    3. Your wrists should be mostly straight throughout your set after grasping the bar.
5. In the starting position, your elbows should be fully straightened with the bar no longer in contact with the bench so that you can train through a full range of motion.
    1. If this is not the case, you can mildly scoot back with an upright torso until you have reached this starting position.
## Exercise technique
1. While keeping your elbows and the back of your upper arms in contact with the bench, curl the bar upward and back toward you in an arcing motion by bending at your elbows until they are fully bent.
    1. While your forearms move through elbow motion, the rest of your body should remain stationary throughout your set.
    2. If your preacher bench allows you to curl the bar past the point when your forearms are completely vertical and perpendicular to the ground, you can finish the lifting phase after your forearms are vertical since the biceps would no longer be working beyond this point.
2. After your elbows have fully bent, reverse the motion by lowering the bar in a slow and controlled manner until your elbows have returned to a fully straightened position.
    1. Continue keeping your elbows and the back of your upper arms in contact with the bench.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set and are ready to set the bar back down onto the preacher bench.

Like other curls, this exercise can effectively train the biceps and brachialis in your upper arm along with the brachioradialis in your forearm.

## Setting up
1. Pick up a dumbbell and stand upright with approximately a shoulder width stance while holding the dumbbell at your side with an extended elbow.
2. Direct your palm so that it is facing forward.
    1. Maintain this underhand grip on the dumbbell throughout the set.
## Exercise technique
1. Curl the dumbbell upward by bending at your elbow while keeping your upper arm fixed at your side (rather than allowing your upper arm to swing forward).
2. After your elbow has fully flexed, reverse the motion by lowering the dumbbell in a controlled manner until your elbow has returned to an extended position.
    1. During the lowering phase, continue to keep your upper arm positioned by your sides.
3. Alternate between curling the dumbbell up and lowering it down until you have completed your set and are ready to repeat the exercise with your other side.

Like other curl variations, this exercise can effectively train your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md).

## Setting up
1. Position an adjustable cable to its highest setting, or approach a cable lat pulldown machine.
    1. Either type of equipment can be used interchangeably for this exercise.
2. Connect a D-handle attachment to the cable and select your weight with the loading pin.
3. Stand facing in front of the cable and slightly to the side such that one of your shoulders is in line with the cable, and with your arm that is in front of the cable, reach up to grasp the handle firmly.
4. Perform a controlled lunging motion into a half kneeling position with your knee on the side you are holding the cable, resting on the ground, after stepping backward with that side’s leg.
    1. While doing so, allow your elbow to extend and your arm to elevate to be aligned with the cable.
    2. Maintain an upright torso position and keep the center of your breastbone facing the same way as the center of your hips rather than having your trunk rotated toward one side.
    3. In this position, you should feel tension from the cable machine with your elbow extended, so if the cable remains slack (which may occur if you have very long arms), you should position yourself a little farther away from the cable station before assuming the half-kneeling position.
5. Based on your preference and what feels most comfortable, you can rotate the handle in a manner that allows you to use a neutral grip with your palm facing in toward the midline of your body or an underhand grip with your palm facing backward.
## Exercise technique
1. Drive your elbow downward and then backward in an arcing manner while progressively bending it to pull the handle down toward the side of your upper chest.
    1. Simultaneosuly pull your shoulder blade down away from your ear.
    2. Keep your forearm aligned in the same direction as the cable, which will naturally occur with the appropriate degree of elbow bend.
    3. Pull through your available range of motion, which will typically result in your elbow being level with your torso or slightly behind your torso at the end of the pull.
    4. During the initial portion of the pull, you will drive your elbow downward, but you will drive your elbow simultaneously backward and downward during the second half of the pull.
    5. After the initial portion of the pull, when your upper arm is approximately parallel with the ground, the bony prominence on the back of your elbow should be pointing predominantly forward as your upper arm is situated in front of your body, rather than having your elbow and upper arm flared out to your side.
2. Reverse the movement by bringing the handle upward in a controlled manner by allowing your elbow to move forward and upward while it progressively extends until you have returned to the starting position.
    1. Finish this step with your elbow fully straightened and your whole arm aligned with the cable.
    2. There is no need to perform this step extremely slowly, but you should avoid letting the machine’s resistance yank your arm up in an uncontrolled fashion.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set and are ready to repeat the exercise with your other side.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop your [lat](../Muscles/Latissimus%20Dorsi%201905c6f170d880109e73f99ab91d4d47.md), [teres major](../Muscles/Teres%20Major%201905c6f170d880dbba32f6bd22e3abe6.md), and [rear delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Posterior%20Head%201905c6f170d880a29e5ec26f4d257c01.md) while also meaningfully training your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md).

## Setting up
1. Adjust a cable station’s pulley to its highest level, connect a rope attachment to the cable, and select your desired weight with the loading pin.
2. Stand in front of the cable station facing the rope.
3. Reach up and grasp each end of the rope with your little fingers and adjacent aspects of your hands contacting the flat surfaces of the attachment’s rubber stoppers. Wrap your thumbs over the outside of your other fingers.

4. Take a step backward and slightly lean forward by hinging at your hips.

5. Pull your upper arms down and back until they are at your sides, with your elbows close to fully bent, so your hands are close together in front of your chest.

## Exercise technique
1. Push the rope downward and spread it apart by extending your elbows until they are straightened.
    1. At the end of this motion, your hands should be near the outer aspects of your thighs, and they should be farther apart from each other compared to when you were in the starting position.
2. Reverse the motion by bending your elbows to raise the rope in a controlled manner as your hands move closer to each other until you have returned to the starting position.

This exercise can effectively develop the [triceps](../Muscles/Triceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88032be38d4f3e73c9e4c.md), including the [long head](../Muscles/Triceps%20Brachii%20Long%20Head%201905c6f170d880b1a0a7eda6c9b74382.md), which is not trained particularly well by compound pressing exercises.

## Setting up
1. With a cable station positioned to its lowest height, clip in a straight bar attachment and select your weight with the loading pin.
2. While facing the middle of the bar, squat down or hinge at your hips with extended elbows.
3. Grasp the bar with approximately a shoulder width grip and an overhand grip (AKA reverse grip) such that your palms are directed back toward you.

To maintain a fully extended elbow position with a diagonal line of pull, you will position your upper arms slightly in front of your body by flexing at your shoulders instead of keeping your upper arms pinned to your sides (like you would with a curl that has a vertically directed resistance, such as free weights).

1. Curl the bar upward by bending at your elbows while keeping your upper arms fixed in the same position that allowed your elbows to be fully extended at the start of the rep (rather than allowing your upper arms to swing further forward).
2. After your elbows have fully flexed, reverse the motion by lowering the bar in a controlled manner until your elbows have returned to an extended position.

## Setting up

4. Move the bar up to your shoulders with your elbows fully bent underneath and slightly in front of the bar.
    1. If the load is light enough to do so, you can just curl the bar up.
    2. With a heavier load, you can perform a cheat curl, where you generate momentum with your hips to help you curl the bar up. Initially sit your buttocks back while allowing your knees to bend mildly and your torso to incline slightly forward. Then drive your hips forcefully forward while bending your elbows and mildly swinging them forward.
    3. The bar should now be in essentially the same position it would be for an overhead press.
    4. The bar should be sitting on top of the bases of your palms (AKA heels of your hands) with reasonably straight wrists. You will maintain this hand and wrist position throughout your set.
    5. While your wrists do not need to be completely straight, you should avoid holding the bar with your wrists cocked back into an excessively extended position that may contribute to an increased risk of experiencing wrist discomfort. Simply squeezing the bar hard will usually keep your wrists from cocking back excessively.
5. Press the bar up overhead in a shoulder press motion until you have fully straightened your elbows.
    1. The bar should be vertically stacked above your shoulders, hips, and knees.
    2. Rather than being excessively arched, your lower back and neck should be near a neutral position, like when you are normally standing upright and looking straight ahead.
## Exercise technique
1. Bend your elbows to lower the bar behind your head in a controlled manner. Based on your preference and what feels most comfortable to your elbows, you can select one of two approaches with respect to your elbow position.
    1. Option 1: Keep your elbows completely up with your upper arms in a vertical position throughout the rep. This will result in the bar moving in an arcing manner exclusively from your forearms hinging at your elbows.
    2. Option 2: Mildly arc your elbows forward and down while bending your elbows to lower the bar. You can mildly tuck your chin toward your chest to create additional space for the bar. This option will result in the bar moving in a closer to vertical path from a combination of shoulder and elbow motion.
    3. Neither of the approaches is inherently superior to the other, so you can feel free to try out both ways and continue using the technique you prefer.
    4. With either option, predominantly keep your elbows tucked in. However, you can allow them to flare slightly out away from your sides if that feels natural and comfortable to you.
2. Continue lowering the bar until you have fully bent your elbows or can lightly tap the base of your neck or your upper back muscles with the bar.
    1. How far you can lower the bar may be limited by the flexibility of your long head of the triceps, particularly if you keep your elbows completely up. While some lifters have the flexibility to reach near their upper back with the bar, others will reach the limit to which they can comfortably bend their elbows before that point. Do not lower the bar beyond the range that your flexibility permits without discomfort.
    2. While you do not have to perform the lowering phase with an extremely slow tempo, you should be actively controlling the weight the entire way.
3. Reverse the movement by straightening your elbows to lift the bar into the starting position overhead.
    1. You should finish with your elbows fully straightened as the bar is vertically above your shoulders.
4. Alternate between steps 1-3 until you have completed your set.
5. After you completed the lifting phase of your last rep, lower the bar in front of your head toward your shoulders like you would during an overhead press.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop the [triceps](../Muscles/Triceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88032be38d4f3e73c9e4c.md), including the [long head](../Muscles/Triceps%20Brachii%20Long%20Head%201905c6f170d880b1a0a7eda6c9b74382.md), which is not trained particularly well by pressing exercises.

## Setting up
1. Pick up a pair of dumbbells and stand upright with approximately a shoulder-width stance while holding the dumbbells just in front of your thighs with your palms facing back toward you and your elbows straight.
    1. If you do not have any experience training Jefferson curls, it is recommended that you initially try out the [bodyweight Jefferson curl](Bodyweight%20Jefferson%20curl%201ec5c6f170d880ba8e43cf305531982d.md) to determine how your body feels with this movement prior to performing a loaded variation.
## Exercise technique
1. Tuck your chin to your chest and lower the dumbbells in a slow and controlled manner by bending over and rounding your whole back through what is your comfortable range of motion while keeping your knees and elbows straight.
    1. As a cue, you can think about rounding forward each segment of your spine successively until your entire spine has achieved a rounded posture.
    2. As you progressively descend, it is natural to feel a stretching sensation in your hamstrings and back muscles.
    3. How far you can descend will be influenced by your hamstring flexibility and the available bending range of motion in your spine.
    4. If you have a high degree of mobility, you may be able to descend until the dumbbells contact the floor, but only move through a range that is painless and feels right to your body.
    5. Your arms should be directed down toward the ground throughout the exercise.
2. Reverse the movement by gradually transitioning from the bent-over position to the upright position in which you started by uncoiling your back, which will lift the dumbbells up.
    1. At the end of the ascent, untuck your chin and look straight ahead.
    2. Continue keeping your knees and elbows in a straightened position.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can dynamically train the [erector spinae](../Muscles/Thoracolumbar%20Erector%20Spinae%201bb5c6f170d880a7a719e8f6d05d00a8.md) and [deep spinal extensor muscles](../Muscles/Deep%20Intrinsic%20Thoracolumbar%20Extensors%201bb5c6f170d880f58501d5f27212caed.md) that run along your entire back, while also training your spinal mobility and hamstring flexibility.

## Setting up
1. Connect to the cable an attachment with a pair of parallel handles that are approximately shoulder-width apart or closer, select your weight with the loading pin, and sit down facing the cable station.
    1. Multiple neutral grip attachments can be used to train the same muscles, including a V-bar row attachment, which enables a close grip and is also known as a double D-handle attachment. Alternatively, you can use a “U-shaped” bar that has a curved body and is available in close grip and shoulder width grip models.
    2. Using a neutral grip attachment with handles outside shoulder width facilitates a different pulling technique that preferentially trains different back muscles, so the [seated neutral wide grip cable row](Neutral%20wide%20grip%20cable%20row%201d15c6f170d880809990ccd6b1a0cac0.md) is a distinct exercise in this database.
    3. You can perform this exercise with essentially the same technique whether you use a seated cable row machine or an adjustable cable station, but a seated cable row machine can be more stable and therefore is ideal.
    4. If you use a seated cable row machine, you naturally will sit down on its seat, but if you are using an adjustable cable station, you will sit down on the ground after adjusting the cable to a height that is approximately level with your shoulders when seated on the floor with an upright torso.
2. Position your feet in contact with the machine’s foot plates or the base of the adjustable cable station.
    1. Allow your knees to bend to an angle that allows you to feel stable and comfortable, which can be a mild to moderately mild knee bend for many people.
    2. With greater knee bend, you will be able to sit closer toward the cable, so you can bend your knees further if you initially cannot reach the bar when leaning forward by bending at your hip
3. Lean forward at your hips until you are able to grasp the handles firmly with straight elbows and your palms facing each other.
4. While holding the bar with straight elbows, lean your torso backward at your hips until you are sitting with an upright torso.
    1. When seated upright, you should feel tension from the cable, so if the cable is still slack, you can extend your knees to scoot yourself backward until the machine’s weight stack separates and you feel the resistance.
## Exercise technique
1. Pull the bar back toward your torso by driving your elbows backward while simultaneously bending them and pulling your shoulder blades together.
    1. Move your elbows through a path of motion that feels comfortable to you, typically keeping them tucked fairly close to your sides with this neutral grip, rather than flaring them away from your sides (which is more comfortable with a wider overhand grip).
    2. Movement should occur at your shoulders, shoulder blades, and elbows, but your knees, hips, and lower back should remain nearly stationary in a stable position throughout the set.
    3. Pull through your available range of motion or until the bar is directly in front of your torso, which will typically result in your elbows being level with your torso or slightly behind your torso at the end of the lifting phase.
    4. As a cue for training your upper back muscles, you can think about squeezing your shoulder blades together at the end of the pull as if you were trying to pinch a pencil with your shoulder blades.
2. Reverse the movement by allowing your elbows to move forward in a controlled manner as they progressively straighten to move the bar forward.
    1. Finish with your arms fully outstretched in front of you.
    2. Your shoulder blades will naturally move apart, but you can exaggerate this motion by intentionally allowing the weight to pull them further apart than your resting position at the end, without rounding your lower back. This will stretch your upper back muscles and may help you to train them more effectively.
    3. While you do not have to perform this step extremely slowly, you should avoid letting the weight abruptly yank your arms forward in an uncontrolled fashion.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
While also training your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md), this row can effectively develop your [lat](../Muscles/Latissimus%20Dorsi%201905c6f170d880109e73f99ab91d4d47.md), [teres major](../Muscles/Teres%20Major%201905c6f170d880dbba32f6bd22e3abe6.md), [rear delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Posterior%20Head%201905c6f170d880a29e5ec26f4d257c01.md), [traps](../Muscles/Trapezius%201b95c6f170d880bebf89c759b592e81f.md), and [rhomboids](../Muscles/Rhomboids%201b95c6f170d880c8a84de94f5232a509.md).

## Setting up
1. Connect a lat pulldown bar to the cable, select your weight with the loading pin, and adjust the thigh pad to a height that lets you position your thighs snugly against it while sitting with your feet flat on the floor.
    1. If you do not have a standard lat pulldown bar attachment, which has a straight body and mildly angled ends, you can use a different attachment that lets you comfortably grasp it with an underhand grip.
2. While facing the bar and standing above the seat, firmly grasp the bar with a closer than shoulder-width underhand grip, such that your palms face backward.
    1. Specifically how closely you position your hands is up to your preference, but they should be clearly closer than what you would use for a standard [underhand grip lat pulldown](Underhand%20grip%20cable%20lat%20pulldown%201a15c6f170d880b2a97ec3d948120f99.md) with a moderate grip width.
    2. For the most stable grip, wrap your fingers around the bar with the bar pressed into where the bases of your fingers meet the palm side of your knuckles.
3. While holding the bar, sit down on the machine’s seat with the lower portion of your thighs snugly pressed against the machine’s thigh pad.
    1. When sitting down, allow your elbows to straighten and your arms to raise overhead in line with the machine’s resistance.
4. In the seated position, slightly lean your torso backward at your hips.
    1. Maintain this slight backward lean throughout your set.
    2. From this position, your elbows should be straight, with your arms overhead and slightly forward (rather than completely vertical), and you should feel tension from the cable station holding your arms in this position.
    3. If you notice the cable remains slack in this position (which may occur for certain individuals who are quite tall and have long arms), widening out your grip may be needed to experience resistance throughout the full range of motion for this exercise.
## Exercise technique
1. Pull the bar down toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down toward your sides as you progressively bend them.
    1. Simultaneosuly pull your shoulder blades down away from your ears.
    2. After the initial half of the pull, when your upper arms are approximately parallel with the ground, the bony prominence on the back of each elbow should be pointing predominantly forward as your upper arms are situated in front of your body, rather than having your elbows and upper arms predominantly flared out to your sides.
    3. During the second half of this pull, drive your elbows simultaneously backward and downward until they are in line with your torso or slightly behind it.
2. Reverse the movement by allowing your elbows to lift upward and away from your torso as they progressively straighten to raise the bar in a controlled manner.
    1. Let your shoulder blades move naturally as they elevate with your arms.
    2. Finish with your arms overhead and your elbows fully straightened.
    3. There is no need to perform this step extremely slowly, but you should avoid letting the machine’s resistance yank your arms up in an uncontrolled fashion.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop your [lat](../Muscles/Latissimus%20Dorsi%201905c6f170d880109e73f99ab91d4d47.md), [teres major](../Muscles/Teres%20Major%201905c6f170d880dbba32f6bd22e3abe6.md), and [rear delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Posterior%20Head%201905c6f170d880a29e5ec26f4d257c01.md) while also meaningfully training your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md).

## Setting up
1. Pick up a pair of dumbbells, and sit down on a bench with your feet flat on the floor and your torso upright. Hold the dumbbells at your sides with slightly bent elbows as your palms are facing in toward your sides (i.e., in a neutral grip position).
    1. You can opt to sit down on a flat bench without any back support or sit down on a seated bench with back support.
## Exercise technique
1. Sweep the dumbbells out and away from your sides until your upper arms are close to parallel with the ground.
2. Reverse the motion by lowering the dumbbells in a controlled manner back to your sides.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop your [lateral delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Lateral%20Head%201905c6f170d8804b9b6ef12253eec774.md) and [supraspinatus](../Muscles/Supraspinatus%201905c6f170d880efb440c1614caf1c97.md) while also training your [front delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Anterior%20Head%201905c6f170d8805da59fc8f9dc0a59e4.md) and [upper trap](../Muscles/Upper%20Trapezius%201925c6f170d880009e2cf04b5b29b467.md).

## Setting up
1. At a cable station, adjust the cable to near the height of your elbows when standing with your arms at your sides, clip in a D-handle attachment, and select your desired weight with the loading pin.
2. While standing with your chest facing near a 135-degree angle away from the cable station, grasp the handle with your hand on the side closer to the cable.
3. On the side holding the handle, position your upper arm by your side and slightly forward while bending your elbow to approximately 90 degrees and keeping your wrist in a fairly straight position.
    1. Maintain this position throughout your set.
    2. Situating your upper arm slightly forward rather than having it be completely vertical at your side can limit your torso from restricting your range of motion during this exercise.
4. Have your forearm rotated outward toward the cable station.
    1. Your shoulder mobility will affect how far you can rotate, and you should use as much range as feels comfortable for your shoulder.
    2. In this position, you should feel tension from the cable, so if that is not the case, take a step to the side away from the cable stack.
## Exercise technique
1. Rotate your forearm inward by pulling the handle away from the cable station and across the front of your torso while moving through your shoulder’s available range of motion as you continue to keep your upper arm positioned slightly in front of your side.
    1. At the end of this motion, your forearm should be contacting or close to contacting your abdomen while your palm is facing backward.
    2. All of this movement should occur from shoulder rotation, and your upper arm should not raise away from your torso.
    3. When thinking about this technique, it can be helpful to view your forearm as a clock’s hand, while your elbow is the center about which rotation occurs without any side-to-side motion.
2. Reverse the motion by rotating your forearm outward as you bring the handle closer toward the cable station in a controlled manner until you have returned to the starting position.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set with one side and are ready to repeat the exercise with your other side.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop your rotator cuff’s [subscapularis](../Muscles/Subscapularis%201905c6f170d88064bf36d328969a3679.md), while also training your [pec major](../Muscles/Pectoralis%20Major%201b95c6f170d880539f8ee236e09d4728.md), [lat](../Muscles/Latissimus%20Dorsi%201905c6f170d880109e73f99ab91d4d47.md), [teres major](../Muscles/Teres%20Major%201905c6f170d880dbba32f6bd22e3abe6.md), and [front delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Anterior%20Head%201905c6f170d8805da59fc8f9dc0a59e4.md).

## Setting up
1. Lie down with your abdomen contacting the ground (i.e., in the prone position) and your head lifted slightly off the ground as you maintain a tucked chin position with your face directed toward the ground.
2. Position your arms straight out in front of you with extended elbows such that your hands are approximately shoulder-width apart while resting on the ground.
    1. Your body position should resemble how you would look if you were reaching up with your arms fully overhead while standing.
3. Rotate your arms so that your palms face in toward each other.
    1. If you make a thumbs-up gesture in this position, your thumb should be pointing up toward the ceiling.
## Exercise technique
1. Lift your arms straight up off the ground through your available shoulder range of motion while keeping your chest in contact with the ground.
    1. Your shoulder mobility will affect how high you can raise your arms.
    2. Most people will not be able to lift their arms particularly high before reaching the end of their available range of motion.
    3. If you notice your chest lifting up off the ground during this movement, that indicates that you most likely are dynamically extending your lumbar spine, which can occur as a compensation pattern instead of lifting your arm only with your shoulder girdle muscles.
2. Reverse the motion by lowering your arms in a controlled manner until your hands lightly contact the ground.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise trains your [traps](../Muscles/Trapezius%201b95c6f170d880bebf89c759b592e81f.md) along with your [serratus anterior](../Muscles/Serratus%20Anterior%201955c6f170d880a8b8b9e712f2ec58e0.md), [front delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Anterior%20Head%201905c6f170d8805da59fc8f9dc0a59e4.md), [side delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Lateral%20Head%201905c6f170d8804b9b6ef12253eec774.md), and [supraspinatus](../Muscles/Supraspinatus%201905c6f170d880efb440c1614caf1c97.md).

## Setting up
1. Add weight plates of your desired load to the machine, and sit down on the seat.
2. Adjust the height of the machine’s thigh pad to a level that allows you to fit the lowest portions of your thighs just underneath it, while the front halves of your feet are situated on the foot plate.
    1. To help find this point, you can initially place the front halves of your feet on the foot plate while your heels are lower than the balls of your feet.
    2. Avoid setting the pad to a height that requires you to lift your heels up higher than the balls of your feet in order for your thighs to press snugly into the pad. The weakest portion of a calf raise occurs when your heels are fully raised. Consequently, it can be difficult to re-rack the weight at the end of a set if your calves are fatigued, and you have to raise your heels meaningfully before adjusting the machine’s stopper to accept the weight.
3. With the front halves of your feet on the foot plate, scoot your knees under and in front of the thigh pad until your lower thighs are securely under the pad.
    1. You can optionally use your hands to help pull the thigh pad up as you scoot forward.
4. Raise your heels up just enough to disengage the machine’s stopper by operating its lever with one of your hands.
    1. You should be primarily bearing weight through the balls of your feet as the back half of your feet are hanging off the foot plate.
    2. For tracking purposes, you can consider your first full rep to start after you have completely lowered your heels when performing step 1 of the exercise technique for the first time in a set. The initial short range of motion heel raise you perform to disengage the stopper does not constitute a full rep.
## Exercise technique
1. In a controlled manner, allow your heels to descend toward the ground through the available range of motion of your ankles while continuing to keep the front halves of your feet on top of the foot plate.
    1. Strive to lower your heels as far as you can, and you will likely feel a stretching sensation in your calf/and or ankle at the bottom position.
    2. Specifically how far you are able to lower your heels will be dependent on your mobility, but individuals with normal ankle mobility can position their heels lower than the balls of their feet at the bottom.
2. Push through the balls of your feet to raise your heels into the air through the available range of motion of your ankles.
    1. At the top, your heels should be higher than the balls of your feet.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
    1. At times during a set, you may feel that your feet slide back somewhat on the foot plate. If that occurs, you can use your hands to pull up the bottom of the thigh pad to make it easier for you to re-position your feet forward on the foot plate.
4. After finishing the lowering phase of your rep, raise your heels high enough to engage the machine’s stopper with your hand.
    1. If you performed as many reps as you possibly could during your set, you may have to rest in the bottom position for several seconds until your calves are ready to lift your heels up high enough to engage the stopper.
5. With the stopper engaged, lower your heels to let the weight rest on the stopper.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop your [soleus](../Muscles/Soleus%201925c6f170d88052bbb6c59dc04f2e1a.md), but it will not train your [gastrocnemius](../Muscles/Gastrocnemius%201b95c6f170d880b59622dd4a8639aa2f.md) nearly as well as calf raise variations performed with straight knees.

## Setting up
1. With a cable station positioned to its lowest height, clip in a d-handle attachment and select your weight with the loading pin.
2. While facing the cable station, take a step to the side such that the handle is positioned directly in front of one hand (rather than having the midline of your body in front of the handle)
3. Squat down or hinge at your hips with an extended elbow before using your closer hand to grasp the handle with an underhand grip such that your palm is directed forward.
4. While keeping your elbow extended, stand upright while gripping the handle.
5. Make sure tension is present from the cable station while your elbow is fully extended, rather than slack being present in the cable.
    1. Depending on your arm length relative to your height and which specific cable station you are using, you likely will have to take a small step backward to take out the slack of the cable.
    2. When taking a small step backwards, the cable will now have a mildly diagonal line of pull rather than being vertical.
    3. To maintain a fully extended elbow position with a diagonal line of pull, you will position your upper arm slightly in front of your body by flexing at your shoulder instead of keeping your upper arm pinned to your sides (like you would with a curl that has a vertically directed resistance, such as free weights).
## Exercise technique
1. Curl the handle upward by bending at your elbow while keeping your upper arm fixed in the same position that allowed your elbow to be fully extended at the start of the rep (rather than allowing your upper arm to swing further forward).
2. After your elbow has fully flexed, reverse the motion by lowering the handle in a controlled manner until your elbow has returned to an extended position.
    1. During the lowering phase, continue to keep your upper arm in the same position used to start the rep.
3. Alternate between curling the handle upwards and lowering it down until you have completed your set and are ready to repeat the exercise with your other side.
## Description
Like other curl variations, this exercise can effectively train your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md).

## Setting up
1. Position the Smith machine’s bar slightly below the height of your hands when standing with your arms at your sides.
2. Add weight plates of your desired load to the bar, and stand upright in a near hip-width stance with the middle of the bar just in front of your legs.
    1. If your Smith machine has angled sliding rails, you can position yourself to face the side in which the bar will track slightly backward when lifting it up (which results in the bottom of the rails being farther in front of you than the top of the rails). Facing this way will help the shrug feel most natural.
    2. If your Smith machine has purely vertical sliding rails, you can perform the same movement regardless of which direction you face.
3. With your arms pointing straight down toward the bar, sit your hips mildly backward while slightly bending your knees until your hands are level with the bar. Keep your lower back flat and chest up rather than rounding your back.
4. With straight elbows, firmly grasp the bar with a slightly outside shoulder width overhand grip such that your palms are facing backward.
    1. For the most stable grip, wrap your fingers around the bar with the bar pressed into where the bases of your fingers meet the palm side of your knuckles.
    2. If you situate the bar closer toward the middle of your palms (rather than the bases of your fingers), the bar can slide down your hand while holding it, which pulls on your hand skin in an uncomfortable manner that increases the risk of tearing a callus.
## Exercise technique
1. Brace your core by tensing the front and sides of your abdominals outward, like you would if you were bracing for someone to strike your stomach with a punch or forcible slap.
    1. Continue bracing your core from this point onward.
2. By extending (straightening) your hips and knees, stand upright with the bar, and rotate the safety hooks out away from the safety bars through a slight wrist flick motion.
3. Shrug your shoulders upward through your available range of motion to lift the bar upward while keeping your elbows straight.
    1. Throughout the exercise, look straight ahead to keep your neck near a neutral position.
    2. As a cue, you can think about driving your shoulders up toward your earlobes.
    3. While you shrug your shoulders upward, the rest of your body should remain stationary as you continue standing upright with straight legs.
4. Reverse the motion by allowing your shoulders to descend fully in a controlled manner to lower the bar.
    1. At the bottom, your shoulders should ideally be positioned a little lower than where they are normally situated while standing at rest due to the downward stretch that the machine’s weight can provide.
    2. While you do not have to perform the lowering phase with an extremely slow tempo, you should avoid letting the weight abruptly yank you downward.
5. Alternate between steps 3 and 4 until you have completed your set and are ready to re-rack the bar.
    1. Following your last rep, rotate the safety hooks toward the safety bars, and mildly bend your hips and knees to rerack the bar onto the safety bars.
## Description
This exercise primarily trains your [upper traps](../Muscles/Upper%20Trapezius%201925c6f170d880009e2cf04b5b29b467.md) and [levator scapulae](../Muscles/Levator%20Scapulae%201955c6f170d880048119fd4b2c6c5737.md).
1a15c6f170d8804d834cef49a7b23f12:
## Setting up
1. Adjust the height of the seat so that your upper arms can be parallel with the floor or a little lower while grasping the handles.
    1. After initially adjusting the seat height, spread your arms outward so that your hands are level with the handles.
    2. You may have to re-adjust the seat if your upper arms are not parallel with the floor or a little lower.
    3. Some people will find their shoulders feel more comfortable when the seat is set to a height that allows their hands to be a bit lower than their shoulders, compared to when their hands are completely level with their shoulders.
2. While sitting with your back against the backrest, spread your arms backward into a “T-position” through your available range of motion.
3. Adjust the pins above the handles to a position that allows you to grasp the vertical handles with a neutral grip (i.e., palms facing forward) when your arms are in this “T-position.”
    1. You may have to readjust the handles and recheck to see that the handles are not positioned too far behind, such that you cannot grab the handles, or positioned too far in front, such that your arms are not as far back into the “T-position” as your mobility allows.
## Exercise technique
1. Pull your shoulder blades back together.
    1. Keep your shoulder blades in this tucked back position throughout the set.
2. Spread your arms apart into the “T-position” with a slight bend in your elbows before grasping the handles with a neutral grip (i.e., palms facing forward).
3. Pull your arms together as the handles move toward each other until they are just about to contact each other or until they lightly contact each other.
4. Reverse the motion by spreading your arms in a controlled manner until you have returned to your starting position (i.e., the “T-position”).
5. Alternate between pulling your arms together and spreading them apart until you have completed the set.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop all regions of your [pec major](../Muscles/Pectoralis%20Major%201b95c6f170d880539f8ee236e09d4728.md) while also training your [front delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Anterior%20Head%201905c6f170d8805da59fc8f9dc0a59e4.md) and [coracobrachialis](../Muscles/Coracobrachialis%201905c6f170d880f78a01c57799591868.md).

## Setting up
1. With a cable station positioned to its lowest height, clip in a rope attachment and select your weight with the loading pin.
2. While facing the middle of the bar, squat down or hinge at your hips with extended elbows.
3. Grasp the bar with a neutral grip (AKA hammer grip) such that your palms are directed in toward each other.
    1. For a particularly stable grip, you can place the outside of your index fingers in contact with the flat surface of the hard plastic end caps of the rope attachment.
    2. Whether you wrap your thumbs around your other fingers or place your thumbs on top of the rope’s end caps will be based on your personal preference.
4. While keeping your elbows extended, stand upright while gripping the rope.
5. Make sure tension is present from the cable station while your elbows are fully extended, rather than slack being present in the cable.
    1. Depending on your arm length relative to your height and which specific cable station you are using, you likely will have to take a small step backward to take out the slack of the cable.
    2. When taking a small step backwards, the cable will now have a mildly diagonal line of pull rather than being vertical.
    3. To maintain a fully extended elbow position with a diagonal line of pull, you will position your upper arms slightly in front of your body by flexing at your shoulders instead of keeping your upper arms pinned to your sides (like you would with a curl that has a vertically directed resistance, such as free weights).
## Exercise technique
1. Curl the rope upward by bending at your elbows while keeping your upper arms fixed in the same position that allowed your elbows to be fully extended at the start of the rep (rather than allowing your upper arms to swing further forward).
2. After your elbows have fully flexed, reverse the motion by lowering the rope in a controlled manner until your elbows have returned to an extended position.
    1. During the lowering phase, continue to keep your upper arms in the same position used to start the rep.
3. Alternate between curling the rope upwards and lowering it down until you have completed your set.
## Description
Like other curl variations, this exercise can effectively train your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md).

## Setting up
1. Adjust the J-hooks of a rack to near mid-chest height, place a barbell on the J-hooks, and add weight plates of your desired load.
    1. The appropriate J-hook height should allow you to walk out with the bar without having to rise up on the balls of your feet.
2. Position the safety pins just under the J-hooks.
3. Face the center of the bar with approximately a shoulder width stance and grasp each side of the bar with a somewhat wider than shoulder width grip that feels comfortable to you.
    1. The proper grip width will vary from person to person, and what feels best to you will be influenced by your shoulder mobility.
    2. If you are not accustomed to exercises that have a bar on your back, you may have to try out different hand placements to find one that personally suits you well.
4. While holding onto the bar, shallowly bend at your hips and knees in a quarter squat-like manner to then walk under the bar and situate the bar on your upper back in a position that feels comfortable and stable for you.
    1. Where precisely the bar feels most comfortable and stable will vary among different individuals, but the bar should feel like it is securely resting on the muscles of your upper back.
    2. If you feel like the bar is placing pressure on your neck, you most likely have the bar placed too high on your back. In particular, you should avoid placing the bar up excessively high to the extent that the weight is pressing on any of the bony prominences at the base of your neck.
    3. If you feel like the bar may slide down your back after standing upright with it, you most likely have the bar placed too low on your back.
    4. While positioning the bar on your upper back, you may have to readjust where you are grasping the bar if your shoulders, elbows, or wrists feel uncomfortable with your initial placement.
    5. If you are not accustomed to having a barbell on your back, you may not feel particularly comfortable doing so, especially when it is loaded with additional weight, but whichever position you use should not be painful.
    6. If you find that deeper than a mild bend at your hips and knees is (e.g., more like a half squat than a quarter squat) is required to position the bar on your back, you can lift the bar out of the J-hooks, set it down, raise the height of the J-hooks, and place the bar back onto the J-hooks.
5. Pull down on the bar to keep it positioned on your upper back and stand up in a quarter squat-like manner by extending your knees and hips.
## Exercise technique
1. Take a couple of steps backward and position your feet into a shoulder width stance.
2. Raise your heels into the air through the available range of motion of your ankles while keeping your knees straight and your trunk upright.
3. In a controlled manner, allow your heels to descend toward the ground while continuing to keep your knees straight.
4. After your heels touch the ground, alternate between steps 3 and 4 until you have completed your set.
5. Rerack the bar by walking forward until the barbell contacts the back of each J-cup and you are ready to rest the bar on the J-hooks by once again bending at your hips and knees in a quarter squat-like manner.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop your [gastrocnemius](../Muscles/Gastrocnemius%201b95c6f170d880b59622dd4a8639aa2f.md) and [soleus](../Muscles/Soleus%201925c6f170d88052bbb6c59dc04f2e1a.md).

## Setting up
1. Adjust the height of the machine’s shoulder pads to a level that initially allows you to stand under the pads with mildly bent knees, which will enable you to perform full range of motion calf raises.
    1. The appropriate shoulder pad height should make it easy for you to assume the starting position and also allow you to feel resistance from the machine both when your heels are fully lowered and fully raised.
    2. If the pads are too high, your knees may be straightened when initially standing under the pads, and you may lose tension from the machine when your heels are fully lowered.
    3. If the pads are too low, you may need to bend your knees excessively to stand under the pads, and you may be restricted from fully raising your heels.
2. Select your desired weight with the loading pin.
3. With your knees mildly bent, position the balls of your feet onto the foot plate with your heels hanging off the edge while your shoulders are snugly resting under the shoulder pads.
4. Straighten your knees to stand fully upright and receive the weight from the machine.
    1. Throughout the set, keep the balls of your feet firmly planted on the step.
    2. Depending on their mobility, some people may be able to adopt a position of knee hyperextension, which is when the knees bend backward beyond a straight position. Being able to reach a mildly hyperextended knee position is normal for many individuals and is not inherently problematic. However, certain individuals may experience knee discomfort if they allow their knees to bend backward into hyperextension during this exercise, so keeping a straight knee position instead of a hyperextended knee position may be preferable.
## Exercise technique
1. Push through the balls of your feet to raise your heels fully upward while keeping your knees straight and your trunk upright.
    1. Once you have lifted your heels as high upward as your ankle mobility permits, you have finished the lifting phase.
    2. While you lift your body upward through ankle motion, the rest of your body should remain stationary throughout the exercise.
2. Reverse the movement in a controlled manner by allowing your heels to descend toward the ground through the full range of motion your calf flexibility permits.
    1. Strive to lower your heels as far as you can below the balls of your feet to stretch your calves and train them most effectively.
    2. If you do not feel a stretching sensation in your calves (which you may feel on the backside of your knees or lower down your legs) at the bottom, you likely are not lowering through your full range of motion.
    3. While you do not have to perform an extremely slow lowering phase, avoid quickly dropping down and trying to bounce out of the bottom into the next rep.
    4. You can optionally briefly pause in the fully stretched bottom position,
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
    1. After finishing your last rep, mildly bend your knees to lower the weight to its resting position (where it no longer provides any resistance to you) before stepping off the foot plate.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop both your [gastrocnemius](../Muscles/Gastrocnemius%201b95c6f170d880b59622dd4a8639aa2f.md) and [soleus](../Muscles/Soleus%201925c6f170d88052bbb6c59dc04f2e1a.md) while simultaneously improving calf flexibility through loaded stretching.

## Setting up
1. Firmly grasp an asymmetrical weighted implement (or a viable alternative) by its lighter end at a position that can provide your desired level of resistance.
    1. Asymmetrical weighted implements include adjustable dumbbells with plates loaded only on one side, hammers, and end-loaded baseball bats.
    2. As an alternative to an asymmetrical weighted implement, you can grasp certain symmetrically weighted cylindrical implements closer toward one end, which can provide the same training effect. Examples include a fixed-weight straight bar, a fixed-weight EZ bar, an adjustable EZ bar, and a cable straight bar attachment (like a lat pulldown bar).
    3. The resistance your forearm pronator muscles experience during this exercise will be dictated by how closely to one end you grasp the implement.
    4. For greater resistance, you can grasp farther away from the weighted end with an asymmetrically loaded implement or closer to whichever end you are holding with a symmetrically loaded implement.
    5. When performing this exercise for the first time with a particular implement, you may have to try out different grip positions to determine specifically where you should grasp the implement to provide the magnitude of resistance you wish to have.
2. Sit down on a seat (e.g., chair, flat exercise bench, plyometric box), and position your forearm (on the side holding the weight) on top of your thigh with a bent elbow and your hand slightly in front of your knee.
    1. You can situate your wrist just above your kneecap, which should allow the weighted implement to rotate freely without contacting any part of your leg.
3. If not already in this position, direct your palm to face in toward your opposite side with a straight wrist position and the heavier end of your weighted implement directed straight up toward the ceiling.
    1. From here, your wrist and forearms are in a neutral position as they would normally be when standing upright with your palms facing in toward your sides.
## Exercise technique
1. While keeping your forearm resting on your thigh, progressively rotate your palm down toward the floor in a controlled manner through your available range of motion.
    1. Doing so will rotate the weighted end (if using an asymmetrically loaded object) or longer end (if using a symmetrically loaded object) in toward the midline of your body, such that this end moves in front of your torso rather than out to the side.
    2. Most people will have the forearm mobility to rotate until their palm is close to facing straight up, which will result in the weight’s handle being close to parallel to the floor, but some people may not be able to rotate quite as far, while others can rotate beyond that point.
    3. As you rotate your forearm, keep your wrist in a straight (neutral) position rather than letting the weight bend your wrist and pull your hand downward (which would bring the palm of your hand closer toward your knee if the wrist flexes).
2. After reaching your end range, reverse the movement until you have returned to the starting position by turning your palm to face in toward your opposite side.
    1. Doing so will lift the weighted end or longer end of the implement upward and outward in an arcing manner until the handle is vertically oriented.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set and are ready to repeat the exercise with your other side.
## Description
This exercise primarily trains your forearm’s [supinator](../Muscles/Supinator%201905c6f170d88034845dfa135173a9ef.md) and your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md).

## Setting up
1. Adjust the machine’s foot plate to a height that aligns the machine’s pivot points with the height of your shoulders once you are standing on the foot plate.
    1. On each side of the machine, the pivot point is the center about which the lever arm rotates, and it is denoted by a small dot or circle in some machines.
    2. Aligning the center of your shoulders with the pivot points can help this exercise feel more comfortable and natural compared to if the seat height resulted in your shoulders being above or below the pivot points.
    3. To confirm whether you selected an appropriate foot plate height, you will have to stand on it and visually check where your shoulders are positioned relative to the pivot points, so you may have to try out different settings before finding one that best suits your body.
    4. A foot plate height that aligns your shoulders with the pivot points will commonly allow you to hold the handles with slightly bent elbows.
2. Select your desired weight with the loading pin, and stand on the foot plate with the handles situated just in front of your thighs.
3. Firmly grasp the handles with slightly bent elbows as your palms are facing in toward each other.
4. Optionally lean your torso slightly forward at your hips by sitting your buttocks slightly backward with a slight knee bend.
    1. People commonly find lateral raises to feel more comfortable with a slight forward torso lean, but you can alternatively stand fully upright if you prefer to do so.
    2. Maintain your preferred torso position throughout your set, as you subsequently move your shoulders without moving your lower body or torso.
## Exercise technique
1. Lift the handles by driving your elbows out and away from your sides until your upper arms are close to parallel with the ground.
    1. Allow your shoulder blades to move naturally rather than trying to keep them in any particular position.
    2. Focusing on moving your elbows in an arcing manner throughout this exercise can help you target the appropriate shoulder muscles.
2. Reverse the motion in a controlled manner by lowering your elbows in toward your sides to return the handles to the starting position.
    1. To confirm you have moved through your full range of motion, you can lightly tap the weights you selected against the rest of the weight stack.
    2. While there is no need to use an extremely slow tempo, you should be actively controlling the weight the entire time. Do not let the weight abruptly swing your arms downward.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop your [lateral delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Lateral%20Head%201905c6f170d8804b9b6ef12253eec774.md) and [supraspinatus](../Muscles/Supraspinatus%201905c6f170d880efb440c1614caf1c97.md), which are assisted by your [front delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Anterior%20Head%201905c6f170d8805da59fc8f9dc0a59e4.md) and [upper trap](../Muscles/Upper%20Trapezius%201925c6f170d880009e2cf04b5b29b467.md).

## Setting up
1. Add weight plates to a barbell situated in a landmine attachment (or a viable substitute).
    1. As an alternative to using a landmine attachment, landmine exercises can be performed with one end of the barbell situated in a wall corner.
    2. While the scraping can be lessened by placing a towel between the wall corner and the barbell, be aware that performing landmine exercises in a wall corner can easily damage the wall corner, so this approach is not appropriate in every environment.
    3. The diameter of the plates you select can influence the range of motion of this exercise, so you can use smaller diameter plates if you wish to row through a longer range of motion.
    4. Plates weighing 45lb or 20kg (which differ slightly), along with bumper plates of various weights, have a diameter near 18in (45cm) that can physically constrain the range of motion for your row by contacting your torso at the end of the lifting phase or by contacting the ground at the end of the lowering phase.
2. Stand directly to one side of the barbell and slightly behind the plates with the landmine’s pivot point behind you.
    1. Position the side you wish to train during this set closer to the bar.
    2. While you keep your opposite arm wherever you prefer throughout the exercise, the subsequent directions specifically refer to the arm closer to the barbell.
3. Sit your hips backward while bending your knees until your hand is level with the bar. Keep your lower back flat and chest up rather than rounding your back.
    1. More motion should come from your hips than your knees as you descend, and your knees should not track far forward. However, you can let your knees shift mildly forward rather than maintaining completely vertical shins.
4. Firmly grasp the end of the barbell’s shaft just behind the bearing (the cylinder separating the shaft from the sleeve where you add plates) with a straight elbow and a neutral grip, resulting in your palm facing in toward your side.
5. Brace your core by tensing the front and sides of your abdominals outward, like you would if you were bracing for someone to strike your stomach with a punch or forcible slap.
    1. Continue bracing your core from now on.
6. While keeping your lower back flat, chest up, and elbow straight, drive through your legs to lift the bar slightly up and assume a slightly more upright torso position.
    1. The objective is to use your hip and thigh muscles to lift the bar just high enough that you can experience resistance from the weight when your elbows are fully straight in the bottom position of each rep, rather than having the plates touch the ground.
    2. In this position, your torso should ideally remain inclined closer to horizontal than to vertical, with your hips mostly bent. However, large-diameter plates may require a more upright torso to keep them off the ground.
## Exercise technique
1. Pull the bar upward and back toward your torso by driving your elbow simultaneously upward and backward while progressively bending your elbow and pulling your shoulder blade backward .
    1. Move your elbow through a path of motion that feels comfortable to you, which will typically involve keeping it tucked fairly close to your side with this neutral grip rather than notably flaring your elbow away from your side.
    2. Keep your torso in a fixed hinged position as you maintain the same angle of bend in your hips and knees throughout your set while keeping your core braced and your lower back near a neutral position.
    3. Pull through your available range of motion, which will typically result in your elbow being level with your torso or slightly behind your torso at the end of the lifting phase.
    4. If using large diameter plates, you may not be able to row as far backward compared to if you use smaller diameter plates.
2. Reverse the movement by lowering the bar in a controlled manner by allowing your elbow to move downward and forward until your elbow has finished extending and the bar has returned to the starting position.
    1. During the lowering phase, your shoulder blade will naturally move forward.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set and are ready to return the bar to its initial position by bending your knees and hips to lower the bar before repeating the exercise with your other side.
