## Setting up
1. After adding weight plates to a trap bar situated on the ground and positioning the high handles up (if your trap bar has high handles), stand within the middle of the trap bar with a hip-width to shoulder-width stance and your arms at your sides.
    1. You can certainly use a trap bar that does not have elevated handles, but the bar is easier to lift into the starting position when using high handles.
    2. Specifically how wide you situate your feet apart can be based on what feels most comfortable to you when picking up a weight off the floor with a deadlifting motion.
2. Hinge at your hips while bending your knees until your hands are level with the handles when your elbows are straight, and your arms are lifted slightly out to your sides (to position your hands directly over the handles).
    1. Throughout this movement, keep your lower back near a neutral position, like you have when you are normally standing upright, rather than meaningfully rounding your lower back while doing so.
3. Firmly grasp the center of the handles with your palms facing in toward each other.
4. While keeping your elbows straight, press your legs into the ground with enough force to feel the trap bar’s sleeves push up into the weight plates, but not enough force to lift the bar off the ground.
    1. Applying this pre-tension to the bar will likely produce an audible “clinking” sound.
    2. The initial submaximal pull allows you to check if you have grasped the handles correctly, which will be indicated by the handles not rotating forward or backward when applying the pre-tension.
    3. If you pick up a trap bar with your hands positioned slightly away from the middle of the handles, the trap bar can start rotating in a manner that makes it very difficult to hold and lift appropriately.
    4. Even for experienced lifters, it can be easy to grasp a trap bar’s handles without having their hands truly centered initially, so applying the pre-tension can make sure you are in your ideal starting position.
    5. If the bar starts rotating when you apply the pre-tension, re-center your grip, and apply the pre-tension again until the bar no longer rotates.
5. Brace your core and stand upright with the bar by extending your hips and knees while continuing to keep your elbows extended and your lower back near a neutral position.
    1. To brace effectively, you can initially take a deep “belly breath” (AKA diaphragmatic breath) that expands the front and sides of your abdominals outward.
    2. Avoid taking a “chest breath” that predominantly lifts your chest upward and leaves your abdominals relaxed or simply sucking your belly button inward.
    3. After the deep “belly breath,” you can continue thinking about tensing the front of your abdominals, sides of your abdominals, and lower back muscles simultaneously in a manner that allows you to form a “360 degree brace” instead of only tensing the front of your core.
    4. As a helpful cue for your “360 degree brace,” you can tense the front and sides of your abdominals outward like you would if you are bracing for someone to strike your stomach with a punch or forcible slap.
    5. While your lower back muscles will work to maintain a rigid trunk position, you should primarily lift the bar with your hip and thigh muscles.
## Exercise technique
1. Shrug your shoulders upward through your available range of motion while keeping your elbows extended, which will lift the bar upward.
    1. While doing so, keep your neck in a neutral position, like you have when you are normally standing upright and looking straight ahead.
2. Reverse the motion by allowing your shoulders to descend in a controlled manner through your available range of motion, which will lower the bar.
    1. At the end of this motion, your shoulders should ideally be positioned a little lower than where they are normally situated while standing at rest due to the downward stretch that the weight can provide.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.

This exercise primarily trains your [upper traps](../Muscles/Upper%20Trapezius%201925c6f170d880009e2cf04b5b29b467.md) and [levator scapulae](../Muscles/Levator%20Scapulae%201955c6f170d880048119fd4b2c6c5737.md).

## Setting up
1. Prepare the barbell with your desired load by adding weight plates to it or leaving the barbell unloaded, which is recommended if performing this exercise for the first time.
    1. If you have access to one, you can also use a fixed-weight straight barbell, which may be lighter than a typical 20kg (44lb) barbell that has sleeves on which to add weight plates.
2. Pick up the barbell with an underhand grip where your palms are facing forward away from you.
3. While holding the barbell, sit down on a flat exercise bench or chair and position your forearms on top of your thighs with your palms facing up and your wrists situated slightly in front of your knees.
    1. To achieve this position, you will be leaning forward at your hips when seated with your elbows bent.
4. Allow the force from the bar to bend your wrists and bring your hands downward such that your palms are facing forward.
    1. In this position, the bar should not be contacting your legs, so scoot your forearms forward if it is initially contacting your legs.
5. While maintaining your grip on the bar, let the bar roll down your fingers.
    1. This downward motion will occur from movement at the joints formed by your knuckles and the finger bones closest to your knuckles.
    2. After it rolls down your fingers, the bar should no longer be fully contacting the palm side of your knuckles, in contrast to when you typically maintain a firm grip on a bar with a fist-like hand position.
## Exercise technique
1. Lift the bar upward by curling your wrists and fingers simultaneously through their available range of motion while keeping your forearms resting on your thighs.
    1. All of the motion should be coming from your wrists and the joints your fingers form with your knuckles.
    2. About halfway through the lifting phase, your palms should be facing straight up when your hands are aligned with your forearms.
    3. At the end of the lifting phase, when the bar is fully raised, your palms should be angled back toward you, and your fingers should be fully wrapped around the bar in a fist-like hand position.
    4. When performing this exercise appropriately, you should feel tension in the muscles on the palm side of your forearms.
2. Reverse the motion by lowering the bar in a controlled manner as it rolls down your fingers until you have returned to the starting position with your palms directed forward away from you.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can effectively train the six [wrist flexor muscles](../Muscles/Wrist%20flexor%20muscles%202c85c6f170d880a49749f7d7a9f307c8.md) on the palm side of your forearm in addition to the [hand muscles](../Muscles/Intrinsic%20Finger%20Flexors%201bb5c6f170d880648d61d9b5db235bf6.md) involved in gripping.

## Setting up
1. Approach a step or a sturdy object that can function as a step. You should be by a surface (e.g., handrail, wall, power rack) where you can place one hand to assist with maintaining your balance while performing this exercise.
    1. Based on the equipment at your disposal, a variety of objects can serve as your step. Make sure the object can support your weight, will not move once you are on it, and allows you to lower your heels through your full range of motion during the exercise.
    2. As an alternative to a staircase’s bottom step, you may select a power rack’s bottom beam if the beam is sufficiently tall.
    3. Additionally, a calf raise block, aerobic step, deadlift block, or thick bumper plate can each be positioned near a wall or power rack for stability. Depending on your bodyweight, anchoring an aerobic step with weight on top of it may be required to prevent the step from tipping.
2. After placing your hand onto the nearby surface for balance assistance, step onto the step with the front halves of your feet on the step while the back halves of your feet are hanging off the step.
## Exercise technique
1. Raise your heels into the air through the available range of motion of your ankles while keeping your knees straight and your trunk upright.
2. In a controlled manner, allow your heels to descend toward the ground through the available range of motion of your ankles while continuing to keep your knees straight.
    1. How far you are able to lower your heel will be dependent on your mobility.
    2. Strive to lower your heel as far as you can, and you will likely feel a stretching sensation in your calf at the bottom position.
3. After your heels have fully descended, alternate between raising and lowering your heels until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop your [gastrocnemius](../Muscles/Gastrocnemius%201b95c6f170d880b59622dd4a8639aa2f.md) and [soleus](../Muscles/Soleus%201925c6f170d88052bbb6c59dc04f2e1a.md) while simultaneously improving calf flexibility through loaded stretching.

## Setting up
1. Adjust a cable station’s pulley to its highest level, select your desired weight with the loading pin, and attach a bar with a straight (or mostly straight) body to the cable.
    1. Any bar that enables you to perform this exercise with an overhand grip can be similarly used, including a standard straight bar, a lat pulldown bar (with a long straight body and angled ends), and a multi-grip EZ bar.
2. While standing directly in front of the cable station and facing away from it, reach up overhead with bent elbows and fairly straight wrists to grasp the bar with an overhand grip such that your palms are facing forward.
    1. Maintain fairly straight wrists throughout your set.
3. While keeping your hands overhead and elbows bent, step forward and adopt a staggered stance with one foot forward in front of the other before moderately leaning forward by hinging at your hips.
    1. Maintain this forward torso lean throughout your set.
    2. In this position, your hands should be behind your head, and you should feel tension from the cable. If that is not the case, walk forward until you feel tension from the cable.
4. Tuck your chin toward your chest and make sure your upper arms are situated parallel to the ground or raised up a little higher.
    1. Doing so will reduce the likelihood that the back of your head obstructs the path of the cable during the exercise.
## Exercise technique
1. Press the bar forward and somewhat downward by extending your elbows until they are straightened, while not moving your upper arms.
    1. At the end of this motion, the bar should be situated in front of you.
    2. If the cable contacts the back of your head during this motion, you can lean forward a little more for additional clearance.
2. Reverse the motion by bending your elbows through your available range of motion to move the bar backward and somewhat upward in a controlled manner until you have returned to the starting position.
    1. Strive to continue keeping your upper arms stationary while all of the movement occurs from elbow motion rather than also involving shoulder motion.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop all three heads of your [triceps](../Muscles/Triceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88032be38d4f3e73c9e4c.md), including its large [long head](../Muscles/Triceps%20Brachii%20Long%20Head%201905c6f170d880b1a0a7eda6c9b74382.md), which may not be trained as well by compound pressing exercises.

## Setting up
1. Adjust the height of the seat so that your upper arms can be parallel with the floor or a little lower while grasping the handles.
    1. After initially adjusting the seat height, spread your arms outward so that your hands are level with the handles.
    2. You may have to re-adjust the seat if your upper arms are not parallel with the floor or a little lower.
    3. Some people will find their shoulders feel more comfortable when the seat is set to a height that allows their hands to be a bit lower than their shoulders, compared to when their hands are completely level with their shoulders.
2. Adjust the pins above the handles to a position that allows you to grasp the handles with your hands as close as they can be to each other while your chest is facing the machine’s pad.
3. After sitting down with your chest against the pad, grasp the horizontal handles with an overhand grip such that your palms are facing down and slightly bend your elbows.
    1. Maintain the slight bend in your elbows throughout the set.
## Exercise technique
1. Spread the handles apart and backward until your arms and torso form a “T-shape.”
2. Reverse the motion by bringing the handles forward and toward each other until they have returned to their starting position.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop your [rear delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Posterior%20Head%201905c6f170d880a29e5ec26f4d257c01.md), which is assisted by your [traps](../Muscles/Trapezius%201b95c6f170d880bebf89c759b592e81f.md) and [rhomboids](../Muscles/Rhomboids%201b95c6f170d880c8a84de94f5232a509.md), along with your rotator cuff’s [infraspinatus](../Muscles/Infraspinatus%201905c6f170d88026aebcf3953e2e440f.md), [teres minor](../Muscles/Teres%20Minor%201905c6f170d88098824dc8136557c410.md), and [supraspinatus](../Muscles/Supraspinatus%201905c6f170d880efb440c1614caf1c97.md).

## Setting up
1. Prepare the barbell with your desired load by adding weight plates while the barbell is on the ground or in an elevated position, such as a power rack.
    1. Setting up will be easier when using an elevated position, especially if you are using relatively heavy loads for this exercise.
    2. The bar will be easiest to pick up if positioned at a height slightly lower than the level of your hands when standing upright with your arms relaxed at your sides.
2. Stand close in front of the middle of the bar with a hip-width stance and extended elbows before hinging at your hips while bending your knees until your hands are level with the bar.
    1. Keep your lower back near a neutral position, like you have when you are normally standing upright, rather than meaningfully rounding your lower back while doing so.
3. Firmly grasp the bar with a shoulder-width overhand grip such that your palms are facing backward.
4. By extending your hips and knees, stand upright with the bar while continuing to keep your elbows extended and your lower back near a neutral position.
## Exercise technique
1. Shrug your shoulders upward through your available range of motion while keeping your elbows extended, which will lift the bar upward.
    1. While doing so, keep your neck in a neutral position, like you have when you are normally standing upright and looking straight ahead.
2. Reverse the motion by allowing your shoulders to descend in a controlled manner through your available range of motion, which will lower the bar.
    1. At the end of this motion, your shoulders should ideally be positioned a little lower than where they are normally situated while standing at rest due to the downward stretch that the weight can provide.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise primarily trains your [upper traps](../Muscles/Upper%20Trapezius%201925c6f170d880009e2cf04b5b29b467.md) and [levator scapulae](../Muscles/Levator%20Scapulae%201955c6f170d880048119fd4b2c6c5737.md).

## Setting up
1. Pick up a pair of dumbbells and sit down on a flat exercise bench or chair.
2. While holding the dumbbells, lean forward at your hips and position your forearms on top of your thighs with your palms facing upward and your wrists situated slightly in front of your knees.
3. Allow the force from the dumbbells to bend your wrists and bring your hands downward such that your palms are facing forward.
    1. In this position, the dumbbells should not be contacting your legs, so scoot your forearms forward if they are initially contacting your legs.
4. While maintaining your grip on them, let the dumbbells roll down your fingers.
    1. This downward motion will occur from movement at the joints formed by your knuckles and the finger bones closest to your knuckles.
    2. After they roll down your fingers, the dumbbells should no longer be fully contacting the palm side of your knuckles, in contrast to when you typically maintain a firm grip on dumbbells with a fist-like hand position.
## Exercise technique
1. Lift the dumbbells upward by curling your wrists and fingers simultaneously through their available range of motion while keeping your forearms resting on your thighs.
    1. All of the motion should be coming from your wrists and the joints your fingers form with your knuckles.
    2. About halfway through the lifting phase, your palms should be facing straight up when your hands are aligned with your forearms.
    3. At the end of the lifting phase, when the dumbbells are fully raised, your palms should be angled back toward you, and your fingers should be fully wrapped around the handles in a fist-like hand position.
    4. When performing this exercise appropriately, you should feel tension in the muscles on the palm side of your forearms.
2. Reverse the motion by lowering the dumbbells in a controlled manner as they roll down your fingers until you have returned to the starting position with your palms directed forward away from you.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can effectively train the six [wrist flexor muscles](../Muscles/Wrist%20flexor%20muscles%202c85c6f170d880a49749f7d7a9f307c8.md) on the palm side of your forearm in addition to the [hand muscles](../Muscles/Intrinsic%20Finger%20Flexors%201bb5c6f170d880648d61d9b5db235bf6.md) involved in gripping.
1a15c6f170d8806390e7e1743452b88c:
## Setting up
1. Prepare the barbell with your desired load by adding weight plates to it or leaving the barbell unloaded, which is recommended if performing this exercise for the first time.
    1. You can initially set the bar up on the floor or from an elevated position, such as from a power rack.
2. While facing the middle of the bar, squat down or hinge at your hips with extended elbows.
3. Grasp the bar with approximately a shoulder width grip and an overhand grip such that your palms are directed toward you.
4. While keeping your elbows extended, stand upright while gripping the bar.
## Exercise technique
1. Curl the bar upward by bending at your elbows while keeping your upper arms fixed at your sides (rather than allowing your upper arms to swing forward).
2. After your elbows have fully flexed, reverse the motion by lowering the bar in a controlled manner until your elbows have returned to an extended position.
    1. During the lowering phase, continue to keep your upper arms positioned by your sides.
3. Alternate between curling the bar up and lowering it down until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can develop your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md), but it may train your biceps somewhat less effectively than a curl with an underhand or neutral grip.

## Setting up
1. Stand upright with your back up against a flat wall, so that the back of your heels, your buttocks, your upper back, and the back of your head are all in contact with the wall.
    1. Keep all of these body regions in contact with the wall throughout the exercise.
2. With your elbows bent to approximately 90-degree angles, raise your upper arms straight out to your sides until they are parallel to the floor.
    1. In this position, the backs of your elbows should be in contact with the wall or very close to the wall if the size of your upper arms limits contact.
3. Rotate your forearms upward and back toward the wall as you strive to position the backs of your forearms and wrists as close to contacting the wall as you can.
    1. How close you will be to contacting the wall fully with your forearms and wrists will be meaningfully affected by your shoulder mobility, so positioning will vary among different individuals, with some being able to reach full contact and others reaching their end range well before contacting the wall with their forearms.
    2. While it is natural to feel a stretch when you have reached your shoulder’s end range, you should not force yourself into any position that is aggravating if you happen to experience pain from a pre-existing issue.
## Exercise technique
1. Slide your arms up the wall through your available shoulder range of motion in a controlled fashion while you continue applying effort to rotate the backs of your forearms toward the wall.
    1. While you may not be able to rotate your forearms any closer to the wall, continuously having the intent to do so may help amplify the training effect of this exercise.
    2. Continue keeping your elbows, head, upper back, buttocks, and heels in full contact with the wall.
    3. This sliding motion should resemble the upper arm movement used while performing a jumping jack or making a snow angel.
    4. How far you are able to slide up the wall will be determined by your shoulder mobility, and you most likely will not be able to raise your arms as high as you would when lifting your arms out to the side in other body positions.
    5. Rather than focusing on keeping a 90-degree bend in your elbows, allow your elbows to extend if that feels natural to you while sliding your arms upward.
2. Reverse the motion by sliding your arms down the wall in a controlled fashion until your elbows are positioned fairly close to your sides.
    1. Continue keeping your elbows, head, upper back, buttocks, and heels in full contact with the wall.
    2. You can allow your elbows to bend if that feels natural to you while sliding your arms downward.
3. Alternate between sliding your arms up and down the wall until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can improve shoulder external rotation range of motion while engaging a variety of muscles situated on the back of your shoulder and in your upper back.

## Setting up
1. Pick up a short looped elastic band and sit down on an object you can use as a seat such as a chair, exercise bench, or plyometric box.
    1. You will remain seated throughout this exercise.
2. Position the band around both of your feet with the band under and on top of the balls of your feet.
    1. The appropriate positioning will keep the band in place during the exercise.
3. Straighten your knees to move your feet out in front of you until only your heels remain on the ground, while the rest of your soles are off the ground.
4. If the band is slack, spread your thighs apart from each other until you feel meaningful tension from the band while allowing the band to rotate your feet inward (through ankle inversion).
    1. In this starting position for the exercise, the soles of your feet should be angled in toward the middle point between your feet (i.e., the midline of your body) and down toward the ground.
## Exercise technique
1. While keeping your legs stationary, rotate your feet outward (via ankle eversion) against the band’s resistance through your available ankle motion.
    1. When imagining a laser pointer shooting out from the middle of your soles, the outward rotation of your feet should prompt the laser pointer to point out away from the middle point between your feet.
    2. When performing this exercise correctly, you should feel tension in the muscles on the outer aspects of your lower legs, a little in front of the outer aspect of your calf muscles.
    3. Particularly avoid letting your thighs rotate via hip motion, which would result in your knee caps moving.
    4. If you have difficulty keeping your legs stationary, you can hold onto your thighs to stabilize them while the motion exclusively comes from your ankles.
2. Reverse the movement by allowing the band to rotate your feet inward (via ankle inversion) in a controlled manner through your available ankle range of motion as you continue keeping your thighs stationary.
    1. When imagining a laser pointer shooting out from the middle of your soles, the inward rotation of your feet should prompt the laser pointer to point in toward the middle point between your feet.
    2. If the band becomes slack toward the end of this movement, you can spread your thighs somewhat further apart in order to experience resistance from the band throughout your full range of motion.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can effectively train the [fibularis muscles](../Muscles/Fibularis%20muscles%201b95c6f170d8801da142f6e7458238a0.md) on the outer aspect of your lower leg that assist in actively stabilizing the ankle.

## Setting up
1. At a dual cable station, adjust each pulley to its lowest height, connect a D-handle attachment, and select your desired weight with the loading pin.
2. After standing centered between the cables with your sides facing the cable stacks, side step to grasp the handle on one side with your opposite hand, grasp the other handle with your free hand, and return to being centered between the cables.
    1. Your palms should be approximately facing each other as your hands are situated just in front of your thighs.
3. Slightly lean forward by hinging at your hips and slightly bend your elbows.
    1. Maintain this position throughout your set.
## Exercise technique
1. Raise the handles out and away from your sides until your upper arms are slightly below parallel with the ground.
2. Reverse the motion by lowering the handles back to your sides in a controlled manner.
3. Alternate between rsteps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop your [lateral delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Lateral%20Head%201905c6f170d8804b9b6ef12253eec774.md) and [supraspinatus](../Muscles/Supraspinatus%201905c6f170d880efb440c1614caf1c97.md), which are assisted by your [front delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Anterior%20Head%201905c6f170d8805da59fc8f9dc0a59e4.md) and [upper trap](../Muscles/Upper%20Trapezius%201925c6f170d880009e2cf04b5b29b467.md).
1a15c6f170d880689ebcce6974abf61c:
## Setting up
1. Position an adjustable bench at a low incline angle (e.g., near 30 degrees) and set a pair of dumbbells under the head of the bench.
    1. As a different variation, which you can use if your bench does not have a low incline setting, you can alternatively select a moderate incline angle (e.g., near 45 degrees) and otherwise use the same technique for this exercise.
2. Lie down with your chest contacting the head of the bench and your legs spread out as you position the balls of your feet on the ground.
3. Grasp the dumbbells, position your arms so that they are perpendicular to the ground with extended elbows, and rotate your arms so that your palms are facing in toward each other.
    1. Keep your elbows extended and your palms facing each other throughout your set.
## Exercise technique
1. Raise your arms straight up out in front of you through your available shoulder range of motion as you continue to keep your chest in contact with the bench.
    1. You can strive to raise your arms until they are close to parallel with the incline bench, but your shoulder mobility will affect how high you can raise your arms.
    2. If you notice your chest lifting up off the bench during this movement, that indicates that you most likely are dynamically extending your lumbar spine, which can occur as a compensation pattern instead of lifting your arm only with your shoulder girdle muscles.
2. Reverse the motion by lowering your arms in a controlled manner until your arms have returned to being perpendicular to the ground.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise trains your [traps](../Muscles/Trapezius%201b95c6f170d880bebf89c759b592e81f.md) along with your [serratus anterior](../Muscles/Serratus%20Anterior%201955c6f170d880a8b8b9e712f2ec58e0.md), [front delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Anterior%20Head%201905c6f170d8805da59fc8f9dc0a59e4.md), [side delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Lateral%20Head%201905c6f170d8804b9b6ef12253eec774.md), and [supraspinatus](../Muscles/Supraspinatus%201905c6f170d880efb440c1614caf1c97.md).

## Setting up
1. Prepare the barbell with your desired load by adding weight plates.
    1. You can initially set the bar up on the floor or from an elevated position, such as from a power rack.
    2. As an alternative to a standard barbell, you can also use a fixed-weight straight bar.
2. While facing the middle of the bar in an approximately hip-width stance with your toes pointing forward, squat down or hinge at your hips in a deadlift-like motion with straight elbows until your hands are level with the bar.
3. Firmly grasp the bar with approximately a shoulder width underhand grip, resulting in your palms facing forward.
4. While keeping your elbows straightened, stand upright with the bar by extending (straightening) your hips and knees while keeping your back flat (instead of meaningfully rounding your lower back).
    1. Once upright, the bar should be directly in front of your thighs.
## Exercise technique
1. Brace your core by tensing the front and sides of your abdominals outward, like you would if you were bracing for someone to strike your stomach with a punch or forcible slap.
    1. You will continue bracing your core throughout your set, which will help you maintain a rigid trunk position while you use hip motion instead of lower back motion to help drive the bar up.
2. While keeping your elbows straight, sit your buttocks back while allowing your knees to bend mildly and your torso to incline slightly forward.
    1. Keep your lower back near a neutral position, like you have when you are normally standing upright, rather than meaningfully rounding your lower back while doing so.
3. As you simultaneously drive your hips forcefully forward to generate momentum from your lower body, curl the bar upward in an arcing manner by bending at your elbows while allowing your elbows to swing a bit forward.
    1. The hip drive motion, which is similar to the lockout of a deadlift, will bring your torso into a vertical position with your knees straightened.
    2. Continue keeping your lower back near a neutral position instead of arching back excessively.
    3. While you are intentionally using momentum to help your biceps and other arm muscles lift the weight, you should not be “cheating” to the extent that you feel out of control.
4. After your elbows have fully bent, lower the bar in a controlled manner, allowing your elbows to straighten and return to your sides until you return to the starting position with straight elbows and the bar just in front of your thighs.
    1. Keep your torso upright and hips stationary as your biceps and other arm muscles control the descent without assistance from the rest of your body.
    2. Your muscles are noticeably stronger during the lowering phase of an exercise compared to the lifting phase, so “cheating” during the lifting phase allows your biceps to experience greater loading during the more controlled lowering phase.
    3. If you are unable to control the lowering phase to any reasonable degree, you are likely using a weight that is excessively heavy relative to your current ability.
5. Alternate between steps 2-4 until you have completed your set.
## Description
Like other curl variations, this exercise can effectively train your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md).
1a15c6f170d88068bf2dc2d1866e0767:
## Setting up
1. Pick a pair of dumbbells and sit down on a seated bench or a flat exercise bench with your feet flat on the ground. As you are sitting down, place the dumbbells onto your thighs.
    1. If you use a seated bench, the back rest should be low enough that it will not be within the path of the dumbbell and restrict your range of motion for this exercise.
    2. The tall backrest of an adjustable bench, positioned fully upright, may be more likely to limit your range than a fixed seated bench with a backrest that does not reach your head.
2. Lift the dumbbells up to shoulder level with your elbows bent by curling the weight and marching your thighs up one at a time for assistance if needed.
    1. Your elbows should now be underneath and slightly in front of the dumbbells.
    2. You should be holding the dumbbells on top of the bases of your palms (AKA heels of your hands) with mostly straight wrists that allow for a comfortable and stable grip that you will maintain throughout your set.
3. Press the dumbbells up overhead in a shoulder press motion until you have fully straightened your elbows.
    1. Point the back of your elbows forward with your palms facing in toward each other.
    2. The dumbbells should be vertically stacked over your shoulder.
    3. Rather than being excessively arched, your lower back and neck should be near a neutral position, like when you are normally standing upright and looking straight ahead.
## Exercise technique
1. Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells behind your head in a controlled manner while keeping your elbows up.
    1. Predominantly keep your elbows tucked in as they are chiefly pointing forward rather than out to your side. However, you can allow your elbows to flare slightly out away from your sides if that feels natural and comfortable to you. If the dumbbells bump into each other, you are flaring your elbows excessively.
    2. Essentially all the motion should occur from your forearms hinging at your elbows without any shoulder motion. You can think of your elbows as the center of an analog clock, while your forearms are the hands that rotate about these center elbows during this exercise.
    3. As you keep your elbows up, your upper arms should remain in a vertical position by the sides of your head.
2. Continue lowering the dumbbells until you have fully bent your elbows or can lightly tap the back of your shoulders with the dumbbells.
    1. It is normal to be able to bend the elbows beyond 90 degrees, but specifically how far you can bend your elbows may be limited by the flexibility of your long head of the triceps.
    2. While some lifters have the flexibility to reach their shoulders with the dumbbells, wherever you feel a notable stretching sensation in your triceps can be an appropriate end range.
    3. While you do not have to perform the lowering phase with an extremely slow tempo, you should be actively controlling the weights the entire way.
3. Reverse the movement by straightening your elbows to lift the dumbbell into the starting position overhead.
    1. You should finish with your elbows fully straightened as the dumbbells are vertically above your shoulders.
    2. Continue keeping your elbow up as all the motion occurs from your elbows without moving your shoulders.
4. Alternate between steps 1-3 until you have completed your set.
5. After you completed the lifting phase of your last rep, lower the dumbbells toward the front of your shoulders like you would during a shoulder press.
6. Lower the dumbbells to your sides as you straighten your elbows and swing your elbows back by your sides.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop the [triceps](../Muscles/Triceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88032be38d4f3e73c9e4c.md), including the [long head](../Muscles/Triceps%20Brachii%20Long%20Head%201905c6f170d880b1a0a7eda6c9b74382.md), which is not trained particularly well by pressing exercises.
1a15c6f170d88069a1d3eb2d608c87b0:
## Setting up
1. Position an adjustable cable to its highest setting, or approach a cable lat pulldown machine.
    1. Either type of equipment can be used interchangeably for this exercise.
2. Connect a D-handle attachment to the cable and select your weight with the loading pin.
3. Stand with one side of your body facing the cable station so that your shoulder is in line with the cable. With your arm near the cable, grasp the handle firmly and direct your palm forward in the same direction your chest is facing.
4. Perform a controlled lunging motion into a half kneeling position with your knee on the side you are holding the cable, resting on the ground, after stepping backward with that side’s leg.
    1. While doing so, allow your elbow to extend and your arm to elevate to be aligned with the cable.
    2. Maintain an upright torso and keep the center of your breastbone facing the same direction as the center of your hips, rather than rotating your trunk toward one side.
    3. In this position, you should feel tension from the cable machine with your elbow extended, so if the cable remains slack (which may occur if you have very long arms), you should position yourself a little farther away from the cable station before assuming the half-kneeling position.
    4. In this position, your arm should be elevated out to your side such that it forms half of a “Y-shape” with your torso, which resembles the position in which one of your arms would be at the top of an overhand wide grip lat pulldown.
## Exercise technique
1. Drive your elbow downward and in toward your side, progressively bending it to pull the handle closer to your torso.
    1. During the initial portion of the pull, you will drive your elbow downward, but you will drive your elbow simultaneously in toward your side and downward during the second half of the pull.
    2. After the initial portion of the pull, when your upper arm is approximately parallel with the ground, the bony prominence on the back of your elbow should be pointing predominantly out to your side toward the cable station as your upper arm and elbow are flared out to your side, which forms half of a “T-shape” with your torso.
    3. Pull through your available range of motion, which will typically result in your elbow being fairly close to the side of your torso at the end of the pull.
    4. Keep your forearm aligned in the same direction as the cable, which will naturally occur with the appropriate degree of elbow bend.
2. Reverse the movement by bringing the handle outward and upward in a controlled manner by allowing your elbow to move out away from your side and upward while it progressively extends until you have returned to the starting position.
    1. At the end of this motion, your elbow should be in an extended position, and your whole arm should be aligned in the same direction as the cable.
    2. There is no need to perform this step extremely slowly, but you should avoid letting the machine’s resistance yank your arm up in an uncontrolled fashion.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set and are ready to repeat the exercise with your other side.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop your [lat](../Muscles/Latissimus%20Dorsi%201905c6f170d880109e73f99ab91d4d47.md) and [teres major](../Muscles/Teres%20Major%201905c6f170d880dbba32f6bd22e3abe6.md) while also meaningfully training your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md).

## Setting up
1. Approach a flat exercise bench or a sturdy object of similar height that allows you to place both hands on top of it, about shoulder-width apart.
    1. In addition to a plyometric box (or a pair of plyometric boxes, depending on the width), you can use an aerobic step elevated on top of risers at a gym.
    2. Outside a gym, you can use objects like a chair (that will not slide), a couch, or a park bench.
2. Sit down on the edge of the bench with an upright torso.
    1. You should be seated with the long part of the bench aligned with your sides.
3. Place your palms on the edge of the bench approximately shoulder width apart, resulting in your arms being directed straight down with straight elbows.
    1. The standard technique involves pointing your knuckles forward with your fingers wrapped around the edge of the bench.
    2. However, pointing your knuckles out to the sides with straight fingers may be preferable. Relative to the standard setup that internally rotates your shoulders, this approach can help you externally rotate your shoulders, as you point your biceps straight forward rather than angling them inward. This difference in shoulder position can result in some people finding bench dips to feel more comfortable for their shoulders when pointing their fingers out to the sides, compared to straight forward.
4. While supporting yourself with your hands, scoot forward until your buttocks are just off the bench. Position your legs out in front of you with straight knees.
    1. You should be bearing weight mostly through the bases of your palms (AKA heels of your hands).
    2. The back of your heels should be on the ground.
5. Pull your shoulder blades back and down to assume a “proud chest” posture.
## Exercise technique
1. Brace your core by tensing the front and sides of your abdominals outward, like you would if you were bracing for someone to strike your stomach with a punch or forcible slap.
    1. Continue bracing your core throughout your set.
2. As you keep them tucked close to your sides, bend your elbows to lower your body in a controlled manner.
    1. Throughout your set, keep your shoulder blades pulled back and down as you avoid letting your shoulders roll forward or shrug up. It can help to think about keeping your chest up.
    2. Keep your hips just in front of the bench rather than letting them drift forward.
    3. Avoid flaring your elbows out away from your sides. When viewed from behind, your elbows should remain aligned with your wrists rather than tracking noticeably outside your wrists.
3. Continue descending through the full range of motion that your shoulder mobility comfortably permits.
    1. It is common for people with healthy shoulders to reach the point at which their elbows are bent by at least 90 degrees, but specifically how deeply you should descend will be influenced by your shoulder mobility.
    2. At your end range, it is normal to feel a stretching sensation in the front of your shoulders, but you should not feel any shoulder discomfort or pain.
    3. If you feel joint discomfort or pain at the bottom, you most likely lowered yourself excessively far relative to your current mobility. Training bench dips over time may improve your mobility, but you should not force yourself into an aggravating range.
    4. While you do not have to perform an extremely slow lowering phase, using a slow and controlled tempo as you approach the bottom position is recommended.
4. Reverse the movement by pushing through the bases of your palms to lift yourself up until you have fully straightened your elbows.
    1. You can think about driving your elbows straight down.
5. Alternate between steps 2-4 until you have completed your set.
    1. Once you have fully straightened your elbows after your last rep, scoot your hips back to sit on the bench.
## Description
While training your [front delts](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Anterior%20Head%201905c6f170d8805da59fc8f9dc0a59e4.md) and [pec major](../Muscles/Pectoralis%20Major%201b95c6f170d880539f8ee236e09d4728.md) to a lesser degree than other dip variations, this exercise will primarily develop your triceps with an emphasis on its [lateral](../Muscles/Triceps%20Brachii%20Lateral%20Head%2018f5c6f170d880c0a504d0d644758f40.md) and [medial](../Muscles/Triceps%20Brachii%20Medial%20Head%201905c6f170d880fbb6e9e7e7ca37f2d1.md) heads.

## Setting up
1. Pick up a pair of kettlebells and stand upright with approximately a shoulder-width stance while holding the kettlebells with straight elbows.
2. Position your hands by the front of your outer thighs and direct your palms so that they are facing backward.
3. Slightly lean forward by hinging at your hips.
    1. Maintain the slight forward lean throughout your set.
## Exercise technique
1. Lift the kettlebells upward by driving your elbows upward and out to your sides through a range of motion that feels comfortable to your shoulders while bending your elbows.
    1. Your mobility will affect how high you are comfortably able to lift the kettlebells, and there is no need to force your shoulders into a range that provokes any discomfort.
    2. While different individuals may be able to lift higher up and others not quite as high, people often can lift their upper arms until they are close to parallel to the ground for a comfortable and effective range of motion.
    3. The kettlebells should remain close to your torso throughout the exercise as they move vertically.
2. Reverse the motion by allowing your elbows to descend in toward your sides as you lower the kettlebells in a controlled manner until you have returned to the starting position with straight elbows.
    1. At the end of the lowering phase, the kettlebells should be situated in front of your thighs.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop your [lateral delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Lateral%20Head%201905c6f170d8804b9b6ef12253eec774.md) and [supraspinatus](../Muscles/Supraspinatus%201905c6f170d880efb440c1614caf1c97.md), which are assisted by your [front delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Anterior%20Head%201905c6f170d8805da59fc8f9dc0a59e4.md) and [upper trap](../Muscles/Upper%20Trapezius%201925c6f170d880009e2cf04b5b29b467.md).

## Setting up
1. Select your weight with the loading pin, and adjust the seat to a height that allows your chest to rest comfortably against the chest pad. 
    1. While you can initially adjust the seat to a height that situates your shoulders approximately level with the parallel handles, the seat height that is best for you depends on the specific machine you use, and trying out different positions may be helpful.
2. Adjust the chest pad to a position that allows you to grasp the parallel handles when your arms are fully outstretched in front of you with straight elbows.
    1. To row through your full range of motion, ideally place the chest pad far enough back that you have to push your shoulder blades forward and apart to grasp the handles with your elbows fully straight.
3. Sit down with your chest resting snugly against the chest pad and your feet flat on the floor before reaching fully forward with extended elbows to grasp the parallel handles firmly with your palms facing in toward each other (i.e., a neutral grip).
    1. If you were able to grasp the handles with any amount of elbow bend, you could let go of the handles and adjust the chest pad before grasping the handles again.
## Exercise technique
1. Pull the handles back toward the sides of your torso by driving your elbows backward while simultaneously bending them and pulling your shoulder blades together.
    1. Move your elbows through a path of motion that feels comfortable to you, which will typically involve keeping them tucked close to your sides with this grip rather than notably flaring your elbows away from your sides (which is typically more comfortable with a wider overhand grip).
    2. Keep your chest in contact with the chest pad throughout the set.
    3. Pull through your available range of motion, which will typically result in your elbows being level with your torso or slightly behind your torso at the end of the lifting phase.
    4. As a cue for training your upper back muscles, you can think about squeezing your shoulder blades together at the end of the pull as if you were trying to pinch a pencil with your shoulder blades.
2. Reverse the movement by allowing your elbows to move forward in a controlled manner, progressively straightening until they are outstretched in front of you.
    1. Your shoulder blades will naturally move apart from one another, but you can exaggerate this motion by intentionally allowing the weight to pull them further apart than your resting position at the bottom. This will stretch your upper back muscles and may help you train them more effectively.
    2. While you do not have to perform this step extremely slowly, you should avoid letting the weight abruptly yank your arms forward in an uncontrolled fashion.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This row primarily trains your [lat](../Muscles/Latissimus%20Dorsi%201905c6f170d880109e73f99ab91d4d47.md), [teres major](../Muscles/Teres%20Major%201905c6f170d880dbba32f6bd22e3abe6.md), [rear delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Posterior%20Head%201905c6f170d880a29e5ec26f4d257c01.md), [traps](../Muscles/Trapezius%201b95c6f170d880bebf89c759b592e81f.md), and [rhomboids](../Muscles/Rhomboids%201b95c6f170d880c8a84de94f5232a509.md), which are assisted by your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md).

## Setting up
1. Prepare the barbell with your desired load by adding weight plates to it or leaving the barbell unloaded, which is recommended if performing this exercise for the first time.
    1. A typical barbell that weighs 20kg (44lb) can commonly be too heavy to use with appropriate technique for individuals who lack much wrist extension training experience, so a wrist extension variation that allows for lighter loads (e.g., seated dumbbell wrist extension) may initially be preferable.
    2. If you have access to one, you can also use a fixed-weight straight barbell, which may be lighter than a typical barbell that has sleeves on which to add weight plates.
2. Pick up the barbell with an overhand grip where your palms are facing back toward you.
3. While holding the barbell, sit down on a flat exercise bench or chair and position your forearms on top of your thighs with your palms facing down toward the floor and your wrists situated slightly in front of your knees.
    1. To achieve this position, you will be leaning forward at your hips when seated with your elbows bent.
4. Allow the force from the bar to bend your wrists and bring your hands downward such that your palms are directed at an angle down and back toward you.
    1. In this position, the bar should not be contacting your legs, so scoot your forearms forward if it is initially contacting your legs.
## Exercise technique
1. Lift the bar upward by extending your wrists through their available range of motion while keeping your forearms resting on your thighs.
    1. All of the motion should be coming from your wrists as your hands move upward.
    2. About halfway through the lifting phase, your palms should be facing straight down toward the floor when your hands are aligned with your forearms.
    3. At the end of the lifting phase, when the bar is fully raised, your palms should be angled forward.
    4. When performing this exercise appropriately, you should feel tension in the muscles on the top side of your forearms.
2. Reverse the motion by lowering the bar in a controlled manner until you have returned to the starting position with your palms directed at an angle down and back toward you.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can effectively train the seven [wrist extensor muscles](../Muscles/Wrist%20extensors%202c35c6f170d8804ab377fe1e53371f25.md) on the side of your forearm opposite your palm.

## Setting up
1. While the barbell is on the ground or in an elevated position, such as a power rack, prepare the barbell with your desired load by adding weight plates to it or by leaving the barbell unloaded.
    1. Setting up will be easier when using an elevated position, especially if you are using relatively heavy loads for this exercise.
    2. The bar will be easiest to pick up if positioned at a height slightly lower than the level of your hands when standing upright with your arms relaxed at your sides.
    3. If you have access to one, you can also use a fixed-weight straight barbell, which may be lighter than a typical 20kg (44lb) barbell that has sleeves on which to add weight plates.
2. With your backside facing the bar, stand close in front of the middle of the bar with a hip-width stance and straight elbows before hinging at your hips while bending your knees until your hands are level with the bar.
    1. Keep your lower back near a neutral position, like you have when you are normally standing upright, rather than meaningfully rounding your lower back while doing so.
3. Firmly grasp the bar with a shoulder-width overhand grip such that your palms are facing backward.
4. By extending your hips and knees, stand upright with the bar while continuing to keep your elbows straight and your lower back near a neutral position.
    1. Once upright, the bar should be directly behind your thighs.
    2. Maintain this upright position with straight elbows throughout your set.
## Exercise technique
1. Lift the bar upward by curling your wrists through their available range of motion while keeping your arms stationary.
    1. All of the motion should be coming from your wrists, and the bar will move slightly farther behind your thighs as it simultaneously moves upward.
    2. Your palms should be angled upward once you have fully curled your wrists.
    3. When performing this exercise appropriately, you should feel tension in the muscles on the palm side of your forearms.
2. Reverse the motion by lowering the bar in a controlled manner until you have returned to the starting position with your palms directed straight backward.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can effectively train the six [wrist flexor muscles](../Muscles/Wrist%20flexor%20muscles%202c85c6f170d880a49749f7d7a9f307c8.md) on the palm side of your forearm.

## Setting up
1. After adding weight plates to the machine, sit down with your back in full contact with the backrest.
    1. The machine’s safety stoppers (which can be moved with one or two safety handles, depending upon the specific machine) should already be locked, and you will keep them locked throughout your set.
    2. If your machine has an adjustable seat, you can also initially adjust the seat to whichever position feels most comfortable to you, but the seat position is unlikely to affect this exercise.
    3. Your lower back should be in a fairly flat position rather than being meaningfully rounded, like in a slouched position, which could occur if you sit your hips excessively forward when sitting down.
2. With approximately a shoulder width stance, place the front halves of your feet onto the bottom of the foot plate with your heels hanging off the edge.
    1. Maintain this foot position throughout your set.
3. While grasping the hand grips, press the platform away from you by extending your knees until they are straight or only slightly bent.
    1. You should maintain this knee position (rather than bending and extending your knees) while performing this exercise until you are ready to finish your set.
    2. Depending on their mobility, some people may be able to adopt a position of knee hyperextension, which is when the knees bend backward beyond a straight position. Being able to reach a mildly hyperextended knee position is normal for many individuals and is not inherently problematic. However, certain individuals may experience knee discomfort if they utilize a hyperextended knee position during this exercise, so keeping a straight or slightly bent knee position instead of a hyperextended knee position may be preferable.
## Exercise technique
1. Press the platform away from you by pointing the balls of your feet away from you (in a manner similar to stepping on a car’s gas pedal) through the available range of motion of your ankles.
    1. Motion should occur exclusively at your ankles, while knees and hips do not move.
2. In a controlled manner, reverse the motion by allowing the front halves of your feet to move back toward you through the available range of motion of your ankles.
    1. How far you are able to move will be dependent on your mobility.
    2. Strive to lower your heels as far as you can, and you will likely feel a stretching sensation in your calf at the bottom position.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set and are ready to lower the platform back onto the safety stoppers by bending your knees.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop your [gastrocnemius](../Muscles/Gastrocnemius%201b95c6f170d880b59622dd4a8639aa2f.md) and [soleus](../Muscles/Soleus%201925c6f170d88052bbb6c59dc04f2e1a.md) while simultaneously improving calf flexibility through loaded stretching.

## Setting up
1. Using an overhand grip, grasp an elastic band with both hands in front of your torso while standing upright with your feet in approximately a shoulder-width stance.
    1. Inspect the band to confirm it does not have any small tears, since a small tear can swiftly become a full tear when stretching a band.
2. Position your hands so that they are somewhat greater than shoulder width apart from each other, with slack taken out of the band.
3. With straight elbows, elevate your arms in front of your torso until they are approximately parallel to the ground.
    1. In this position, your palms should be directed down toward the ground.
    2. Maintain this position throughout your set.
## Exercise technique
1. Pull your hands apart and backward until your arms and torso form a “T-shape.”
    1. If you set up by grasping the band with your hands too close together, you may reach the limit of the band’s extensibility (as indicated by an abrupt increase in resistance from the band) prior to your hands being pulled entirely apart from each other. If you notice this occurring, bring your hands back together and adjust your setup by gripping the band with your hands further apart. Continuing to pull the band apart once a portion has fully stretched may cause the band to tear.
2. Reverse the motion by bringing your hands forward and toward each other until they have returned to their starting position.
    1. You should feel tension from the band throughout the entire range of motion.
    2. Do not bring your hands so close together that the band becomes slack.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise trains your [rear delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Posterior%20Head%201905c6f170d880a29e5ec26f4d257c01.md), which is assisted by your [traps](../Muscles/Trapezius%201b95c6f170d880bebf89c759b592e81f.md) and [rhomboids](../Muscles/Rhomboids%201b95c6f170d880c8a84de94f5232a509.md), along with your rotator cuff’s [infraspinatus](../Muscles/Infraspinatus%201905c6f170d88026aebcf3953e2e440f.md), [teres minor](../Muscles/Teres%20Minor%201905c6f170d88098824dc8136557c410.md), and [supraspinatus](../Muscles/Supraspinatus%201905c6f170d880efb440c1614caf1c97.md).

## Setting up
1. Position an adjustable bench at a low incline angle (e.g., near 30 degrees) and set a pair of dumbbells under the head of the bench.
    1. As a different variation, which you can use if your bench does not have a low incline setting, you can alternatively select a moderate incline angle (e.g., near 45 degrees) and otherwise use the same technique for this exercise.
2. Lie down with your chest contacting the head of the bench and your legs spread out as you position the balls of your feet on the ground.
3. Grasp the dumbbells, position your arms so that they are perpendicular to the ground with extended elbows, and rotate your arms so that your palms are facing forward.
    1. Keep your elbows extended and your palms facing this direction throughout your set.
## Exercise technique
1. Raise your arms upward and straight out to your sides through your available shoulder range of motion so that they form a “T-shape” with your torso as you continue to keep your chest in contact with the bench.
    1. You can strive to raise your arms until they are at least parallel to the floor, but your shoulder mobility will affect how high you can raise your arms.
    2. If you notice your chest lifting up off the bench during this movement, that indicates that you most likely are dynamically extending your lumbar spine, which can occur as a compensation pattern instead of lifting your arm only with your shoulder girdle muscles.
2. Reverse the motion by lowering your arms in a controlled manner until your arms have returned to being perpendicular to the ground.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise trains your [rear delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Posterior%20Head%201905c6f170d880a29e5ec26f4d257c01.md), [traps](../Muscles/Trapezius%201b95c6f170d880bebf89c759b592e81f.md), and [rhomboids](../Muscles/Rhomboids%201b95c6f170d880c8a84de94f5232a509.md), which are assisted by your rotator cuff’s [infraspinatus](../Muscles/Infraspinatus%201905c6f170d88026aebcf3953e2e440f.md), [teres minor](../Muscles/Teres%20Minor%201905c6f170d88098824dc8136557c410.md), and [supraspinatus](../Muscles/Supraspinatus%201905c6f170d880efb440c1614caf1c97.md).

## Setting up
1. Pick up one dumbbell and sit down on a seated bench or a flat exercise bench with your feet flat on the ground. As you are sitting down, place the dumbbell onto one of your thighs as you are holding the handle with both hands wrapped around each other.
    1. If you use a seated bench, the back rest should be low enough that it will not be within the path of the dumbbell and restrict your range of motion for this exercise.
    2. The tall back rest of an adjustable bench positioned fully upright may be more likely to limit your range than a fixed seated bench with a back rest that does not reach your head.
2. Lift the dumbbell up to shoulder level with your elbows bent by curling the weight with both arms.
    1. To assist in moving the weight into position, you can march your thigh up while curling it.
3. Press the dumbbell up overhead with both arms in a shoulder press motion until your arms are vertical.
    1. The back of your elbows should be pointing forward.
    2. Rather than being excessively arched, your lower back and neck should be near a neutral position, like when you are normally standing upright and looking straight ahead.
4. While keeping your elbows up, slightly bend your elbows to tilt one end of the dumbbell down.
5. Reposition your hands so that both palms are firmly contacting the higher end of the dumbbell. Cross your thumbs over each other firmly around the handle. Simultaneously cross your index fingers over each other, resulting in your thumbs and index fingers resembling close to a diamond shape.
    1. In this position, one end of the dumbbell should be above your hands, while the other end is below your hands.
    2. You will continue securely gripping the dumbbell in this manner throughout your set. Make sure that your thumbs stay wrapped around the handle for stability.
## Exercise technique
1. Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head in a controlled manner while keeping your elbow up.
    1. Essentially all the motion should occur from your forearms hinging at your elbows without any shoulder motion. You can think of your elbows as the center of an analog clock, while your forearms are the hands that rotate about these center elbows during this exercise.
    2. Predominantly keep your elbows tucked in as they are chiefly pointing forward rather than out to your side. However, you can allow your elbows to flare slightly out away from your sides if that feels natural and comfortable to you.
    3. As you keep your elbows up, your upper arms should remain in a vertical position by the sides of your head.
2. Continue lowering the dumbbell until you have fully bent your elbows or can lightly tap your upper back with the dumbbell.
    1. It is normal to be able to bend the elbows beyond 90 degrees during this exercise, but specifically how far you can bend your elbows may be limited by the flexibility of your long head of the triceps.
    2. While some lifters have the flexibility to reach their upper back with the dumbbell, wherever you feel a notable stretching sensation in your triceps can be an appropriate end range.
    3. While you do not have to perform the lowering phase with an extremely slow tempo, you should be actively controlling the weight the entire way.
3. Reverse the movement by straightening your elbows to lift the dumbbell overhead.
    1. You can finish the lifting phase with a slight bend in your elbows rather than fully straightening them. A slight bend will keep one end of the dumbbell tilted down and make it easier to maintain a secure grip with the higher end of the dumbbell resting on your palms.
    2. Continue keeping your elbows up as all the motion occurs from your elbow without moving your shoulders.
4. Alternate between steps 1-3 until you have completed your set.
5. After you have completed the lifting phase of your last rep, firmly grasp the handle with your lower hand while keeping the palm of your upper hand against the side of the dumbbell.
    1. Grasping the handle with one hand will make it easier for you to lower the weight compared to if you kept both palms against one end of the dumbbell.
6. Use both hands to lower the dumbbell toward your chest before setting it down.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop the [triceps](../Muscles/Triceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88032be38d4f3e73c9e4c.md), including the [long head](../Muscles/Triceps%20Brachii%20Long%20Head%201905c6f170d880b1a0a7eda6c9b74382.md), which is not trained particularly well by pressing exercises.
1a15c6f170d88076b7f5e24347a8d8a0:
## Setting up
1. Adjust the machine’s seat to a height that places the handles slightly above shoulder level once you are seated.
    1. This seat height is an appropriate starting point for most people, but the ideal seat height specifically should allow you to press through your full range of motion while initially gripping the handles with your elbows stacked under the handles.
    2. If the seat is excessively high, you will not be able to position your elbows directly under the handles (when viewed from the side).
    3. If the seat is excessively low, your range of motion for this exercise will be limited.
    4. Some trial and error may be needed to find the best height for you as an individual.
2. Add weight plates of your desired load to the machine. 
3. Sit down on the machine’s seat with your back and the back of your hip bones snugly against the backrest.
    1. Your feet should be flat on the ground.
    2. You can optionally rest your head against the backrest if it is tall enough, or you can simply keep your neck near a neutral position, like when you are normally looking straight ahead.
4. With your palms facing in toward each other and elbows bent, firmly grasp the handles that are angled forward. Position your elbows directly under the handles, resulting in your forearms being vertical when viewed from the side.
    1. If your machine only has handles directed out to the sides that can allow an overhand grip but not a neutral grip, you cannot perform this specific variation. However, you can select the “[overhand grip plate-loaded machine shoulder press](Plate-loaded%20machine%20shoulder%20press%201a15c6f170d880208cfdca4035bdedab.md)” from this database as an alternative.
    2. Rather than having handles directed completely forward, which allows a pure neutral grip, some machines have handles angled between forward and out to the side, allowing a semi-neutral grip. 
    3. Hold the handles on top of the bases of your palms (AKA heels of your hands) with mostly straight wrists that allow for a comfortable and stable grip that you will maintain throughout your set. Squeezing the handles firmly can help promote this wrist position.
    4. If you cannot comfortably position your elbows under the handles, mildly lower the seat height before resuming your setup.
    5. Situating your elbows under the handles and maintaining this alignment will naturally promote the appropriate degree of elbow tuck during this exercise.
5. Assume a “proud chest” posture that puffs your chest slightly up toward the ceiling, and maintain this posture throughout your set.
    1. Rather than excessively arching your lower back, maintain the natural curvature of your lower back like when you are normally standing upright.
## Exercise technique
1. Brace your core by tensing the front and sides of your abdominals outward, like you would if you were bracing for someone to strike your stomach with a punch or forcible slap.
    1. You will continue bracing your core throughout your set, which will help your body function as a stable platform from which to press.
2. Press the handles up overhead until you have straightened your elbows.
    1. While motion simultaneously occurs at your shoulders and elbows, your elbows should remain stacked under your wrists when viewed from the side. This will result in your elbows driving up in front of your body rather than being excessively flared out away from your sides.
    2. Throughout your set, continue keeping your back snuggly against the backrest and your feet planted on the ground.
3. Reverse the movement by lowering the handles in a controlled manner toward the starting position.
    1. With the appropriate seat height, you should finish the lowering phase with the handles slightly above shoulder level, as your elbows are lower than your shoulders.
    2. At the bottom, you can lightly tap the machine’s arms against the stoppers underneath them. A gentle tap will confirm that you have moved through the full range of motion in a controlled manner.
    3. Continue keeping your elbows stacked underneath the handles, resulting in your forearms remaining in a vertical position when viewed from the side.
4. Alternate between steps 2 and 3 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop your [front delts](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Anterior%20Head%201905c6f170d8805da59fc8f9dc0a59e4.md) while also training your [lateral delts](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Lateral%20Head%201905c6f170d8804b9b6ef12253eec774.md), [upper pec major](../Muscles/Pectoralis%20Major%20(Clavicular%20Head%201905c6f170d880ef9b6bd48adbf440bd.md), [triceps](../Muscles/Triceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88032be38d4f3e73c9e4c.md), [traps](../Muscles/Trapezius%201b95c6f170d880bebf89c759b592e81f.md), and [serratus anterior](../Muscles/Serratus%20Anterior%201955c6f170d880a8b8b9e712f2ec58e0.md).

## Setting up
1. Position a barbell in the J-cups of a power rack set approximately to the height of your hips while standing or alternatively position a Smith machine’s bar to the same height.
    1. This exercise can be performed with the same technique whether you use a barbell and power rack or a Smith machine.
    2. If you use a power rack, situate the barbell snugly in contact with the back corner of the J-cups since the middle portion of certain J-cups can be wide enough to allow the barbell to roll forward or backward, which is undesirable for this exercise.
2. Stand in front of the middle of the bar with your back facing the back of the power rack/Smith machine and firmly grasp the bar with your hands slightly outside of shoulder width using an overhand grip that results in your palms facing down.
3. While holding the bar, walk your feet forward to recline your torso into a more horizontal position until your chest is underneath the bar. Simultanesouly allow your elbows to straighten, and bridge your hips up by squeezing your glutes.
    1. In the bridged position, which you will maintain throughout your set, you should be able to draw a straight line from your knees through your hips to your shoulders when viewed from the side.
    2. For the standard technique, you will walk your feet forward until you can fully extend your knees with the back of your heels on the ground, while the soles of your feet are off the ground and facing forward.
## Exercise technique
1. Pull your chest toward the bar by driving your elbows simultaneously downward and backward while progressively bending them and pulling your shoulder blades together.
    1. Allow your elbows naturally to flare out away from your sides in a manner that feels comfortable to you.
    2. Pull through your full range of motion while aiming for your chest to reach the bar.
    3. Movement should occur at your shoulders, shoulder blades, and elbows, but your torso and lower body should remain nearly stationary in the bridged position that is akin to holding a [reverse plank](Reverse%20plank%201a45c6f170d880faa555d3e604efa65f.md).
2. Reverse the movement by letting your chest move down away from the bar in a controlled manner as your elbows progressively straighten.
    1. Fully return to the starting position with your arms outstretched up in front of you.
    2. Continue keeping your knees, hips, and shoulders aligned.
    3. Allow your shoulder blades to spread apart naturally.
    4. While you do not have to lower yourself extremely slowly, you should actively resist the descent rather than abruptly dropping in an uncontrolled fashion.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This row can effectively develop your [lats](../Muscles/Latissimus%20Dorsi%201905c6f170d880109e73f99ab91d4d47.md), [teres majores](../Muscles/Teres%20Major%201905c6f170d880dbba32f6bd22e3abe6.md), [rear delts](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Posterior%20Head%201905c6f170d880a29e5ec26f4d257c01.md), [traps](../Muscles/Trapezius%201b95c6f170d880bebf89c759b592e81f.md), and [rhomboids](../Muscles/Rhomboids%201b95c6f170d880c8a84de94f5232a509.md), which are assisted by your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md).

## Setting up
1. If your machine allows you to adjust the height of the footplate, select a height that will allow your legs to be in an approximately horizontal position once you are in the starting position.
    1. After estimating where this setting may be, you can adjust it during later steps if warranted.
    2. Not all machines permit you to adjust the footplate height.
2. Horizontally adjust the machine’s footplate to a setting that will allow the pad to support the front of your hip bones without meaningfully restricting back motion when you set up with your feet on the foot plate.
    1. If the footplate is positioned excessively close to the pad (resulting in the pad predominantly supporting your thighs), your hips will not be stabilized as well, which can make it more challenging to emphasize training your back muscles.
    2. If the footplate is positioned excessively far from the pad, the pad can restrict your lower back’s motion.
    3. Since a sweet spot exists, some trial and error may be needed to find your ideal pad position.
3. Climb up onto the machine, and position your feet against the footplate with your lower legs between the leg rollers while the front of your hips are resting on the pad.
    1. The back of your lower legs should be snugly pressed into the top pair of leg rollers slightly above your heels.
    2. Your knees should be straight, and your soles should be firmly contacting the footplate.
    3. While you are setting your feet, you can use the handles for assistance.
    4. Some machines have a step that you can use to help you get into position.
    5. With the appropriate footplate setting, the front of your hip bones should be resting on the pad, while your torso is unsupported.
4. Cross your arms across your chest with bent elbows to position each hand on the front of the opposite shoulder.
    1. Maintain this arm position throughout your set.
    2. Your back and neck should be near a neutral position, like when you are normally standing upright, looking straight ahead.
## Exercise technique
1. Round your entire back in a slow and controlled curling manner through the full range of motion that is comfortable for you.
    1. You may feel a stretching sensation in your back muscles in the bottom position, but you should not feel any discomfort at the end range. Only round your back as far as is comfortable.
    2. At the bottom, your abdomen may be curled around the rounded front half of the pad.
    3. Rather than moving only one part of your back, strive to round your lower, middle, and upper back.
2. Reverse the movement by extending (straightening) your back in a controlled manner without hinging at your hips.
    1. At the end of the lifting phase, your back should be near a neutral position, which involves your lower back being mildly arched.
    2. For increasing the size and strength of your back muscles, there is no need to arch your back maximally like you would during a cobra yoga pose.
    3. Keep your glutes relaxed to the best of your ability as you focus on moving your spine rather than your hips.
    4. You should feel your spinal extensor muscles, which run along each side of the spine, contract to extend your back.
3. Alternate between steps 2 and 3 until you have completed your set.
4. After your last rep, you can grasp the handles to help you dismount the machine.
## Description
This exercise can dynamically train the [erector spinae](../Muscles/Thoracolumbar%20Erector%20Spinae%201bb5c6f170d880a7a719e8f6d05d00a8.md) and [deep intrinsic spinal extensor muscles](../Muscles/Deep%20Intrinsic%20Thoracolumbar%20Extensors%201bb5c6f170d880f58501d5f27212caed.md) that run along the length of your entire back.
