## Setting up
1. Anchor a long looped elastic band of your desired tension level around the center of a pull-up bar.
    1. To anchor the band, you can initially drape the band over the bar, loop one end of the band into the middle of the other end, and pull that end until it is taut.
    2. If the bar is out of reach when standing on the ground, you can initially position it, then step up onto an aerobic step, sturdy box, or bumper plate to place the bar within reach while situating the band and grasping the bar during the next step. Position the step slightly behind the bar rather than directly underneath it, so you can keep your legs straight during the exercise without contacting the step.
    3. If your bar has rough knurling rather than a smooth surface, anchoring the band directly around the bar can increase the likelihood of the band tearing over time. Initially, placing a fat grip attachment or hand towel around a bar before anchoring the band can help prevent a bar with knurling from tearing the band.
    4. Before using it, inspect the band to confirm it has no small tears, as a small tear can quickly become a full tear when stretching the band.
2. Stand under the bar, and pull the band down with both arms.
    1. Each side of the band should be flat with no twists.
3. March up one leg and step into the band with the middle of your foot snugly against the bottom end of the band’s loop before lowering your foot while straightening your leg. Alternatively, you can bend one knee and loop the band around your upper shin.
    1. Since the band’s tension increases as you stretch it, situating the band around your foot with a straight knee will provide greater assistance compared to if you situate the band around your upper shin with your knee bent.
    2. If your pull-up bar is not tall enough for you to avoid contacting the ground with your foot at the bottom of the rep when keeping your leg straight, looping the band around your upper shin will be a better option. Otherwise, you can select whichever approach aligns with your preference while providing your desired level of assistance.
    3. With either setup, the band should feel secure rather than feeling like it may slide around during the exercise.
4. Reach up overhead and firmly grasp the pull-up bar with your palms facing forward (i.e., an overhand grip) and your hands situated slightly outside shoulder width.
    1. For the most stable grip, wrap your fingers around the bar with the bar pressed into where the bases of your fingers meet the palm side of your knuckles.
    2. If you position the bar closer to the middle of your palms (rather than the bases of your fingers), it can slide up your hand while hanging on it, which can pull on your hand skin in an uncomfortable way and increase the risk of tearing a callus.
5. Hang on the bar with your elbows straightened. If you are standing on a step and have the band under your foot, step off the step and let both legs hang straight down toward the ground. If you have the band around your upper shin, lift your other foot off the ground by bending that knee and keeping both knees bent throughout the exercise.
    1. You can optionally place your other leg (which was not initially in contact with the band) within the band if you wish. 
## Exercise technique
1. While hanging on the bar with straight elbows, simultaneously pull your shoulder blades down and mildly arch your middle and upper back to assume a “proud chest” that is angled slightly upward.
    1. Maintain this “proud chest” posture throughout your set.
2. Pull your chest up toward the bar by driving your elbows down and toward your sides while progressively bending your elbows.
    1. Since the bar is fixed, your elbows won't actually drive downward; having the intention helps you pull yourself upward with an appropriate technique that effectively trains your back muscles.
    2. Strive to pull through your full available range of motion, which commonly results in the upper arms near the sides of the torso and elbows bent enough that the forearms contact the biceps. However, individuals may have different ranges of motion that their bodies allow.
    3. Rather than swinging your legs, statically keep them in a similar position throughout the rep.
3. Reverse the motion by lowering your body in a controlled manner until you have returned to the starting position with your elbows straightened and arms fully overhead.
    1. You do not have to perform an extremely slow lowering phase, but you should actively control the entire descent rather than simply dropping down.
4. Alternate between steps 2 and 3 until you have completed your set.
    1. Once you have fully straightened your elbows after your last rep, you can return one foot onto the ground or step, shift your weight into step/ground, march your other leg up and out of the band, and release the bar.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop your [lat](../Muscles/Latissimus%20Dorsi%201905c6f170d880109e73f99ab91d4d47.md) and [teres major](../Muscles/Teres%20Major%201905c6f170d880dbba32f6bd22e3abe6.md) while also meaningfully training your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md).
1a15c6f170d880cdb451e459ddf41d2a:
## Setting up
1. While standing under a pull-up bar, reach up and grasp it with your palms facing forward (i.e., an overhand grip) and your hands situated near shoulder-width apart or somewhat wider.
    1. If you wish to do so, you can use a different grip, such as an underhand or a neutral (i.e., palms facing toward each other) grip, while otherwise using the same technique for this exercise.
2. Hang on the bar with straight elbows by bending your knees and lifting your feet off the ground.
## Exercise technique
1. While keeping your elbows straight, pull your shoulder blades downward through your available range of motion.
    1. This will move your shoulders away from your ears, while the rest of your body, except for your arms, lifts upward to a small extent.
    2. While the range of motion for this exercise may vary among different individuals, this exercise involves a low amplitude of total movement.
    3. You can think about packing your armpits down into your pockets as a technique cue.
2. Reverse the motion by allowing your shoulder blades to move upward in a controlled manner until you have reached a position that is akin to when you shrug your shoulders upward.
    1. This will move your shoulders closer toward your ears, while the rest of your body, except for your arms, moves downward to a small extent.
    2. Continue to keep your elbows straight.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise will train your [lats](../Muscles/Latissimus%20Dorsi%201905c6f170d880109e73f99ab91d4d47.md), [lower traps](../Muscles/Lower%20Trapezius%201925c6f170d88092b0bfc88e7ed9e50a.md), and [pec minor](../Muscles/Pectoralis%20Minor%201905c6f170d88030b03dd3f99706ecb0.md).

## Setting up
1. At a cable station, adjust the cable to near the height of your waist when standing, clip in a D-handle attachment, and select your desired weight with the loading pin.
2. While standing in front of the cable station and slightly to the side (such that the front of one shoulder is in line with the cable station), use your hand on the side closer to the cable to grasp the handle with an overhand grip and take a step backward.
3. On the side holding the handle, raise your upper arm approximately 90 degrees out to your side (so that it is parallel to the ground) while bending your elbow to approximately 90 degrees and keeping your wrist in a fairly straight position.
    1. Maintain this position throughout your set.
4. Rotate your forearm so that it is parallel to the ground, which will result in your palm facing down toward the ground.
    1. In this position, you should feel tension from the cable, so if that is not the case, take another step backward away from the cable station.
## Exercise technique
1. Pull the handle upward and backward by rotating your forearm away from the cable station while moving through your shoulder’s available range of motion as you continue to keep your upper arm held out to your side and parallel to the ground.
    1. If you have typical shoulder mobility, you should be able to finish this motion with your forearm near a vertical position, but not everyone will be able to rotate as far backward.
    2. All of this movement should occur from shoulder rotation as the bony prominence on the back of your elbow continues pointing straight out to the side throughout the rep.
    3. When thinking about this technique, it can be helpful to view your forearm as a clock’s hand, while your elbow is the center about which rotation occurs without any side-to-side motion.
2. Reverse the motion by rotating your forearm toward the cable station as you move the handle downward and forward in a controlled manner until you have returned to the starting position.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set with one side and are ready to repeat the exercise with your other side.
## Description
This exercise can effectively train your rotator cuff’s [infraspinatus](../Muscles/Infraspinatus%201905c6f170d88026aebcf3953e2e440f.md) and [teres minor](../Muscles/Teres%20Minor%201905c6f170d88098824dc8136557c410.md), along with a portion of the [supraspinatus](../Muscles/Supraspinatus%201905c6f170d880efb440c1614caf1c97.md).

## Setting up
1. Connect a lat pulldown bar to the cable, select your weight with the loading pin, and adjust the thigh pad to a height that lets you position your thighs snugly against it while sitting with your feet flat on the floor.
    1. If you do not have a standard lat pulldown bar attachment, which has a straight body and mildly angled ends, you can use a different attachment that lets you grasp it with a wide overhand grip.
2. While facing the bar and standing above the seat, firmly grasp the bar with a well outside shoulder width overhand grip, such that your palms are directed forward, and your arms form a “Y-shape” with your torso.
    1. Positioning your hands about 50% further apart than your shoulder width is appropriate, but a wide grip can encompass a range of grip widths, and specifically how wide you grasp the bar is up to your preference.
    2. What is personally considered a wide grip to you can also be influenced by the specific grip width you use for your standard pulldown, which you can somewhat widen to individualize your wide grip. For instance, for your wide grip, you can place your index finger on the bar just outside where you would otherwise place your little finger when performing your standard pulldown.
    3. Feel free to try out mildly different grip widths to determine if any particular position feels best to you.
3. While holding the bar, sit down on the machine’s seat and scoot forward as far as you can with the upper portion of your thighs snugly pressed against the machine’s thigh pad.
    1. When sitting down, allow your elbows to extend and your arms to raise overhead in line with the cable's resistance.
    2. Compared to the standard lat pulldown, where you pull the bar down to your chest, you sit farther forward on the seat with the behind-the-neck variation, so your head does not restrict the bar's path.
4. As you are seated upright, nod your head to bring your chin closer toward your chest, which reduces the likelihood of your head obstructing the bar path.
    1. From this position, your elbows should be in an extended position with your arms situated overhead, and you should feel tension from the cable station holding your arms in this position.
    2. If you notice the cable remains slack in this position (which may occur for certain individuals who are quite tall and have long arms), widening out your grip even further may be needed to experience resistance throughout the full range of motion for this exercise.
## Exercise technique
1. Pull the bar down behind your head toward your upper back by driving your elbows down toward your sides as you progressively bend them.
    1. Simultaneosuly pull your shoulder blades down away from your ears.
    2. How far you can pull the bar will be affected by your shoulder mobility.
    3. If your shoulders feel comfortable doing so, you can pull the bar downward until it contacts your upper back, but you should not force yourself into any range of motion that produces shoulder discomfort.
2. Reverse the movement by allowing your elbows to lift upward and away from your torso as they progressively straighten to raise the bar in a controlled manner.
    1. Let your shoulder blades move naturally as they elevate with your arms.
    2. Finish with your arms overhead and your elbows fully straightened.
    3. There is no need to perform this step extremely slowly, but you should avoid letting the machine’s resistance yank your arms up in an uncontrolled fashion.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop your [lat](../Muscles/Latissimus%20Dorsi%201905c6f170d880109e73f99ab91d4d47.md) and [teres major](../Muscles/Teres%20Major%201905c6f170d880dbba32f6bd22e3abe6.md) while also meaningfully training your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md).

## Setting up
1. Approach a step or a sturdy object that can function as a step. You should be by a surface (e.g., handrail, wall, power rack) where you can place one hand to assist with maintaining your balance while performing this exercise.
    1. Based on the equipment at your disposal, a variety of objects can serve as your step. Make sure the object can support your weight, will not move once you are on it, and allows you to lower your heels through your full range of motion during the exercise.
    2. As an alternative to a staircase’s bottom step, you may select a power rack’s bottom beam if the beam is sufficiently tall.
    3. Additionally, a calf raise block, aerobic step, deadlift block, or thick bumper plate can each be positioned near a wall or power rack for stability. Depending on your bodyweight, anchoring an aerobic step with weight on top of it may be required to prevent the step from tipping.
2. After placing your hand onto the nearby surface for balance assistance, step onto the step with the front halves of your feet on the step while the back halves of your feet are hanging off the step.
3. While keeping one foot on the step, lift your other foot off the step by bending that knee.
    1. Keep this foot in this position off the step throughout the set while you keep the front half of your working leg’s foot on the step.
## Exercise technique
1. With the leg that is standing on the step, raise your heel into the air while keeping that side’s knee straight and your trunk upright.
2. In a controlled manner, allow your heel to descend toward the ground through your ankle’s available range of motion while continuing to keep the knee straight on your working side.
    1. How far you are able to lower your heel will be dependent on your mobility.
    2. Strive to lower your heel as far as you can, and you will likely feel a stretching sensation in your calf at the bottom position.
3. Reverse the motion by lifting your heel up through your ankle’s available range of motion.
4. Continue to perform the calf raises by alternating between steps 2 and 3 until you have completed your set and are ready to repeat this exercise with your other side.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop your [gastrocnemius](../Muscles/Gastrocnemius%201b95c6f170d880b59622dd4a8639aa2f.md) and [soleus](../Muscles/Soleus%201925c6f170d88052bbb6c59dc04f2e1a.md) while simultaneously improving calf flexibility through loaded stretching.
1a15c6f170d880d2be19ea52502589f2:
## Setting up
1. Adjust a cable station’s pulley to near waist height, select your desired weight with the loading pin, and attach a bar with a straight (or mostly straight) body to the cable.
    1. Any bar that enables you to perform this exercise with an overhand grip can be similarly used, including a standard straight bar, a lat pulldown bar (with a long straight body and angled ends), and a multi-grip EZ bar.
2. While facing the cable station, grasp the bar with an overhand grip.
3. Pivot your body 180 degrees while simultaneously repositioning your arms such that your upper arms are raised up high with your elbows close to being fully bent with fairly straight wrists as the cable is applying a downward force to the bar behind your head.
    1. The arm movement performed during this step is akin to a controlled swinging-like motion.
    2. How high you can raise your upper arms is influenced by your mobility.
4. Adopt a staggered stance by stepping forward with one foot, and slightly lean forward by hinging at your hips
    1. In this position, you should feel tension from the cable, so if that is not the case, you should step further forward until you feel tension from the cable.
    2. Maintain this position throughout your set.
## Exercise technique
1. While keeping your elbows high, press the bar upward by extending your elbows until they are straightened.
    1. At the end of this motion, the bar should be situated above your head.
    2. If the cable contacts the back of your head during this motion, you can tuck your chin closer to your chest for clearance.
2. Reverse the motion by bending your elbows through your available range of motion to lower the bar in a controlled manner until you have returned to the starting position.
    1. Strive to have your elbows as close to fully bent as you can by the time you have finished this motion.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop the [triceps](../Muscles/Triceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88032be38d4f3e73c9e4c.md), including the [long head](../Muscles/Triceps%20Brachii%20Long%20Head%201905c6f170d880b1a0a7eda6c9b74382.md), which is not trained particularly well by compound pressing exercises.

## Setting up
1. Use both hands to pick up one kettlebell by its horns (the two side handles) with the base of the weighted bell facing forward away from you. Stand upright with approximately a shoulder-width stance.
    1. Strive to keep your wrists fairly straight while setting up and performing the exercise. Firmly gripping the horns can help you do so, since the kettlebell can bend your wrists to the side of the weight unless you actively resist it. It is not inherently problematic for your wrists to bend to a degree during this exercise, but you should avoid letting your wrists bend to the extent that you experience any wrist discomfort.
    2. Your palms should be facing in toward each other.
2. Lift the kettlebell up in front of your chest with your elbows bent by curling the weight and using momentum from your lower body as needed.
    1. You can perform a cheat curl-like motion to move the kettlebell into position if it is too heavy to lift without momentum. To do so, first sit your buttocks back while allowing your knees to bend mildly. Then drive your hips forcefully forward while bending your elbows and mildly swinging them forward to lift the weight.
    2. The base of the weighted bell should now be facing toward you.
3. Press the kettlebell up overhead with both arms in a shoulder press motion until your arms are vertical.
    1. The base of the weighted bell should now be facing behind you as your hands are level with the bell.
    2. The back of your elbows should be pointing forward.
    3. Rather than being excessively arched, your lower back and neck should be near a neutral position along with your neck, like when you are normally standing upright and looking straight ahead.
## Exercise technique
1. Bend your elbows to lower the kettlebell behind your head in a controlled manner while keeping your elbows up.
    1. Essentially all the motion should occur from your forearms hinging at your elbows without any shoulder motion. You can think of your elbows as the center of an analog clock, while your forearms are the hands that rotate about these center elbows during this exercise.
    2. Predominantly keep your elbows tucked in as they are chiefly pointing forward rather than out to your side. However, you can allow your elbows to flare slightly out away from your sides if that feels natural and comfortable to you.
    3. As you keep your elbows up, your upper arms should remain in a vertical position by the sides of your head.
2. Continue lowering the kettlebell until you have fully bent your elbows or can lightly tap your upper back with the kettlebell.
    1. It is normal to be able to bend the elbows beyond 90 degrees during this exercise, but specifically how far you can bend your elbows may be limited by the flexibility of your long head of the triceps.
    2. While some lifters have the flexibility to reach their upper back with the kettlebell, wherever you feel a notable stretching sensation in your triceps can be an appropriate end range.
    3. While you do not have to perform the lowering phase with an extremely slow tempo, you should be actively controlling the weight the entire way.
3. Reverse the movement by straightening your elbows to lift the dumbbell overhead.
    1. You should finish with your elbows fully straightened.
    2. Continue keeping your wrists reasonably straight and your elbows up, as all the motion occurs from your elbows without moving your shoulders.
4. Alternate between steps 1-3 until you have completed your set.
5. After you complete the lifting phase of your last rep, lower the kettlebell toward your chest (like during the lowering phase of a shoulder press) before setting it down.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop the [triceps](../Muscles/Triceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88032be38d4f3e73c9e4c.md), including the [long head](../Muscles/Triceps%20Brachii%20Long%20Head%201905c6f170d880b1a0a7eda6c9b74382.md), which is not trained particularly well by pressing exercises.

## Setting up
1. Pick up a pair of dumbbells and sit down on a flat exercise bench or chair.
2. While holding the dumbbells, lean forward at your hips and position your forearms on top of your thighs with your palms facing down toward the floor and your wrists situated slightly in front of your knees.
3. Allow the force from the dumbbells to bend your wrists and bring your hands downward such that your palms are directed at an angle down and back toward you.
    1. In this position, the dumbbells should not be contacting your legs, so scoot your forearms forward if they are initially contacting your legs.
## Exercise technique
1. Lift the dumbbells upward by extending your wrists through their available range of motion while keeping your forearms resting on your thighs.
    1. All of the motion should be coming from your wrists as your hands move upward.
    2. About halfway through the lifting phase, your palms should be facing straight down toward the floor when your hands are aligned with your forearms.
    3. At the end of the lifting phase, when the dumbbells are fully raised, your palms should be angled forward.
    4. When performing this exercise appropriately, you should feel tension in the muscles on the top side of your forearms.
2. Reverse the motion by lowering the dumbbells in a controlled manner until you have returned to the starting position with your palms directed at an angle down and back toward you.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can effectively train the seven [wrist extensor muscles](../Muscles/Wrist%20extensors%202c35c6f170d8804ab377fe1e53371f25.md) on the side of your forearm opposite your palm.
1a15c6f170d880d7b8cbf608580aaa50:
## Setting up
1. Pick up one dumbbell and place it on the ground right next to the long side of a flat exercise bench (or similar object on which you can sit, such as a plyometric or a couch if training at home).
2. Sit down on the bench with your legs spread wide apart and the dumbbell in between your legs as your feet are on the floor.
3. Lean forward at your hips to grasp the dumbbell firmly with the side you are about to train.
    1. For additional stability, you can place your free hand on top of your thigh (on the same side as your free hand) and keep it there throughout your set.
    2. All the subsequent directions will apply to the side in which you are holding the dumbbell since that is the arm you will be training first.
4. Lean your torso slightly back toward an upright position until the dumbbell lifts off the ground with your elbow fully straightened.
5. Position the back of your elbow against the inside of your thigh while holding the dumbbell with an underhand grip, which will direct your palm to be angled forward and in toward your other side.
    1. In this starting position, your entire arm should be directed straight down toward the ground.
## Exercise technique
1. While keeping your elbow pinned against your inner thigh, curl the dumbbell upward in an arcing motion by bending your elbow until it is fully bent.
    1. While your one forearm moves through elbow motion, the rest of your body should remain stationary throughout your set.
2. After your elbow has fully bent, reverse the motion by lowering the dumbbell in a controlled manner until your elbow has returned to a fully straightened position with your forearm directed straight down toward the ground.
    1. Continue keeping your elbow braced against your inner thigh.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set and are ready to repeat the exercise with your other arm.
## Description
Like other curl variations, this exercise can effectively train your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md).
1a15c6f170d880da9085c9c6ed1ec342:
## Setting up
1. You can select either a fixed-weight EZ bar or an adjustable plate-loaded EZ bar, which are functionally interchangeable for this exercise.
2. While facing the middle of the bar, squat down or hinge at your hips with extended elbows.
    1. If the EZ bar is already positioned in an elevated rack at mid-thigh level or above, you naturally would not have to squat down or hinge at your hips before picking it up.
3. Grasp the bar with approximately a wider than shoulder width grip and a semi-underhand grip (AKA semi-neutral grip) such that your palms are directed at an angle that is facing forward and inward.
    1. With the zig-zag-like shape of the EZ bar, you may have to rotate it before an outside shoulder width semi-underhand grip is accessible on the bar.
4. While keeping your elbows extended, stand fully upright while gripping the bar.
## Exercise technique
1. Curl the bar upward by bending at your elbows while keeping your upper arms fixed at your sides (rather than allowing your upper arms to swing forward).
2. After your elbows have fully flexed, reverse the motion by lowering the bar in a controlled manner until your elbows have returned to an extended position.
    1. During the lowering phase, continue to keep your upper arms positioned by your sides.
3. Alternate between curling the bar upwards and lowering it down until you have completed your set.
## Description
Like other curl variations, this exercise can effectively train your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md).
1a15c6f170d880db8633e3bec8b7e8fe:
## Setting up
1. Adjust the height of the seat so that your upper arms can be parallel with the floor or a little lower while grasping the handles.
    1. After initially adjusting the seat height, spread your arms outward so that your hands are level with the handles.
    2. You may have to re-adjust the seat if your upper arms are not parallel with the floor or a little lower.
    3. Some people will find their shoulders feel more comfortable when the seat is set to a height that allows their hands to be a bit lower than their shoulders, compared to when their hands are completely level with their shoulders.
2. Adjust the pins above the handles to a position that allows you to grasp the handles with your hands as close as they can be to each other while your chest is facing the machine’s pad.
3. After sitting down with your chest against the pad, grasp the vertical handles with a neutral grip such that your palms face toward each other and slightly bend your elbows.
    1. Maintain the slight bend in your elbows throughout the set.
## Exercise technique
1. Spread the handles apart and backward until your arms and torso form a “T-shape.”
2. Reverse the motion by bringing the handles forward and toward each other until they have returned to their starting position.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop your [rear delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Posterior%20Head%201905c6f170d880a29e5ec26f4d257c01.md), which is assisted by your [traps](../Muscles/Trapezius%201b95c6f170d880bebf89c759b592e81f.md) and [rhomboids](../Muscles/Rhomboids%201b95c6f170d880c8a84de94f5232a509.md), along with your rotator cuff’s [infraspinatus](../Muscles/Infraspinatus%201905c6f170d88026aebcf3953e2e440f.md), [teres minor](../Muscles/Teres%20Minor%201905c6f170d88098824dc8136557c410.md), and [supraspinatus](../Muscles/Supraspinatus%201905c6f170d880efb440c1614caf1c97.md).
1a15c6f170d880dfacd1c620c1010d79:
## Setting up
1. Position yourself with your palms, knees, and toes on the ground as your elbows are straight, and your knees are bent (i.e., the quadruped position, which is also known as being “on all fours”).
    1. In this position, your elbows should be stacked underneath your shoulders with your arms pointing straight down toward the ground.
2. Situate your hands slightly outside shoulder width apart from each other, with your fingers spread somewhat apart from each other.
    1. Your middle fingers should be pointing slightly out to the sides or straight ahead, depending upon which hand position feels most comfortable and stable to you.
3. Straighten one knee to move your foot behind you, and position the bottom of its toes onto the ground before doing the same with your other leg.
4. Walk your feet forward while lifting your hips and angling your torso downward. Finish with your knees straight and your body as close to forming an inverted “V” shape (when viewed from the side) as your flexibility permits.
    1. How far you can walk your feet forward and consequently lift your hips up with straight knees can be determined by your hamstring flexibility.
    2. Based on your preference, you can situate your feet hip-width apart or closer together.
    3. Strive to keep your back flat and your neck near a neutral position, like when you are normally standing upright and looking straight ahead.
5. While bearing weight through the bases of your palms (i.e., heels of your hands) and the balls of your feet, lift your heels off the ground in a calf raise-like motion.
    1. Maintain this foot position throughout the set.
## Exercise technique
1. Brace your core by tensing the front and sides of your abdominals outward, like you would if you were bracing for someone to strike your stomach with a punch or forcible slap.
    1. Continue bracing your core throughout your set to help you keep your back flat.
2. While keeping your hips bent and high, lower your head toward the ground by bending your elbows in a controlled manner.
    1. Rather than keeping them completely tucked by your sides or fully flaring them out, allow your elbows to flare out mildly away from your sides to a degree that feels comfortable and natural to you.
    2. Avoid letting your hips drop down vertically closer to your chest, which would involve reducing the degree to which your hips are bent. As you bend your elbows, your hips will naturally descend as well, but they should lower at the same rate as your head and torso, while they all move together as one unit. This should result in your hips finishing at about the same height above your head at the bottom of the rep as at the top of the rep.
    3. Continue keeping your neck near a neutral position rather than meaningfully tilting your head up or down.
    4. You can finish the lowering phase once your head lightly taps the ground or just before this point.
    5. There is no need to perform this step extremely slowly, but you should avoid dropping down in an uncontrolled fashion.
3. Reverse the movement by pressing into the ground to lift your head, torso, and hips up in unison until you have fully straightened your elbows.
    1. Continue maintaining the same degree of bend in your hips with your knees still straightened.
    2. As a cue, you think about pushing the ground down and away from you.
4. Alternate between steps 2 and 3 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop your [front delts](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Anterior%20Head%201905c6f170d8805da59fc8f9dc0a59e4.md) while also training your [upper pec major,](../Muscles/Pectoralis%20Major%20(Clavicular%20Head%201905c6f170d880ef9b6bd48adbf440bd.md) [lateral delts](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Lateral%20Head%201905c6f170d8804b9b6ef12253eec774.md), [triceps](../Muscles/Triceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88032be38d4f3e73c9e4c.md), [traps](../Muscles/Trapezius%201b95c6f170d880bebf89c759b592e81f.md), [serratus anterior](../Muscles/Serratus%20Anterior%201955c6f170d880a8b8b9e712f2ec58e0.md), and [supraspinatus](../Muscles/Supraspinatus%201905c6f170d880efb440c1614caf1c97.md).

## Setting up
1. Pick up a pair of dumbbells and sit down on a bench with an upright posture and your feet flat on the floor while holding the dumbbells at your sides with extended elbows.
    1. You can opt to sit down on a flat bench without any back support or sit down on a seated bench with back support.
2. Direct your palms so that they are facing back behind you, which positions you with a reverse (AKA overhand) grip.
    1. Maintain this reverse grip on the dumbbells throughout the set.
## Exercise technique
1. Curl both dumbbells upward by bending at your elbows while keeping your upper arms fixed at your sides (rather than allowing your upper arms to swing forward).
2. After your elbows have fully flexed, reverse the motion by lowering the dumbbells in a controlled manner until your elbows have returned to an extended position.
    1. During the lowering phase, continue to keep your upper arms positioned by your sides.
3. Alternate between curling the dumbbells up and lowering them down until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can develop your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md), but it may train your biceps somewhat less effectively than a curl with an underhand or neutral grip.
1a15c6f170d880e39adec8726186fa3f:
## Setting up
1. Approach a step or a sturdy object that can function as a step. You should be by a surface (e.g., handrail, wall, power rack) where you can place one hand to assist with maintaining your balance while performing this exercise.
    1. Based on the equipment at your disposal, a variety of objects can serve as your step. Make sure the object can support your weight, will not move once you are on it, and allows you to lower your heels through your full range of motion during the exercise.
    2. As an alternative to a staircase’s bottom step, you may select a power rack’s bottom beam if the beam is sufficiently tall.
    3. Additionally, a calf raise block, aerobic step, deadlift block, or thick bumper plate can each be positioned near a wall or power rack for stability. Depending on your bodyweight, anchoring an aerobic step with weight on top of it may be required to prevent the step from tipping.
2. After placing your hand onto the nearby surface for balance assistance, stand with your heels on top of a step as the front half of your feet hang off the step.
    1. Once on the step, your knees should be straight throughout this exercise.
3. While keeping your heels on the step, allow your feet to point downward as the balls of your feet move toward the ground as low as your ankle mobility allows .
    1. After doing so, your toes should be situated closer to the ground than your heels.
## Exercise technique
1. While keeping your heels on the step, lift the rest of your feet upward away from the ground through your available ankle range of motion.
    1. At the end of the lifting phase, the balls of your feet should be approximately level with your heels or above them if you have normal ankle mobility.
    2. Motion should occur exclusively at your ankle as the rest of your body remains stationary.
    3. You will likely feel the muscles on the front of your shins engage while doing so.
    4. With the balls of your feet lifting up rather than your heels, this is the opposite movement of a calf raise.
2. Reverse the motion by lowering your feet in a controlled manner until you have returned to the starting position with your toes pointing down toward the ground.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can train the four muscle ankle dorsiflexor muscles on the front of your lower leg, the largest of which is the [tibialis anterior](../Muscles/Tibialis%20Anterior%201925c6f170d880f78c80c47a8fbb2627.md).

## Setting up
1. After adding weight plates to the machine’s weight sleeve, straddle the machine as you are facing toward the weights.
2. Place your feet onto the foot plates and your chest onto the chest pad such that your whole body is inclined forward.
    1. You will be most stable when the entirety of the soles of your feet are in contact with the foot plates.
3. Depending upon your height and leg lengths, you may want to bend your knees somewhat or keep them extended to determine where your torso is situated on the chest pad.
    1. How you position your knees will be based on what feels most comfortable and stable to you, but you can initially see how you feel when positioning your knees to allow the uppermost aspect of the chest pad to be approximately level with your collarbone.
    2. Individuals who have longer legs will typically feel more comfortable when using a somewhat more bent knee position, while those with shorter legs will typically feel more comfortable with extended knees.
4. After determining which degree of knee bend places you in a comfortable position, firmly grasp the parallel handles with a neutral grip such that your palms are directed in toward each other.
    1. Certain T-bar row machines have a pair of inner handles that are angled outward and backward (which allow you to use a semi-neutral grip) and outer handles directed straight out to the sides (which allow you to use an overhand grip) but lack parallel handles required to use a neutral grip.
    2. If your T-bar row machine does not have parallel handles, you can select the [chest-supported semi-neutral grip  machine T-bar row](Chest-supported%20semi-neutral%20grip%20T-bar%20row%201a15c6f170d8803bb4dbc83c2279dbcf.md) as an alternative.
5. Lift the bar up off the machine’s stopper, center the bar so that it no longer lies above the stopper, and lower it until your elbows are extended.
    1. In this bottom position, allow the weight to pull your shoulder blades apart from one another, which will likely prompt you to feel a stretching sensation in your upper back.
## Exercise technique
1. Pull the bar upward and back toward your torso by driving your elbows simultaneously upward and backward while progressively bending your elbows and pulling your shoulder blades together.
    1. Move your elbows through a path of motion that feels comfortable to you, which will typically involve keeping them tucked fairly close to your sides with this neutral grip rather than notably flaring your elbows away from your sides (which is typically more comfortable with a wider overhand grip).
    2. Keep your torso in contact with the chest pad throughout the set rather than arching your lower back to lift your chest up off the pad.
    3. Pull through your available range of motion, which will typically result in your elbows being level with your torso or slightly behind your torso at the end of the lifting phase.
    4. As a cue for training your upper back muscles, you can think about squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the pull as if you were trying to pinch a pencil with your shoulder blades.
2. Reverse the movement by lowering the bar in a controlled manner by allowing your elbows to move downward and forward until your elbows have finished extending and the bar has returned to the starting position.
    1. During the lowering phase, your shoulder blades will naturally move apart from one another, but you can exaggerate this motion by intentionally allowing the weight to pull them further apart than your resting position at the bottom, which will stretch your upper back muscles.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set and are ready to return the bar back onto the machine’s stopper.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop your [lats](../Muscles/Latissimus%20Dorsi%201905c6f170d880109e73f99ab91d4d47.md), [teres majores](../Muscles/Teres%20Major%201905c6f170d880dbba32f6bd22e3abe6.md), [rear delts](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Posterior%20Head%201905c6f170d880a29e5ec26f4d257c01.md), [traps](../Muscles/Trapezius%201b95c6f170d880bebf89c759b592e81f.md), and [rhomboids](../Muscles/Rhomboids%201b95c6f170d880c8a84de94f5232a509.md), which are assisted by your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md).

## Setting up
1. Pick up a pair of dumbbells, and stand upright in a near hip width stance with your arms hanging down by your sides as your elbows are straight.
## Exercise technique
1. Direct your palms forward to adopt an underhand grip.
2. Curl the dumbbells upward in an arcing manner by bending your elbows without rotating your palms.
    1. Keep your wrists straight, torso upright, and your elbows by your sides, rather than swinging your elbows forward through shoulder motion.
    2. While your forearms move through elbow joint motion, the rest of your body should remain stationary.
    3. Since you will maintain an underhand grip during this lifting phase, your palms should be facing upward when your forearms are parallel to the ground.
    4. At the top of the curl, your elbows should be fully bent with your forearms touching your biceps and your palms facing back toward your shoulders.
3. Rotate your palms forward away from you to adopt an overhand grip, which is also called a reverse grip.
4. While keeping your wrists straight, lower the dumbbells in a controlled manner by allowing your elbows to straighten progressively without rotating your palms.
    1. Since you will maintain a reverse grip during this lowering phase, your palms should be facing down when your forearms are parallel to the ground before facing backward once you have fully straightened your elbows.
    2. You do not have to perform an extremely slow lowering phase, but you should avoid letting gravity abruptly swing the dumbbells down.
5. Alternate between steps 1-4 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can develop your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md) while also training your [wrist extensor muscles](../Muscles/Wrist%20extensors%202c35c6f170d8804ab377fe1e53371f25.md) more effectively than most curl variations.

## Setting up
1. Connect an attachment with a straight bar shaft to the cable, select your weight with the loading pin, and sit down facing the cable station.
    1. You can use any attachment that allows you to hold it comfortably with an underhand grip with your hands approximately shoulder width apart.
    2. The most commonly available attachment appropriate for this exercise is a standard lat pulldown bar attachment, which has a straight shaft with mildly angled ends and may be found attached to a cable lat pulldown machine.
    3. You can readily perform this exercise with essentially the same technique whether you use a seated cable row machine or an adjustable cable station.
    4. If you use a seated cable row machine, you naturally will sit down on its seat, but if you are using an adjustable cable station, you will sit down on the ground after adjusting the cable to a height that is approximately level with your shoulders when seated on the floor with an upright torso.
2. Position your feet in contact with the machine’s foot plates or the base of the adjustable cable station.
    1. Allow your knees to bend to an angle that allows you to feel stable and comfortable, which can be a mild to moderately mild knee bend for many people.
    2. With greater knee bend, you will be able to sit closer toward the cable, so you can bend your knees further if you initially cannot reach the bar when leaning forward by bending at your hip
3. Lean forward at your hips until you are able to grasp the bar firmly with straight elbows. Grasp it with a near shoulder-width underhand grip, such that your palms face upward.
4. While holding the bar with straight elbows, lean your torso backward at your hips until you are sitting with an upright torso.
    1. When seated upright, you should feel tension from the cable, so if the cable is still slack, you can extend your knees to scoot yourself backward until the machine’s weight stack separates and you feel the resistance.
## Exercise technique
1. Pull the bar back toward your torso by driving your elbows backward while simultaneously bending them and pulling your shoulder blades together.
    1. Move your elbows through a path of motion that feels comfortable to you, which will typically involve keeping them tucked fairly close to your sides with this underhand grip rather than notably flaring your elbows away from your sides (which is typically more comfortable with a wider overhand grip).
    2. Movement should occur at your shoulders, shoulder blades, and elbows, but your knees, hips, and lower back should remain nearly stationary in a stable position throughout the set.
    3. Pull through your available range of motion or until the bar is directly in front of your torso, which will typically result in your elbows being level with your torso or slightly behind your torso at the end of the lifting phase.
    4. As a cue for training your upper back muscles, you can think about squeezing your shoulder blades together at the end of the pull as if you were trying to pinch a pencil with your shoulder blades.
2. Reverse the movement by allowing your elbows to move forward in a controlled manner as they progressively straighten to move the bar forward.
    1. Finish with your arms fully outstretched in front of you.
    2. Your shoulder blades will naturally move apart, but you can exaggerate this motion by intentionally allowing the weight to pull them further apart than your resting position at the end, without rounding your lower back. This will stretch your upper back muscles and may help you to train them more effectively.
    3. While you do not have to perform this step extremely slowly, you should avoid letting the weight abruptly yank your arms forward in an uncontrolled fashion.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This row primarily trains your [lat](../Muscles/Latissimus%20Dorsi%201905c6f170d880109e73f99ab91d4d47.md), [teres major](../Muscles/Teres%20Major%201905c6f170d880dbba32f6bd22e3abe6.md), [rear delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Posterior%20Head%201905c6f170d880a29e5ec26f4d257c01.md), [traps](../Muscles/Trapezius%201b95c6f170d880bebf89c759b592e81f.md), and [rhomboids](../Muscles/Rhomboids%201b95c6f170d880c8a84de94f5232a509.md), which are assisted by your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md).

## Setting up
1. Adjust a cable station’s pulley to near waist height, connect a rope attachment to the cable, and select your desired weight with the loading pin.
2. Grasp the ends of the rope with a neutral grip such that your palms are facing in toward each other.
    1. Your little fingers and the adjacent aspects of your hands should be in contact with the flat surfaces of the attachment’s rubber stoppers as your thumbs wrap over the outside of your other fingers.
3. Pivot your body away from the pulley while simultaneously repositioning your arms such that your upper arms are raised up high with your elbows close to being fully bent as the cable is applying a downward force to the rope behind your head.
    1. To get into position with a heavier load, you can lunge down into a half-kneeling position during this step before standing upright once the rope is behind your head.
    2. The arm movement performed during this step is akin to a controlled swinging-like motion.
    3. How high you can raise your upper arms is influenced by your mobility.
4. Take a step forward, and slightly lean your torso forward by hinging at your hips while standing in a staggered stance with one foot in front of the other.
    1. In this position, you should feel tension from the cable, so if that is not the case, you should step further forward until you feel tension from the cable.
    2. Maintain this position throughout your set.
## Exercise technique
1. While keeping your elbows high, press the rope upward by extending your elbows until they are straightened.
    1. At the end of this motion, the rope should be situated above your head.
    2. If the cable contacts the back of your head during this motion, you can tuck your chin closer to your chest for clearance.
2. Reverse the motion by bending your elbows through your available range of motion to lower the rope in a controlled manner until you have returned to the starting position.
    1. Strive to have your elbows as close to fully bent as you can by the time you have finished this motion.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop the [triceps](../Muscles/Triceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88032be38d4f3e73c9e4c.md), including the [long head](../Muscles/Triceps%20Brachii%20Long%20Head%201905c6f170d880b1a0a7eda6c9b74382.md), which is not trained particularly well by compound pressing exercises.

## Setting up
1. Adjust the height of the Roman chair’s pad to a level that positions its top slightly below the top of your hip bones when you set up with your feet on the foot plate.
    1. The appropriate position should allow you to move your lower back freely while supporting your hips.
    2. While it can effectively stabilize your hips, positioning the top of the pad higher than the top of your hip bones can restrict your lower back’s motion, which is suboptimal for training lower back muscles.
    3. If the top of the pad is positioned much lower than the top of the hip bones (rather than only slightly lower), the hips will not be stabilized as well, which can make it more challenging to emphasize training your back muscles.
    4. Since a sweet spot exists, some trial and error may be needed to find your ideal pad position.
2. While placing your hands onto the handles for balance support, step onto the foot plate one leg at a time. Place the back of your heels against the back of the foot plate, as your soles fully contact the foot plate.
    1. Based on your preference, you can point your toes straight forward, or you can rotate them to point inward. Pointing the toes inward may help some people limit the hip muscle engagement while focusing on the back muscles.
    2. Situating your feet approximately hip width to shoulder apart from each other will result in a viable stance width, but how wide of a stance you can use will be influenced by the width of your Roman chair’s foot plate.
    3. Your knees should be straight after you have finished setting your feet on the foot plate.
3. Check to make sure that the pad is positioned as described by step 1, and readjust the pad height if warranted before resuming your setup.
4. Cross your arms across your chest with bent elbows to position each hand on the front of the opposite shoulder.
    1. Maintain this arm position throughout your set.
    2. Your back and neck should be near a neutral position, like when you are normally standing upright and looking straight ahead.
## Exercise technique
1. While keeping your back mostly flat, hinge at your hips through the range of motion that is permitted by the pad and your flexibility.
    1. Only during this step are you intentionally moving about your hips to assume the starting position.
    2. Once you have reached the end range of your hip motion, it will be easier to emphasize back motion.
    3. Depending on specifically where you have the pad positioned, the pad may limit how far you can hinge, or your hamstring flexibility may limit it.
2. Round your entire back in a slow and controlled curling manner through the full range of motion that is comfortable for you.
    1. The degree to which you can round your back will be affected by your spinal mobility.
    2. It is normal to feel a stretching sensation in your back muscles in the bottom position, but you should not feel any discomfort at the end range. Only round your back as far as is comfortable.
    3. Rather than moving only one part of your back, strive to round your lower, middle, and upper back simultaneously.
    4. As a cue, you can think about bringing the bottom of your ribs toward the top of your hip bones.
3. Reverse the movement by extending (straightening) your back in a controlled manner without hinging at your hips.
    1. At the end of the lifting phase, your back should be near a neutral position, which involves your lower back being mildly arched.
    2. For increasing the size and strength of your back muscles, there is no need to arch your back maximally like you would during a cobra yoga pose.
    3. Keep your glutes relaxed to the best of your ability as you focus on moving your spine rather than your hips.
    4. You should feel your spinal extensor muscles, which run along each side of the spine, contract to extend your back.
4. Alternate between steps 2 and 3 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can dynamically train the [erector spinae](../Muscles/Thoracolumbar%20Erector%20Spinae%201bb5c6f170d880a7a719e8f6d05d00a8.md) and [deep intrinsic spinal extensor muscles](../Muscles/Deep%20Intrinsic%20Thoracolumbar%20Extensors%201bb5c6f170d880f58501d5f27212caed.md) that run along the length of your entire back.

## Setting up
1. Add weight plates of your desired load to a barbell situated on the ground, and stand close in front of the middle of the bar with approximately a hip-width stance.
    1. You can set up with the bar approximately over the middle of your feet, which should situate the bar close to one inch (2.5cm) away from most individuals’ shins while initially standing upright.
    2. The diameter of the weight plates you add to the bar will determine how high the bar lies above the ground, which consequently affects your range of motion. If you do not have a pair of full-diameter plates (like 45lb (20kg) plates or any bumper plates) on the bar, this exercise can functionally serve as a [deficit Pendlay row](Deficit%20Pendlay%20row%202a05c6f170d88091a3e9e33a249035ae.md) with a greater range of motion than what is typical for a standard Pendlay row. Rowing the bar from a lower than standard height is not recommended for individuals who lack the flexibility to reach the bar with a flat lower back position. If you have to round your lower back meaningfully to reach the bar, you can elevate the plates on top of aerobic steps, deadlift blocks, or stacks of full-diameter weight plates, like you could do when setting up for a block pull.
2. With your arms pointing straight down toward the ground, sit your hips backward while bending your knees until your hands are level with the bar. Keep your lower back flat and chest up rather than rounding your back.
    1. More motion should come from your hips than your knees as you descend, and your knees should not track particularly far forward, but you can allow your knees to shift mildly forward rather than maintaining completely vertical shins.
    2. As a cue for hinging at your hips, you can think about closing a car door with your buttocks while your hands are carrying something. Once you fully sit back and feel a stretching sensation in your hamstrings, you can bend your knees further to reach the bar.
    3. Throughout the exercise, keep your neck near a neutral position, like when you are normally looking straight ahead while standing upright.
3. With straight elbows, firmly grasp the bar with a slightly outside shoulder-width overhand grip, such that your palms are facing backward.
    1. For the most stable grip, wrap your fingers around the bar with the bar pressed into where the bases of your fingers meet the palm side of your knuckles.
    2. If you situate the bar closer toward the middle of your palms (rather than the bases of your fingers), the bar can slide down your hand while holding it, which pulls on your hand skin in an uncomfortable manner that increases the risk of tearing a callus.
## Exercise technique
1. Brace your core by tensing the front and sides of your abdominals outward, like you would if you were bracing for someone to strike your stomach with a punch or forcible slap.
    1. For additional stability, you can initially take a deep “belly breath” (AKA diaphragmatic breath) that expands the front and sides of your abdominals outward. Avoid taking a “chest breath” that predominantly lifts your chest upward and leaves your abdominals relaxed or simply sucking your belly button inward.
    2. Continue bracing your core from this point onward to help you maintain a rigid back position.
2. Explosively pull the bar up toward your upper abdomen by driving your elbows simultaneously backward and upward as you pull your shoulder blades back together.
    1. Keep your torso in a hinged position as you maintain the same angle of bend in your hips and knees throughout your set. All the movement should occur from motion at your shoulders, shoulder blades, and elbows while your lower body remains stationary.
    2. Continue keeping your core braced, lower back flat, and chest up.
    3. Allow your elbows naturally to flare out away from your sides in a manner that feels comfortable to you, which may result in your upper arms forming near 45-degree angles with your torso toward the end of the lifting phase.
    4. You can aim to row the bar until it touches near your upper abdomen or is close to doing so, which will result in your elbows being behind your torso (or at least aligned with your torso) at the end of the lifting phase.
3. Reverse the movement by lowering the bar until it is fully resting on the ground.
    1. During the lowering phase, your shoulder blades will naturally move apart from one another, and your elbows will move downward and forward until your arms are directed down toward the ground with straight elbows.
    2. Continue maintaining the same degree of forward torso lean with your chest up and lower back flat.
    3. The lowering phase of the Pendlay row is typically performed with a very quick tempo, but you can alternatively lower the bar in a more controlled manner if you wish to do so.
4. Allow the weight to come to a dead stop on the ground for a moment (rather than using momentum) before continuing to alternate between steps 2 and 3 until you have completed your set.
    1. You will be able to brace most effectively when you breathe in between reps while the weight is resting on the ground. After taking a breath, make sure to resume bracing your core prior to initiating the next rep.
## Description
While statically training your [erector spinae](../Muscles/Thoracolumbar%20Erector%20Spinae%201bb5c6f170d880a7a719e8f6d05d00a8.md), this exercise can effectively develop your [lats](../Muscles/Latissimus%20Dorsi%201905c6f170d880109e73f99ab91d4d47.md), [teres majores](../Muscles/Teres%20Major%201905c6f170d880dbba32f6bd22e3abe6.md), [rear delts](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Posterior%20Head%201905c6f170d880a29e5ec26f4d257c01.md), [traps](../Muscles/Trapezius%201b95c6f170d880bebf89c759b592e81f.md), and [rhomboids](../Muscles/Rhomboids%201b95c6f170d880c8a84de94f5232a509.md).

## Setting up
1. Symmetrically elevate each end of a mobile flat bench on top of sturdy objects like aerobic steps with risers, bumper plates, plyometric boxes, or deadlift blocks. Elevate it to the level where you can lie face-down on the bench without your hands contacting the ground when your arms are hanging down on each side of the bench.
    1. If you have access to one, you can alternatively use a specific seal row bench, which is already elevated, but this is not a particularly common type of equipment.
    2. When elevating the bench, make sure that each base is level and that you stack the bench onto only objects that are able to handle the combined weight of you, your dumbbells, and the bench.
    3. Setting up this exercise can take more time than most row variations, and you can train your back muscles in a very similar manner with a shorter setup if you perform the “[low incline neutral grip chest-supported dumbbell row](Chest-supported%20elbows-in%20dumbbell%20row%201a15c6f170d8802d969ae139f42062fa.md)” from this database.
2. Place a pair of dumbbells on an elevated surface near the head of your bench in a position where you can grasp them while lying down on the bench.
    1. If there is sufficient space, you would ideally place the dumbbells onto the object you used to elevate the bench.
    2. Alternatively, you can situate the dumbbells on top of bumper plates (or something similar) that you place near the head of the bench in a position you can grasp while lying on the bench, but would not restrict your rowing motion.
    3. With a sufficiently low setup, you also may be able to position the dumbbells on the floor underneath the bench and still be able to pick them up, but this would not be feasible with a more elevated setup.
3. Lie down with the front of your torso and thighs flat on the bench in a position that allows your arms to hang straight down toward the floor without being obstructed by the objects you used to elevate the bench.
    1. Based on your preference, you can either keep your knees extended or bent.
    2. Position your head in a comfortable position, such as tucking your chin and lifting your head slightly up to keep your face off the bench.
4. Firmly grasp each dumbbell, and angle your palms in toward each other while your arms hang down with straight elbows.
    1. The bony bump on the back of each elbow should be pointing backward, which is the direction in which you will row.
    2. Maintain this neutral grip throughout your set.
    3. To be able to row through a full range of motion, the dumbbells should not be in contact with anything in this position.
5. Grasp each dumbbell, position your arms so that they are perpendicular to the ground with extended elbows, and direct your palms in toward each other to utilize a neutral grip.
    1. To be able to row through a full range of motion, the dumbbells should not be in contact with anything in this position.
## Exercise technique
1. Drive your elbows backward and upward in an arcing motion to pull the dumbbells toward your hip. Simultaneously pull your shoulder blades back together.
    1. Keep your elbows tucked by your sides, rather than flaring them outward.
    2. Progressively bend your elbows to the extent that keeps your forearms close to being perpendicular to the ground throughout the row.
    3. Keep your torso in contact with the bench throughout the set rather than arching your lower back to lift your chest up off the bench.
    4. Pull through your full range of motion, which will typically result in your elbows being level with your torso or slightly behind your torso at the end of the lifting phase.
    5. While performing this arcing motion, the dumbbells should not move straight upward in a vertical path.
    6. As a cue for training your upper back muscles, you can think about squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the pull as if you were trying to pinch a pencil with your shoulder blades.
2. Reverse the movement by lowering the dumbbells in a controlled arcing forward motion until your arms are directed down toward the ground with straight elbows.
    1. Allow the weights to pull your shoulder blades apart to stretch your upper back muscles.
    2. You do not have to perform an extremely slow lowering phase, but you should actively control the entire descent rather than letting the weights rapidly pull your arms down.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set and are ready to set the dumbbells back down.
## Description
While also training your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md), this row can effectively develop your [lat](../Muscles/Latissimus%20Dorsi%201905c6f170d880109e73f99ab91d4d47.md), [teres major](../Muscles/Teres%20Major%201905c6f170d880dbba32f6bd22e3abe6.md), [rear delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Posterior%20Head%201905c6f170d880a29e5ec26f4d257c01.md), [traps](../Muscles/Trapezius%201b95c6f170d880bebf89c759b592e81f.md), and [rhomboids](../Muscles/Rhomboids%201b95c6f170d880c8a84de94f5232a509.md).

## Setting up
1. Prepare the barbell with your desired load by adding weight plates to it or leaving the barbell unloaded, which is recommended if performing this exercise for the first time.
    1. If you have access to one, you can also use a fixed-weight straight barbell, which may be lighter than a typical 20kg (44lb) barbell that has sleeves on which to add weight plates.
2. Stand close in front of the middle of the bar with a hip-width stance and straight elbows before hinging at your hips while bending your knees until your hands are level with the bar.
    1. Keep your lower back near flat, rather than meaningfully rounding it while doing so.
3. Firmly grasp the bar with a shoulder-width underhand grip such that your palms are facing forward away from you.
4. By extending (straightening) your hips and knees, stand upright with the bar while continuing to keep your elbows straight.
    1. Once upright, the bar should be directly in front of your thighs.
    2. Maintain this upright position with straight elbows throughout your set.
## Exercise technique
1. Lift the bar upward by curling your wrists through their available range of motion while keeping your arms stationary.
    1. All motion should come from your wrists while you keep the rest of your body stationary.
    2. Your palms should be angled upward once you have fully curled your wrists.
    3. When performing this exercise appropriately, you should feel tension in the muscles on the palm side of your forearms.
2. Reverse the motion by lowering the bar in a controlled manner until you have returned to the starting position with your palms directed forward away from you.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can effectively train the six [wrist flexor muscles](../Muscles/Wrist%20flexor%20muscles%202c85c6f170d880a49749f7d7a9f307c8.md) on the palm side of your forearm.

## Setting up
1. Pick up a pair of dumbbells and stand upright with approximately a shoulder width stance while holding the dumbbells at your sides with extended elbows.
## Exercise technique
1. Raise your heels into the air through the available range of motion of your ankles while keeping your knees straight and your trunk upright.
2. In a controlled manner, allow your heels to descend toward the ground while continuing to keep your knees straight.
3. After your heels touch the ground, alternate between raising and lowering your heels until you have completed your set.

## Setting up
1. Prepare the barbell with your desired load by adding weight plates to it or leaving the barbell unloaded, which is recommended if performing this exercise for the first time.
    1. You can initially set the bar up on the floor or from an elevated position, such as from a power rack.
2. While facing the middle of the bar, squat down or hinge at your hips with extended elbows.
3. Grasp the bar with approximately a shoulder width grip and an underhand grip such that your palms are directed forward.
4. While keeping your elbows extended, stand upright while gripping the bar.
## Exercise technique
1. Curl the bar upward by bending at your elbows while keeping your upper arms fixed at your sides (rather than allowing your upper arms to swing forward).
2. After your elbows have fully flexed, reverse the motion by lowering the bar in a controlled manner until your elbows have returned to an extended position.
    1. During the lowering phase, continue to keep your upper arms positioned by your sides.
3. Alternate between curling the bar up and lowering it down until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise is a time-tested means of effectively training the [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md).

## Setting up
1. At a dual cable station, adjust each cable to a height approximately level with your shoulders or slightly above them, clip in a D-handle attachment, and select your desired weight with the loading pin.
2. After standing centered between the cables with your sides facing the cable stacks, take a step backward, raise your arms in front of you until they are approximately parallel to the ground, and side-step toward one cable.
3. Reach across your body with your arm that is opposite to the cable to grasp its handle as your palm is facing the cable stack, before side-stepping toward the other cable and grasping its handle with your free hand.
4. Return to being centered between the cables with your arms crossed in front of your torso, with slightly bent elbows, as the cable stacks are situated a little in front of you.
    1. In this position, your arms should resemble an “X-shape” with each other.
    2. Maintain slightly bent elbows throughout your set.
## Exercise technique
1. Pull the handles out and away from each other as you move your arms backward until they form a “T-shape” with your torso.
2. Reverse the motion by bringing the handles inward and toward each other in a controlled manner until they have crossed and returned to their starting position.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop your [rear delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Posterior%20Head%201905c6f170d880a29e5ec26f4d257c01.md), which is assisted by your [traps](../Muscles/Trapezius%201b95c6f170d880bebf89c759b592e81f.md) and [rhomboids](../Muscles/Rhomboids%201b95c6f170d880c8a84de94f5232a509.md), along with your rotator cuff’s [infraspinatus](../Muscles/Infraspinatus%201905c6f170d88026aebcf3953e2e440f.md), [teres minor](../Muscles/Teres%20Minor%201905c6f170d88098824dc8136557c410.md), and [supraspinatus](../Muscles/Supraspinatus%201905c6f170d880efb440c1614caf1c97.md).

## Setting up
1. Pick up a kettlebell with one hand, carry it over to a flat bench, and position yourself near the base of the bench and directly to its side with your side that is holding the kettlebell farther away from the bench.
    1. If you have to carry the kettlebell a meaningful distance before reaching your bench and your grip is somewhat fatigued, you can place the kettlebell on the bench before picking it up with your opposite hand to start your set with the side that does not have a fatigued grip.
2. Sit your buttocks back to hinge at your hips, reach out with your free arm to place its hand on the bench with a straight elbow, and place your knee (on the side not holding the kettlebell) onto the bench.
    1. In this position, your torso should now be reasonably close to being parallel to the ground, and your lower back should be flat rather than being meaningfully rounded.
    2. While setting up, keep your elbow straight on the side holding the kettlebell and allow that arm to hang down toward the ground with your shoulder blade naturally pulled forward toward the ground from the weight.
    3. Based on your comfort and preference, you can place the open palm of your free hand onto the bench, or you can make a fist and place your knuckles onto the bench.
    4. Your foot on the side of the kettlebell should remain firmly in contact with the floor and be sufficiently far behind the kettlebell that your leg does not restrict your row. If you initially do not feel well-balanced, you can try positioning this foot somewhat further out to the side to widen your base of support.
3. Direct your palm so that it is facing in toward the opposite side of your body, and maintain this neutral grip position throughout your set.
    1. The bony bump on the back of your elbow should be directed backward, which is the direction you will row.
## Exercise technique
1. Brace your core by tensing the front and sides of your abdominals outward, like you would if you were bracing for someone to strike your stomach with a punch or forcible slap.
    1. Continue bracing your core from this point onward.
2. Drive your elbow backward and upward in an arcing motion to pull the kettlebell toward your hip. Simultaneously pull your shoulder blade backward, and keep your elbow tucked by your side rather than flaring it outward.
    1. When allowing your elbow to bend naturally, your forearm should remain fairly close to being perpendicular to the ground throughout the row.
    2. At the top of the row, your elbow should be aligned with your torso or slightly behind your torso.
    3. Keep your torso in a mostly fixed position with your chest facing a similar direction throughout this movement. A mild degree of torso rotation is not problematic, but avoid letting it become excessive and turning the exercise into a cheat row.
    4. While performing this arcing motion, the kettlebell should not move straight upward in a vertical path.
3. Reverse the movement by lowering the kettlebell in a controlled arcing motion until your arm is directed down toward the ground with your elbow straightened.
    1. Allow the weight to pull your shoulder blade forward, which will stretch your upper back muscles and result in your working side’s shoulder being mildly closer to the ground than your other side’s shoulder at the bottom of the row.
    2. You do not have to perform an extremely slow lowering phase, but you should actively control the entire descent rather than letting the weight rapidly pull your arm down.
4. Alternate between steps 2 and 3 until you have completed your set and are ready to repeat the exercise with your other side.
## Description
This exercise can effectively train much of the musculature constituting your middle and upper back, including your [lat](../Muscles/Latissimus%20Dorsi%201905c6f170d880109e73f99ab91d4d47.md), [teres major](../Muscles/Teres%20Major%201905c6f170d880dbba32f6bd22e3abe6.md), [rear delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Posterior%20Head%201905c6f170d880a29e5ec26f4d257c01.md), [traps](../Muscles/Trapezius%201b95c6f170d880bebf89c759b592e81f.md), and [rhomboids](../Muscles/Rhomboids%201b95c6f170d880c8a84de94f5232a509.md).

## Setting up
1. Pick up a pair of dumbbells and stand upright with approximately a shoulder width stance while holding the dumbbells at your sides with extended elbows.
2. Direct your palms so that they are facing forward.
    1. Maintain this underhand grip on the dumbbells throughout the set.
## Exercise technique
1. Curl both dumbbells upward by bending at your elbows while keeping your upper arms fixed at your sides (rather than allowing your upper arms to swing forward).
2. After your elbows have fully flexed, reverse the motion by lowering the dumbbells in a controlled manner until your elbows have returned to an extended position.
    1. During the lowering phase, continue to keep your upper arms positioned by your sides.
3. Alternate between curling the dumbbells up and lowering them down until you have completed your set.
## Description
Like other curl variations, this exercise can effectively train your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md).
