## Setting up
1. Position an adjustable cable station’s pulley to its highest setting, or approach a cable lat pulldown machine.
    1. Either type of equipment can be used interchangeably for this exercise.
2. Select your desired weight with the loading pin, and connect a rope attachment to the cable.
3. While facing the cable station, reach up and firmly grasp the ends of the rope with straight elbows while keeping your wrists fairly straight.
    1. You can point your palms in toward each other and grasp each end of the rope with your little fingers and the adjacent aspects of your hands contacting the flat surfaces of the attachment’s rubber stoppers. Simultaneously wrap your thumbs over the outside of your other fingers for a stable grip.
4. While keeping your arms outstretched with straight elbows in line with the cable, walk backward until you feel tension from the cable as the weight stack separates.
5. Sit your buttocks back to hinge at your hips and moderately incline your torso while keeping your arms in line with the cable and your back flat.
    1. The appropriate degree of torso incline should allow you to draw a mostly straight line from your arms through your shoulders to your hips when viewed from the side. From this position, the cable’s resistance should situate your arms fully overhead relative to what your shoulder mobility comfortably permits.
    2. As a cue for hinging at your hips, you can think about closing a car door with your buttocks while your hands are carrying something.
## Exercise technique
1. While keeping your elbows straightened and your torso inclined, sweep your arms down and back toward your sides in an arcing motion until your hands are right by your thighs.
    1. During the initial half of this movement, you can focus on driving down, while you can focus on pulling back during the latter half of this movement.
    2. As your arms move through motion at your shoulders, the rest of your body should be stationary.
2. Reverse the movement by allowing your arms to sweep forward and upward in a controlled arcing manner until you have returned to the starting position with your arms fully overhead in line with the cable.
    1. Continue keeping your elbows straightened and your torso inclined.
    2. While you do not have to reverse the movement with an extremely slow tempo, you should avoid letting the cable abruptly swing your arms upward in an uncontrolled fashion.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
    1. After your last rep, you can stand upright and walk forward to return the cable to its initial position.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop your [lats](../Muscles/Latissimus%20Dorsi%201905c6f170d880109e73f99ab91d4d47.md), [teres major](../Muscles/Teres%20Major%201905c6f170d880dbba32f6bd22e3abe6.md), and [rear delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Posterior%20Head%201905c6f170d880a29e5ec26f4d257c01.md), which are assisted by the [lowest portion of your pec major](../Muscles/Pectoralis%20Major%20Sternocostal%20Head%201905c6f170d8807d8e58cc809442a60b.md) and the [long head of your triceps](../Muscles/Triceps%20Brachii%20Long%20Head%201905c6f170d880b1a0a7eda6c9b74382.md) in the overhead position of each rep.

## Exercise technique
1. Take a deep breath, and then fully exhale until you feel that you have released all the air you can.

3. Statically hold this position for your target duration (e.g., 10-15 seconds) before inhaling and relaxing your abdomen.

## Setting up
1. Position a seated exercise bench (or an adjustable bench positioned fully upright) centered in front of two pulleys from a dual cable station.
    1. Place the bench far enough in front of the pulleys that the cables will be able to provide resistance to you when your arms are fully spread apart in the starting position.
2. Adjust each pulley to be near the height of your lower chest when you are seated on the bench.
    1. If you are using a machine (like the Freemotion dual cable cross) that has its pulleys connected to adjustable arms that can be swiveled forward or backward, you can set the arms so that their ends are somewhat less than the length of your wingspan apart from each other. Ideally, the ends of the lever arms can be situated just close enough together that you can grasp both handles at the same time rather than having to grasp one cable and then step over to the other cable to reach it.
3. Connect a D-handle attachment to each cable, and select your weight with the loading pin at each weight stack.
4. After standing with one pulley by your side while facing forward toward the bench, lunge down to assume a half-kneeling position.
5. With your hand that is closer to the pulley, grasp the handle with your elbow fully bent, palm angled inward and forward, and upper arm by your side. If the other pulley is close enough for you to do so, grasp its handle the same way.
    1. This arm position should resemble the starting position of a neutral grip dumbbell overhead press.
6. Stand upright while maintaining the arm position you just adopted. If the pulleys were too far apart for you to grasp both handles during the last step, stand upright, and step over to the other pulley to lunge down and grasp its handle in the same manner you just did before standing upright again.
7. Walk forward on one side of the bench until you can straddle the bench and sit down with your back snugly against the back pad.
    1. Keep your elbows bent with the handles close to you while walking forward against the cables’ resistance.
    2. Place your feet flat on the floor or against the foot bar if your seated bench has a foot bar.
8. Pull your shoulder blades back together with your chest up to assume a “proud chest” posture.
9. Flare your elbows out away from your sides to chest height and point them toward the pulleys. Simultaneously, allow the cables to pull your elbows behind your torso through the full range of motion your shoulder mobility comfortably permits.
    1. You should now look like you are in the starting position of a seated cable chest press.
10. Point your palms in toward each other before letting your elbows straighten until they are only mildly bent.
    1. Once your elbows are mildly bent, your palms should be pointing forward.
## Exercise technique
1. Sweep your arms forward and in toward each other in an arcing manner while keeping your elbows mildly bent.
    1. You should finish with your hands about to touch each other in front of your chest.
    2. The wide arcing motion should resemble hugging a thick barrel, as all the motion comes from your shoulders while you keep the rest of your body stationary throughout the set.
    3. As your hands approach each other, it is natural for your shoulder blades to move mildly forward, but you should avoid letting your shoulders round forward into a slouched posture.
2. Reverse the movement by allowing your arms to spread apart from each other in a controlled manner as they arc backward through the full range of motion your shoulder mobility comfortably permits.
    1. You should finish in a “proud chest” posture with your chest up and shoulder blades pulled back.
    2. It is normal to feel a stretching sensation in your chest and/or the front of your shoulders with your arms fully spread apart, but you should not experience any shoulder discomfort.
    3. Continue keeping your elbows only mildly bent as avoid bending your elbows any further and turning this exercise into a chest press.
    4. While you do not have to perform this step extremely slowly, avoid letting the cables abruptly swing your arms apart in an uncontrolled fashion.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
    1. After your last rep, bend your elbows to bring the handles in front of your shoulders to return to the position you adopted when initially sitting down. Then stand up, step to one side of the bench, and walk backward while keeping your arms close to your torso before returning the cables to their starting position.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop all regions of your [pec major](../Muscles/Pectoralis%20Major%201b95c6f170d880539f8ee236e09d4728.md) while also meaningfully training your [front delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Anterior%20Head%201905c6f170d8805da59fc8f9dc0a59e4.md) and [coracobrachialis](../Muscles/Coracobrachialis%201905c6f170d880f78a01c57799591868.md).

## Setting up
1. Select your weight with the machine’s loading pin, and adjust the seat to a height that allows your chest to rest comfortably against the chest pad.
    1. As a starting point, you can set the seat to a height that situates the horizontal handles level with the middle of your chest when you are seated. From this point, you can adjust the seat height based on what feels best to you with the specific machine model you are using.
2. If your machine has an adjustable chest pad, set it to a position that allows you to grasp the horizontal handles when your arms are fully outstretched forward in front of you with straight elbows.
    1. To be able to row through your full range of motion, you should ideally situate the chest pad far enough back that you have to push your shoulder blades forward and apart to grasp the handles with fully straightened elbows.
3. Sit down with your chest resting snugly against the chest pad and your feet flat on the floor.
4. Reach forward to grasp the horizontally directed handles firmly with your palms facing down (i.e., an overhand grip) and your hands clearly outside shoulder width.
    1. The appropriate grip width for this upper-back focused variation should naturally let your elbows flare prominently out away from your sides. At the end of your row, this should result in your upper arms being closer to forming a “T-shape” with your torso when viewed from behind, rather than being closer to being tucked by your sides (which can naturally occur with a closer grip).
    2. To find a viable wide grip based on your typical grip, you can place your index fingers on the handles where you would otherwise place your little fingers when performing your standard overhand grip machine row.
    3. If your machine does not have an adjustable chest pad and the handles are far enough from you to make it difficult to grasp both of them simultaneously, it may be easier for you to grasp one handle at a time.
## Exercise technique
1. Pull the handles back toward you by driving your elbows backward and outward while bending them. Simultaneously pull your shoulder blades back together.
    1. Rather than trying to keep them tucked close to your sides, allow your elbows to flare out meaningfully away from your sides to a degree that feels natural and comfortable to you.
    2. Keep your chest in contact with the chest pad throughout the set.
    3. Pull through your full range of motion, which will typically result in your elbows being level with your torso or slightly behind your torso at the end of the lifting phase.
    4. As a cue for training your upper back muscles, you can think about squeezing your shoulder blades together at the end of the pull as if you were trying to pinch a pencil with your shoulder blades.
2. Reverse the movement by allowing your elbows to move forward in a controlled manner as they progressively straighten until your arms are fully outstretched in front of you.
    1. Your shoulder blades will naturally move apart from one another, but you can exaggerate this motion by intentionally allowing the weight to pull them further apart than your resting position at the end, which will stretch your upper back muscles.
    2. While you do not have to perform this step extremely slowly, you should avoid letting the weight abruptly yank your arms forward in an uncontrolled fashion.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This row can effectively develop your [traps](../Muscles/Trapezius%201b95c6f170d880bebf89c759b592e81f.md), [rhomboids](../Muscles/Rhomboids%201b95c6f170d880c8a84de94f5232a509.md), and [rear delts](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Posterior%20Head%201905c6f170d880a29e5ec26f4d257c01.md) while also training your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md), and three [rotator cuff](../Muscles/Rotator%20Cuff%201b95c6f170d880b3b0d8eab69c3a7683.md) muscles.

## Setting up
1. Lie down on your back with your knees bent to about 90 degrees.
    1. For comfort, you optionally can lie down on an exercise mat.
2. With straight elbows, raise both arms straight up toward the ceiling as your elbows and wrists are vertically stacked above your shoulders.
    1. You can point your palms in toward each other.
3. While keeping your knees bent to about 90 degrees, march both legs up until your knees are vertically stacked above your hips.
    1. In this position, your thighs should be perpendicular to the ground, and your shins should be parallel to the ground.
4. Based on your preference, you can keep your head resting on the ground, or you can slightly tuck your chin toward your chest to lift your head just barely off the ground.
    1. Lifting your head slightly off the ground can mildly increase the difficulty and allow you to train your neck muscles statically, but doing so is optional. If you opt to lift your head just off the ground, keep it that position throughout your set. Otherwise, continue resting your head on the ground during the exercise.
## Exercise technique
1. Brace your core by tensing the front and sides of your abdominals outward, like you would if you were bracing for someone to strike your stomach with a punch or forcible slap.
    1. In this starting position, your lower back should be near a neutral position with the natural mild curvature you have when normally standing upright, rather than being excessively arched or flattened.
2. Sweep arms backward and downward while simultaneously straightening your legs and lowering them toward the ground. Throughout the entire exercise, rigidly maintain the mild curvature of your lower back that naturally have.
    1. As you lower your arms and legs, you will need to continue bracing your core to prevent your lower back from arching further. Unintended arching would be demonstrated by an increase in the space between the ground and your lower back, so you can focus on maintaining this space each rep.
    2. Strive to move your arms and legs at the same rate through the full range of motion you can without dynamically arching your lower back.
    3. With sufficient core control, you can finish with your arms and legs parallel to the ground as they are fully straightened. From this position, you can gently tap the ground with your hands and heels simultaneously. If your lower back starts arching to a greater degree before this point, shorten the range of motion to what you can perform without further arching.
    4. All the movement should occur from your shoulders, hips, and knees as your spine remains motionless.
    5. Move slowly and deliberately throughout your set, focusing on high-quality technique at every degree of motion.
3. Reverse the movement by lifting your arms and legs up to return to the starting position.
    1. Since the lifting phase should simply be a reversal of the lowering phase, no motion should occur at your lower back as you continue bracing your core.
    2. While keeping your elbows straight, bend your knees as you march your thighs up to finish with your knees bent to approximately 90 degrees.
    3. At the top, both of your knees should be stacked vertically above your hips, and your arms should be vertically stacked above your shoulders.
4. Alternate between steps 2 and 3 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can statically train your [rectus abdominis](../Muscles/Rectus%20Abdominis%201955c6f170d880ffa74fdc1ed9f102dd.md) and [obliques](../Muscles/Abdominal%20Obliques%201b95c6f170d880f5bdc1c2ca4cd25d5f.md) to maintain a rigid back position as you refine your ability to move through your hips and shoulders with a stable trunk.

## Setting up
1. Pick up a pair of dumbbells, and sit down on a bench with your torso upright, feet flat on the floor, and arms hanging straight down.
    1. You can opt to sit down on a seated bench with your back resting against the back support, or you can sit on a flat bench without any back support.
## Exercise technique
1. While holding the dumbbells by your sides with straight elbows, direct your palms forward to adopt an underhand grip.
2. Curl the dumbbells upward in an arcing manner by bending your elbows without rotating your palms.
    1. Keep your wrists straight and your elbows by your sides, rather than swinging your elbows forward through shoulder motion.
    2. While your forearms move through elbow joint motion, the rest of your body should remain stationary.
    3. Since you will maintain an underhand grip during this lifting phase, your palms should be facing upward when your forearms are parallel to the ground.
    4. At the top of the curl, your elbows should be fully bent with your forearms touching your biceps and your palms facing back toward your shoulders.
3. Rotate your palms forward away from you to adopt an overhand grip, which is also called a reverse grip.
4. While keeping your wrists straight, lower the dumbbells in a controlled manner by allowing your elbows to straighten progressively without rotating your palms.
    1. Since you will maintain a reverse grip during this lowering phase, your palms should be facing down when your forearms are parallel to the ground before facing backward once you have fully straightened your elbows.
    2. You do not have to perform an extremely slow lowering phase, but you should avoid letting gravity abruptly swing the dumbbells down.
5. Alternate between steps 1-4 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can develop your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md) while also training your [wrist extensor muscles](../Muscles/Wrist%20extensors%202c35c6f170d8804ab377fe1e53371f25.md) more effectively than most curl variations.

## Setting up
1. In an approximately hip-width stance, face a stable object with a flat, elevated surface that you will use for this push-up variation.
    1. So long as the object can support your bodyweight and will not slide, you can use a variety of objects based on the degree of difficulty you wish to have and what is available to you.
    2. As the height of the surface decreases, the difficulty of the exercise will increase from being able to adopt a closer to horizontal torso position, where gravity can provide greater resistance.
    3. A flat exercise bench (which typically has a surface near 18in (46cm) above the ground) can be appropriate to use in a gym as an initial starting point for many people.
    4. In addition to a plyometric box, an aerobic step elevated on top of risers can also be a quality object to use, since you can adjust the height (typically in 2in (5cm) increments) to match the specific level of difficulty you wish to have.
    5. For a lower intensity variation at home, furniture like a bed can alternatively be used to elevate your hands.
2. After leaning forward at your hips, place your palms on top of the elevated object with the base of your palms on the corner as your elbows are straight, and your hands are mildly outside shoulder width apart from each other.
    1. In this position, your middle fingers should be pointing slightly out to the sides or straight ahead, depending upon what hand position feels most comfortable and stable to you.
    2. Based on your preference, you can spread your fingers somewhat apart from each other or keep them close together.
3. While bearing weight through your hands and allowing your heels to lift off the ground, walk your feet back until your hips and knees are straightened as your arms form approximately 90-degree angles with your torso.
    1. After doing so, you should be able to draw a straight line from your legs through your hips to your torso.
    2. Your toes and the balls of your feet should be on the ground as your feet are approximately hip-width apart.
    3. Keep your neck in a neutral position, as you would normally do when standing upright, which should direct your gaze diagonally down and forward.
## Exercise technique
1. From this tall plank position, tighten your abdominal muscles and squeeze your glutes, which you will continue doing throughout your set.
    1. Contracting your abs and glutes will help you keep your back in a mostly flat position with your hips held up (but not excessively hiked up) rather than letting your hips sag downward, which would result in an exaggerated arch of your lower back.
    2. This should allow you to draw a straight line from your legs through your hips to your torso.
2. Push the ground away from you by spreading your shoulder blades apart as far as you can while keeping your elbows straight.
    1. While prompting your upper back to round mildly, this will lift your chest up a little higher above the ground, but it is a fairly small amplitude of motion.
    2. If you performed this shoulder blade motion when standing with your arms outstretched parallel to the ground, your shoulder blades would move forward.
    3. As a cue, you can imagine what it would feel like if you were leaning forward with your arms outstretched in front of you, and you are trying to touch something just beyond your reach with your elbows fully straightened. Pushing your shoulder blades forward as they spread apart would push your hands slightly forward to touch that object, and you should be performing the same shoulder blade motion during this step.
3. Reverse the movement in a controlled manner by allowing your blades to move fully back together without bending your elbows.
    1. This will lower your chest mildly toward the ground and result in your chest being closer to the ground than your shoulders.
    2. Allow your shoulder blades to move back as close together as they can without letting your hips sag down through lower back arching.
    3. You do not have to perform the lowering phase with an extremely slow tempo, but you should actively control the descent.
4. Alternate between steps 2 and 3 until you have completed your set.
## Description
While statically engaging the [rectus abdominis](../Muscles/Rectus%20Abdominis%201955c6f170d880ffa74fdc1ed9f102dd.md), this exercise can effectively develop the large [serratus anterior](../Muscles/Serratus%20Anterior%201955c6f170d880a8b8b9e712f2ec58e0.md) and the smaller [pec minor](../Muscles/Pectoralis%20Minor%201905c6f170d88030b03dd3f99706ecb0.md) in a targeted manner.

## Setting up
1. Connect your preferred bar attachment to a seated cable row machine, and select your weight with the loading pin.
    1. You can perform this exercise with essentially any row attachment that you can comfortably hold throughout the set, so it is up to you which specific attachment you use. If you are unsure what to select initially, you can use a standard lat pulldown attachment with a straight shaft.
    2. If your machine allows you to adjust the seat height, you can set it to a height that allows the cable to run approximately horizontally during this exercise rather than meaningfully angling upward or downward. A seat height that situates the pulley a little lower than your chest (once you are seated with an upright torso) is normally appropriate.
2. Sit down on the seat, and position your feet in contact with the machine’s foot plates as your knees are mildly bent.
    1. The appropriate degree of knee bend should allow you to feel stable and comfortable throughout the exercise while experiencing resistance throughout its full range of motion. If you lose resistance (from the weight you selected contacting the rest of the weight stack) before you reach the end range to which you can comfortably round your back during the exercise, you can adopt a lesser degree of knee bend to scoot yourself further back.
3. Fully reach your arms forward, and lean forward at your hips until you can firmly grasp the bar you attached.
    1. Specifically how you grasp the bar will be influenced by which attachment you selected, but the grip you use should feel comfortable and stable.
    2. If you initially cannot reach the bar, you can scoot forward closer toward the cable by bending your knees further.
4. While holding the bar with straight elbows, lean your torso backward by moving at your hips until you are sitting with an upright torso.
## Exercise technique
1. In a slow and controlled manner, lean forward by rounding your entire back through your full comfortable range of motion.
    1. You should finish with your back comfortably rounded and arms fully outstretched in front of you with straight elbows.
    2. Rather than moving only one part of your back, strive to round your lower, middle, and upper back simultaneously, which will bring the bottom of your ribs toward the top of your hip bones.
    3. It is normal to feel a stretching sensation throughout your back in this position, but you should not experience lower back discomfort. If you begin feeling lower back discomfort at the end range, it may be appropriate not to round your back quite as much, since you should only move through what is your back’s comfortable range of motion.
    4. While you do not need to perform this step extremely slowly, using a reasonably slow tempo is recommended to help reinforce the controlled technique desirable for this variation.
2. Reverse the movement by extending (straightening) your back in a controlled manner until you are sitting with a fully upright torso position.
    1. At the end of this step, you should have a “proud chest” posture, and your lower back should exhibit the mild curvature it naturally has when you are standing upright. This should result in your shoulders being vertically aligned above your hips rather than behind your hips, which could otherwise occur if you excessively arch your lower back from exaggerating leaning back.
    2. Keep your elbows straight as you uncurl your back through spinal motion while minimizing any hip motion.
    3. You should feel your spinal extensor muscles, which run along each side of the spine, contract to extend your back.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can dynamically train the [erector spinae](../Muscles/Thoracolumbar%20Erector%20Spinae%201bb5c6f170d880a7a719e8f6d05d00a8.md) and [deep intrinsic spinal extensor muscles](../Muscles/Deep%20Intrinsic%20Thoracolumbar%20Extensors%201bb5c6f170d880f58501d5f27212caed.md) that run along the length of your entire back.

## Setting up
1. Add weight plates of your desired load to a sled situated in an area where you have sufficient space for pushing it.
    1. With certain wheeled sleds, you may also be able to adjust your resistance level with a lever that changes its friction. For these sleds, increasing the friction will increase the intensity of the exercise, similar to adding weight plates.
    2. Note that the type of surface on which you will move the sled will affect how much resistance you experience during this exercise. When tracking progress, it is consequently best to compare sets performed on the same surface.
2. Stand centered directly behind the sled in a hip-width stance with your toes pointing straight ahead.
3. With mostly straight wrists, firmly grasp the handles in a position that is comfortable and stable for you.
    1. Position the bases of your palms (AKA heels of your hands) directly behind the handles so that you can push primarily through the bases of your palms.
    2. Sleds commonly have vertical posts that function as handles, but some models have horizontal handles or handles that are angled diagonally. For this bent-arm variation, it is best to use handles that are vertical or angled diagonally.
    3. With vertical handles, you can direct your palms in toward each other and adjust how high up you grasp them. Initially gripping the handles a little below hip height is an appropriate starting point. However, a range of grip heights can be viable, so feel free to try out different hand positions over time to determine what feels best to you.
    4. With angled handles, you can grasp them with palms angled inward and downward.
4. Take a step backward with one foot and lean your torso forward while moderately bending your front leg’s knee and keeping your rear leg’s knee mildly bent. Allow your elbows to bend naturally while leaning into the sled as you keep your elbows aligned with your wrists, chest up, and back flat.
    1. Rather than simply rounding your back, the forward torso lean should arise from you hinging at your front leg’s hip.
    2. The degree to which you should lean your torso will be affected by the height of your hands when holding the handles. As a general rule of thumb, it is often appropriate to lean your torso forward by about 45 degrees, but you should feel free to try out different degrees of forward lean to determine what personally feels best to you.
    3. When leaning into the sled, it is natural for your elbows to bend greater than 90 degrees, with your forearms reasonably close to being parallel to the ground during this variation. Specifically how much you bend your elbows should be based on which position feels the most stable and comfortable while pushing the sled.
    4. Rather than being closer together or farther apart than your wrists (when viewed from the front or back), your elbows should be stacked behind your wrists for stability.
## Exercise technique
1. Brace your core by tensing the front and sides of your abdominals outward, like you would if you were bracing for someone to strike your stomach with a punch or forcible slap.
    1. Continue bracing your core from this point onward to help you maintain a rigid back position as you push through your legs.
2. Begin pushing the sled forward by pushing through your rear leg. Drive your rear knee backward while straightening it and pushing off through your foot in a calf raise-like ankle motion.
    1. It can help to think about pushing the ground away from you.
    2. Strive to push through your rear leg until you can draw a straight line from that leg through your hip to your shoulder when viewed from the side.
    3. While the toes and the ball of your foot remain on the ground, the rest of your rear foot’s sole should be off the ground and facing backward.
    4. Since you are starting with your rear knee only mildly bent, this initial step involves a short range of motion to start moving the sled
3. As you finish driving through your rear leg, push through your front leg to continue pushing the sled forward. Simultaneously, march what initially was your rear leg forward as you drive that knee forward while bending it.
    1. Keep your back flat and chest up the whole time while you maintain the same degree of forward torso lean.
    2. All the motion should come from your hips, knees, and ankles while the rest of your body remains in essentially a static position throughout your set.
    3. Rather than using your upper body to push the sled, your arms should simply function to transmit force from your legs to the sled.
4. Continue pushing the sled forward as you reciprocally move your legs until you have reached your target distance or the end of your available space, and have to switch to pushing it in the opposite direction.
    1. With some sled models, you may have to rotate your sled 180 degrees to be able to access the same type of handles before pushing the sled in the opposite direction. With other models, you may be able to walk to the other side of the sled and access another pair of handles.
## Description
This exercise will train your [gluteus maximus](../Muscles/Gluteus%20Maximus%201bb5c6f170d8805380e7c611cd051f9f.md), [quads](../Muscles/Monoarticular%20Quadriceps%20Femoris%201be5c6f170d880119155c2e8184c0d0d.md), [adductor magnus](../Muscles/Adductor%20Magnus%201b95c6f170d880518436f037bd6a822d.md), [gastrocnemius](../Muscles/Gastrocnemius%201b95c6f170d880b59622dd4a8639aa2f.md), and [soleus](../Muscles/Soleus%201925c6f170d88052bbb6c59dc04f2e1a.md) as they function to extend your hips, knees, and ankles simultaneously.

## Setting up
1. Adjust a cable station’s pulley to be near chest height, connect a rope attachment to the cable, and select your weight with the loading pin.
2. While facing the cable station, grasp each end of the rope with your index fingers and adjacent aspects of your hands contacting the flat surfaces of the attachment’s rubber stoppers. Wrap your thumbs over the rounded outer aspects of the stoppers.
    1. If you are using a long strap attachment with looped ends rather than ropes, you naturally will situate your hands within the loops and grasp the inner part of each loop.
3. With your elbows straightened and arms raised to be parallel with the cable, step backward until the machine’s weight plates separate and you feel tension from the cable.
    1. In this position, your palms should be directed down as your arms are outstretched in front of your torso while you are standing upright with your hands close to each other.
4. With your feet near hip width apart, slightly bend your knees, and adopt a staggered stance with one foot mildly in front of the other, or keep your feet symmetrical with each other.
    1. Utilize whichever stance helps you feel the most stable and balanced.
## Exercise technique
1. Drive your elbows backward while flaring them straight out away from your sides to pull the rope toward your shoulders.
    1. While emphasizing driving your elbows back behind you, your elbows will naturally bend without having to focus on pulling with your hands.
    2. Your elbows should finish pointing straight out to your sides as your upper arms are approximately parallel with the ground, forming a “T-shape” with your torso
    3. Finish pulling with your shoulder blades fully pulled back together and your chest up in a “proud chest” posture.
    4. In contrast to a face pull, your hands should remain in front of your shoulders rather than above your shoulders during this high row.
2. Reverse the movement in a controlled manner by allowing your elbows to arc forward and in toward each other while naturally straightening.
    1. Allow your shoulder blades to spread apart naturally from each other as your arms move in line with the cable’s resistance.
    2. You should finish in the starting position with your elbows straightened and arms outstretched in front of you.
    3. You do not have to perform this phase with an extremely slow tempo, but you should avoid letting the cable abruptly yank your arms forward in an uncontrolled fashion.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This row can effectively develop your [traps](../Muscles/Trapezius%201b95c6f170d880bebf89c759b592e81f.md), [rhomboids](../Muscles/Rhomboids%201b95c6f170d880c8a84de94f5232a509.md), and [rear delts](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Posterior%20Head%201905c6f170d880a29e5ec26f4d257c01.md) while also training your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md), and three [rotator cuff](../Muscles/Rotator%20Cuff%201b95c6f170d880b3b0d8eab69c3a7683.md) muscles.

## Setting up
1. Adjust the machine’s seat to a height that allows you to rest your torso against the chest pad and enables you to row comfortably with your elbow tucked fairly close to your side.
    1. The appropriate seat height often naturally allows you to finish the lifting phase with your elbow bent by about 90 degrees.
    2. If the seat is too low, the upward angle in which the handle moves during the lifting phase can cause the row to feel awkward as you have to shrug your shoulder up and/or meaningfully flare your elbow out away from your side.
    3. If the seat is too high, you may notice that you have to pack your shoulder blade down to reach the handles with your arm directed further downward than forward. This could limit your range of motion and prompt the row to not feel as natural as it otherwise could.
2. If your machine has an adjustable chest pad, set it to a position that allows you to just grasp the handle when your arm is fully outstretched with a straight elbow.
    1. Machines often lack an adjustable chest pad.
3. Add weight plates of your desired load to the machine, and sit down on the seat with your torso against the chest pad.
    1. Based on your preference, you can position your feet against the machine’s foot plates (if your machine model has foot plates), or you can place your feet flat on the floor.
    2. As an alternative to sitting on the seat, you optionally can adopt a staggered stance with one foot forward and the other backward as you lightly contact the seat with your buttocks while predominantly bearing weight through your feet.
    3. Set up in whichever position feels most stable and comfortable to you.
4. Reach forward and firmly grasp the handle with the side you are going to train. If your machine allows you to use different grips, grasp the handle at a spot where you can angle your palm inward to adopt a neutral or semi-neutral grip.
    1. Hold the handle with a straight wrist and elbow.
    2. If your machine has a stationary center handle (that is not connected to either of the machine’s mobile lever arms), you can grasp it with your free hand and continue holding it throughout the set for additional stability. Otherwise, place your free hand wherever you prefer.
## Exercise technique
1. Pull the handle back toward you by driving your elbow backward while bending it. Simultaneously pull your shoulder blade fully back.
    1. Rather than meaningfully flaring it out away from your side, keep your elbow tucked reasonably close to your side to a degree that feels natural and comfortable to you. This should keep your forearm aligned with the direction in which you are rowing.
    2. Pull through your full range of motion, which will typically result in your elbow being slightly behind your torso or at least level with your torso at the end of the lifting phase.
    3. Instead of moving straight backward in a fully horizontal direction, this machine type will normally have its handle move at an upward angle while you pull it backward.
    4. Keep your torso in contact with the chest pad throughout the set.
2. Reverse the movement by allowing your elbow to move forward in a controlled manner as it progressively straightens until your arm is fully outstretched in front of you.
    1. Your shoulder blade will naturally move forward and away from the center of your back, but you can exaggerate this motion by intentionally allowing the weight to pull it further forward than your resting position at the end, which will stretch your upper back muscles.
    2. While you do not have to perform this step extremely slowly, you should avoid letting the weight abruptly yank your arm forward in an uncontrolled fashion.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set and are ready to repeat the exercise with your other side.
## Description
While also training your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md), this row can effectively develop your [lat](../Muscles/Latissimus%20Dorsi%201905c6f170d880109e73f99ab91d4d47.md), [teres major](../Muscles/Teres%20Major%201905c6f170d880dbba32f6bd22e3abe6.md), [rear delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Posterior%20Head%201905c6f170d880a29e5ec26f4d257c01.md), [traps](../Muscles/Trapezius%201b95c6f170d880bebf89c759b592e81f.md), and [rhomboids](../Muscles/Rhomboids%201b95c6f170d880c8a84de94f5232a509.md).

## Setting up
1. Position a cable station’s pulley near mid-shin height, and select your weight with the loading pin.
2. Securely attach an ankle cuff just above the ankle of the leg you will train. Position the cuff so that one of its attachment rings is directed straight forward.
    1. If you lack an ankle cuff, you can alternatively perform this exercise by connecting a D-handle attachment to the cable and then stepping your foot into the attachment with its handle contacting the back third of your sole. However, this page will describe setting up with the ankle cuff, which is ideal to use given its greater stability.
3. While facing the cable station in a hip-width stance, stand with your cuffed leg directly in front of the pulley.
4. Bend over and connect the cable to your cuff’s attachment to its front ring before grasping part of the cable station (with your fingers away from the weight stack) with your hands.
    1. Continue holding part of the cable station (such as by its vertical beam) from now onward for additional stability.
    2. It will be easiest to connect the cable when your working leg is close enough to the pulley that the cable does not provide resistance when connecting it.
5. While leaning your torso forward at your hips, step backward until you are in a position where you can march your cuffed leg toward the pulley while still experiencing resistance from the cable.
    1. It is generally appropriate to adopt a degree of torso lean that positions your torso somewhat closer to horizontal than vertical, but you can decide specifically how much forward torso lean you utilize based on what feels best to you.
    2. After stepping backward, your knees should be slightly bent with your feet approximately hip-width apart.
    3. Aim to walk backward far enough that you will not lose tension from the cable at the start of each rep.
## Exercise technique
1. Brace your core by tensing the front and sides of your abdominals outward, like you would if you were bracing for someone to strike your stomach with a punch or forcible slap.
    1. Continue bracing throughout your set to amplify your stability and performance.
2. Shift your bodyweight into your non-working side’s foot, and allow the cable’s resistance to sweep your cuffed leg forward as your knee naturally bends.
    1. Your cuffed leg should now look like it is in a marching position.
    2. Specifically how far forward the cable pulls your cuffed leg can be affected by the degree to which you leaned your torso forward.
    3. All the subsequent directions will apply to your cuffed side’s leg as you keep your other leg still.
3. Drive your knee backward in an arcing manner through your hip’s full range of motion while squeezing your glute and allowing your knee to straighten naturally.
    1. How far you personally can drive your knee backward will be influenced by your hip mobility. With normal hip mobility, you should be able to at least reach the point where you can draw a straight line from your knee through your hip to your shoulder when viewed from the side.
    2. Strive to have almost all the motion come from your working leg while keeping the rest of your body stationary. This should result in your torso maintaining essentially the same degree of inclination, with your hip bones fairly level and your back mostly flat. It is not inherently problematic for a mild degree of motion to occur beyond your working leg, but having the intent to minimize it can help prevent it from becoming excessive.
    3. Aim to avoid arching your lower back excessively at the top, which can occur when kicking your leg upward as high as you can rather than driving it back until you have fully squeezed your glute.
    4. Try to keep your imaginary belt buckle facing the same direction throughout the set instead of letting it angle out to the side from hiking your working leg’s hip bone up.
    5. Rather than focusing on kicking your foot backward, thinking about sweeping your knee back through hip motion may help cue the intended glute engagement. If you wish to do so, you can hold the full glute squeeze at the top for a moment, which may additionally assist with feeling your glute engage.
4. Reverse the movement in a controlled manner by letting your knee arc forward in line with the cable’s resistance while naturally bending.
    1. You should finish with your working leg’s knee mildly in front of your other knee.
    2. There is no need to perform this step extremely slowly, but you should avoid letting the cable abruptly swing your leg forward in an uncontrolled fashion.
5. Alternate between steps 3 and 4 until you have completed your set and are ready to repeat the exercise with your other side.
## Description

## Setting up
1. Adjust the machine’s seat to a height that situates the handles level with your middle-to-upper chest once you are seated.
    1. This is an appropriate starting point for most people, and it can result in somewhat of a range of viable seat heights. Feel free to try out different settings to determine what personally feels best to your body.
    2. The seat height that is ideal for you as an individual should allow your shoulders to feel comfortable throughout the exercise while simultaneously allowing you to feel meaningful tension in your chest.
    3. If the seat is excessively low or high, the exercise may feel awkward and uncomfortable.
2. If your machine allows you to do so, adjust the stoppers (that are positioned under the arms) to a height that allows you to press through the full range of motion your shoulder mobility comfortably permits.
    1. Ideally, position the stoppers as low as you can while being able to grip the handles comfortably with elbows stacked under your wrists in the starting position.
    2. Finding the optimal height may require some trial and error, but you can initially position the stoppers to the bottom setting before performing a couple of warm-up reps without any additional load on the machine. If you experience shoulder discomfort getting into the starting position or are unable to grasp the handles with proper positioning, the stoppers are likely too low, and you should try raising them. Otherwise, the stopper height is appropriate, and you can proceed to add weight to the machine.
    3. Various machine models do not allow you to adjust the stoppers.
3. Add weight plates of your desired load to the machine.
4. Sit down on the machine’s seat with your back and the back of your hip bones snugly against the back pad.
    1. Your feet should be flat on the ground under your bent knees.
    2. If the back pad is sufficiently tall, rest your head against it. Otherwise, keep your neck near a neutral position, like when you are normally looking straight ahead.
5. On the side of your body you will train during this set, firmly grasp one of the handles with your palm angled down. Stack your elbow with your wrist such that your forearm is aligned with the incline angle at which you will press.
    1. Grasping the handle where it would result in a moderately outside shoulder-width grip if you used both handles works well for many lifters, but you can try out different grip widths to determine where you personally feel best while being able to achieve the aforementioned stacking of your elbow and wrist.
    2. In contrast to a purely horizontal seated chest press, where you would position your elbow at the height of your wrist, your elbow should be lower than your wrist during this incline variation. Specifically how much lower you should position your elbow will be affected by the machine model you are using, but machines commonly allow you to press at an angle that is 30-45 degrees beyond horizontal. Consequently, you can initially position your elbow so that your forearm forms approximately a 30-45 angle with the ground. After starting your set, you can allow this forearm angle based on what feels most natural and comfortable with the machine you are using.
    3. Aligning your forearm with the incline angle at which you will press will naturally promote the appropriate degree of elbow flare during this exercise, provided that you selected a proper seat height.
    4. Hold the handle on top of the base of your palm (AKA heel of your hand) with mostly straight wrists that allow for a comfortable and stable grip that you will maintain throughout your set. Squeezing the handle firmly can help promote this wrist position.
6. Pull your shoulder blades back together to assume a “proud chest” posture that puffs your chest slightly up toward the ceiling.
    1. Maintain this posture throughout your set.
    2. Rather than excessively arching your lower back, maintain the natural curvature of your lower back like when you are normally standing upright.
    3. As a cue for pulling your shoulder blades back, you can think about trying to squeeze a pencil between your shoulder blades.
## Exercise technique
1. Brace your core by tensing the front and sides of your abdominals outward, like you would if you were bracing for someone to strike your stomach with a punch or forcible slap.
    1. You will continue bracing your core throughout your set, which will help your body function as a stable platform from which to press.
2. While keeping your forearm aligned with the angle at which you are pressing, press the handle forward and upward until you have straightened your elbow.
    1. You can think about driving your elbow diagonally forward and upward as it progressively straightens.
    2. Throughout your set, continue keeping your shoulder blades pulled back together, back snugly against the back pad, and feet planted on the ground.
3. Reverse the movement by allowing the handle to move downward and backward in a controlled manner toward the starting position.
    1. Continue keeping your forearm aligned with the angle of your press.
    2. At the end range, you can lightly tap the machine’s arm to the stopper underneath it or stop right before that point.
    3. There is no need to perform this step extremely slowly, but you should avoid letting the machine’s weight swing your arm abruptly back in an uncontrolled fashion.
    4. If your machine allows you to train through the full range of motion that your mobility enables, it is normal to feel a painless stretching sensation in your chest and/or the front of your shoulder at the end range. Some machines will limit the range of motion before reaching this point, even when set up ideally.
4. Alternate between steps 2 and 3 until you have completed your set and are ready to repeat the exercise with your other side.
## Description
With an emphasis on your [upper pec](../Muscles/Pectoralis%20Major%20(Clavicular%20Head%201905c6f170d880ef9b6bd48adbf440bd.md), this exercise primarily trains your [pec major](../Muscles/Pectoralis%20Major%201b95c6f170d880539f8ee236e09d4728.md) and [front delts](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Anterior%20Head%201905c6f170d8805da59fc8f9dc0a59e4.md), which are assisted by your [triceps](../Muscles/Triceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88032be38d4f3e73c9e4c.md).

## Setting up
1. Adjust a cable station’s pulley to be slightly above shoulder height, connect a D-handle attachment to the cable, and select your weight with the loading pin.
2. While standing with the side of your shoulder (on the side of your body you will train during this set) facing the pulley, reach out to your side and firmly grasp the handle with a straight elbow.
3. Take a step out to the side away from the pulley while allowing the resistance from the cable to keep your arm raised out to the side.
    1. Based on what feels most stable, you can stand in a staggered stance with one foot further in front than the other, or you can utilize a near shoulder width symmetrical stance.
4. Rotate your palm to point up toward the ceiling with a straight wrist if it is not already facing this way.
    1. Situate your free hand wherever you like throughout the exercise.
5. Pull your shoulder blades back together with a “proud chest” posture that lifts your chest slightly up toward the ceiling.
## Exercise technique
1. Bend your elbow to curl the handle in toward your ear. Keep your upper arm stationary as it remains directed toward the pulley.
    1. You should finish with your elbow fully bent as your forearm is contacting your biceps or is close to doing so. Depending on the length of your forearm, you may not be able to fully bend your elbow if your hand is about to contact your head.
    2. At the end of this movement, you should look like you are flexing for a biceps pose.
    3. While you move your forearm through elbow motion, the rest of your body should remain still throughout your set.
2. Reverse the movement by allowing your elbow to straighten to move the handle outward in a controlled manner.
    1. Finish with your elbow fully straightened, like in the starting position.
    2. While you do not have to perform an extremely slow lowering phase, avoid letting the cable abruptly yank the handle outward in an uncontrolled manner.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set and are ready to repeat the exercise with your other side as you face the opposite direction.
## Description
Like other curl variations, this exercise can effectively train your [biceps](../Muscles/Biceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88027b895ed4c0bb40b68.md), [brachialis](../Muscles/Brachialis%2018f5c6f170d880c181eed18b5b379fe9.md), and [brachioradialis](../Muscles/Brachioradialis%201905c6f170d8808f8207e301c4acd3b3.md).

## Setting up
1. Securely anchor a long elastic band of your desired tension level above head height.
    1. Based on your equipment availability and preference, you can use a looped band or a tube band.
    2. With a looped elastic band, you can anchor around a pull-up bar or the top of a power rack. To do so, you can initially drape the band over the bar, loop one end of the band into the middle of the other end, and pull that end until it is taut.
    3. In addition to draping the middle of a tube band over a pull-up bar or the top of a power rack, you can also set up a tube band by sliding it through a specific tube band anchor point that can be secured between a closed door and its door frame. Tube bands are commonly sold with D-handle attachments that you can optionally connect to each end of the band if you prefer to grip the handles rather than the band directly during this exercise.
    4. If you are anchoring your band to a pull-up bar that has rough knurling rather than a smooth surface, anchoring the band directly around the bar can increase the likelihood that the band will tear when using it over time. Initially placing a fat grip attachment or hand towel around a bar before anchoring the band can help stop a bar with knurling from tearing a band.
    5. Prior to using it, it is recommended to inspect the band to confirm it does not have any small tears, since a small tear can swiftly become a full tear when stretching a band.
2. Stand directly in front of the band and firmly grasp its ends with your elbows fully bent by your sides. Keep your wrists fairly straight.
    1. If you are not using a band with D-handle attachments, you can directly grasp the ends of the bands with a neutral grip as your palms are facing in toward each other.
    2. If you opted to connect D-handle attachments to your bands, you can grasp the handles with an overhand grip as your palms are angled forward and downward.
    3. Based on the length of your band and how high up you anchored it, you may initially have to reach up to grasp it before pulling your elbows back down by your sides against the band’s resistance.
3. If the band is slack when standing upright directly next to the anchor point, step backward, and mildly lean forward at your hips until the band is taut.
    1. Alternatively, you can kneel on the ground with your torso upright to remove any slack from the band if the band is not particularly close to being taut during step 2.
    2. The appropriate starting position should allow you to feel tension from the band with your elbows fully bent by your sides. Simultaneously, you should be able to straighten your elbows fully without overstretching the band, which can be indicated by an abrupt increase in resistance from the band at the bottom of the rep.
## Exercise technique
1. While keeping your elbows pinned by your sides, push the ends of the band downward by straightening your elbows
    1. You should finish with your elbows fully straightened, where you optionally can focus on squeezing your triceps for a moment if you wish to do so.
    2. While your forearms arc down toward your sides through motion at your elbows, the rest of your body should remain stationary throughout the set. This will involve keeping your shoulders, torso, and hips still, whether you are standing or kneeling.
2. Reverse the movement by allowing your elbows to bend in a controlled manner to raise your forearms and the ends of the band upward.
    1. Continue keeping your elbows pinned by your sides rather than letting them swing forward through shoulder motion.
    2. To train your triceps through a full range of motion, strive to finish with your elbows fully bent as your forearms are contacting your biceps.
    3. There is no need to perform this step extremely slowly, but you should actively control it rather than letting the band abruptly yank your hands upward.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can develop all three heads of your [triceps](../Muscles/Triceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88032be38d4f3e73c9e4c.md), which constitute the majority of muscle mass in your upper arms.

## Setting up
1. Set a pair of kettlebells close together (without touching each other) on the ground with their handles facing up. Angle them so that their handles form a “V-shape” together.
2. On the side of the kettlebells where their handles form a “V-shape” when looking down, stand upright in a near shoulder-width stance with the kettlebells centered mildly in front of your toes.
    1. When standing on the appropriate side of the kettlebells, the horns (i.e., side handles) closer to you should be closer together than the horns further in front of you. If the handles form an inverted “V-shape,” you are standing on the incorrect side of the kettlebells.
    2. You specifically can position your toes one “foot length” behind the weights by initially standing with the kettlebells directly in front of your toes. Then take a step back with one foot until its big toe is just behind the heel of your front foot, before stepping back the same distance with your front foot.
3. While keeping your back flat, hinge at your hips to incline your torso while allowing your knees to bend until the handles are within your reach.
    1. As a cue for hinging, you can think about closing a car door with your buttocks as you sit back while your hands are carrying something. After you have hinged through your available hip range of motion (which should prompt you to feel a hamstring stretch), you can bend your knees further to reach the handle.
    2. More motion should come from your hips than your knees, and you should minimize forward knee tracking, since you are not squatting. Try to keep your shins as close to vertical as you can without rounding your back.
    3. Keep your neck and back near a neutral position, like when you are normally looking straight ahead while standing upright.
4. Reach forward with your hands and grasp the kettlebells by the closer corners of their handles. Angle your palms in toward you with the handles running diagonally across your palms.
    1. Your hands should be directly next to where the top handles meet the horns, and your wrists should be fairly straight.
    2. Due to the diagonal angling of the kettlebells, the bases of your thumbs should be angled backward and in toward each other.
## Exercise technique
1. Tilt the kettlebells slightly toward you on the closer edge of their bases by pulling your shoulders slightly away from your ears (opposite to if you were shrugging your shoulders up).
    1. In this starting position, you should have your back locked into a stable position with the muscles running up the length of your back fully tensed.
    2. The edge of the kettlebell’s base further in front of you should now be just off the ground
2. Brace your core by tensing the front and sides of your abdominals outward, like you would if you were bracing for someone to strike your stomach with a punch or forcible slap.
    1. Continue bracing your core throughout your set to help maintain a rigid trunk.
3. Sweep the kettlebells back between your legs while keeping your torso inclined, lower back flat, and chest up.
    1. You should look like you are hiking two footballs (referring to American football) while moving your shoulders as you would do during a straight arm lat pulldown.
    2. The objective is to generate some momentum and shift the weight into a position that loads your hips.
4. Once your forearms contact your inner thighs, explosively thrust your hips forward to drive your body into an upright position and swing the kettlebells out in front of you.
    1. Instead of pulling with your arms, the power from your hips is what should chiefly drive the kettlebells up. First and foremost, a kettlebell clean is a kettlebell swing, and your hips are the key to swinging the kettlebells into the front rack position.
    2. Finish thrusting forward by momentarily squeezing your glutes as you avoid arching your lower back excessively. Stay tall while looking straight ahead rather than leaning back or tilting your head up at the top.
    3. While you focus on driving your hips, your knees will naturally straighten as well. At the top of your swing, you should essentially be able to draw a straight line (when viewed from the side) from your shoulders to your feet that moves through your hips and knees.
    4. Throughout your set, keep your neck and back locked in the same position in which you started while keeping the soles of your feet fully in contact with the ground.
5. As the kettlebells reach the peak of the swing, roll your arms around them while bending your elbows and pulling them back to move your forearms into a mostly vertical position. Simultaneously, shoot your hands through the handles to allow the kettlebells to rest against the back of your forearms at the top with mostly straight wrists.
    1. Keep the kettlebells close to your torso as you let the kettlebells roll around your forearms in a controlled manner, rather than flipping the kettlebells over and having them crash into your forearms.
    2. At the end of this step, the kettlebells should feel supported by your forearms rather than you having to grip the weights forcefully to keep them in position. Rather than keeping them fully vertical, allowing the forearms to angle slightly inward (such that your wrists are slightly closer to the midline of your body than your elbows) can maximize stability in this front rack position.
    3. You should finish with your palms facing in toward each other and your elbows slightly in front of your ribcage.
    4. If you are not experienced with holding kettlebells in the front rack position and/or you are using rather heavy weights, it is normal to experience some discomfort from the kettlebell pressing into your forearms, but the appropriate position should not feel painful.
6. Reverse the movement by guiding the kettlebells back down in the opposite manner to how you cleaned them. Let the kettlebells fall forward as you swing your arms down while straightening your elbows and hinging at your hips to absorb the force of the lowering phase.
    1. Like when setting up, sit your hips back while allowing your knees to bend naturally and keeping your back flat to control the downward swing with your hip muscles.
    2. Let your palms rotate so that they finish facing diagonally back toward you, while your thumbs are angled in toward each other.
7. Alternate between 4-6 until you have completed your set and are ready to set the kettlebells down
    1. As an alternative to transitioning continuously from one rep directly into the next, you have the option of setting the kettlebell back down onto the ground and resetting between reps. This approach can help with learning the technique if you find it difficult to transition fluidly between reps.
## Description
This exercise can develop explosive hip extension strength while dynamically training your [gluteus maximus](../Muscles/Gluteus%20Maximus%201bb5c6f170d8805380e7c611cd051f9f.md), [hamstrings](../Muscles/Biarticular%20Hamstrings%201bd5c6f170d8802cacc4e4bbc2a290cb.md), and [adductor magnus](../Muscles/Adductor%20Magnus%201b95c6f170d880518436f037bd6a822d.md).

## Setting up
1. Follow the set-up instructions for the [single arm kettlebell clean](Single%20arm%20kettlebell%20clean%202cf5c6f170d880ba964ffcbd097f377d.md), and perform the lifting phase of the [single arm kettlebell clean](Single%20arm%20kettlebell%20clean%202cf5c6f170d880ba964ffcbd097f377d.md) described in steps 1-5 of its exercise technique instructions.
    1. After doing so, you should now be holding the kettlebell in the front rack position. This involves situating it in front of your shoulder with your elbow bent slightly in front of your ribcage, palm facing in toward your other side, and the weight resting on your forearm, which is mostly vertically with your wrist slightly closer to the midline of your body than your elbow. The handle should also be diagonally contacting your palm, such that the side of the handle by your thumb is angled mildly higher than the side of the handle by your little finger.
    2. As an alternative to cleaning the kettlebell, you can curl it up while using your free hand to help lift the weight up under its base and guide the kettlebell into the same front rack position described above. Initially grasp the handle with your little finger closer to one of the corner horns than your thumb to help the handle rest diagonally across your palm in the front rack position. Feel free to perform a cheat curl-like motion where you initially generate some momentum by swinging the weight mildly backward with a straight elbow before swinging your elbow forward while curling it and assisting with your free hand. This is a less technically complicated means of moving the kettlebell into the front rack, but it is not as efficient when using a heavy weight for lifters who are proficient with cleaning the kettlebell.
    3. Once the kettlebell is in the front rack position, you can keep your free hand wherever you prefer. All the subsequent directions will apply to the arm in which you are holding the kettlebell.
2. While looking straight ahead with your neck near a neutral position, keep your chest up in a “proud chest” posture, rather than letting your shoulders and upper back round forward into a hunched position.
    1. Rather than excessively arching your lower back, maintain its natural curvature like when you are normally standing upright.
## Exercise technique
1. Brace your core by tensing the front and sides of your abdominals outward, like you would if you were bracing for someone to strike your stomach with a punch or forcible slap.
    1. Continue keeping your core braced throughout your set.
2. Without moving your arm, mildly bend your knees in a quarter squat-like manner to dip down while maintaining an upright torso position with your chest up.
    1. Keep the soles of your feet fully in contact with the ground during this dip phase.
    2. Your knees should track straight forward toward your toes rather than caving inward.
3. Directly after reaching the bottom of your dip, forcibly push through your feet as you rapidly extend (straighten) your knees and hips to generate upward momentum.
    1. The intent of this leg drive phase should be akin to a jump without lifting your feet fully off the ground.
    2. At the end of this drive, you can either keep the soles of your feet fully on the ground, or you can allow your heels to lift up slightly off the ground while keeping the front of your feet firmly in contact with the ground if a slight heel lift feels natural to you.
4. Immediately after you have finished extending your legs, explosively push the kettlebell upward by forcibly driving your elbow upward as you swiftly straighten your elbow. Allow your elbow to flare out away from your side when driving up, so that your palm faces forward at the top.
    1. At the end of the pressing phase, your knees, hips, and elbow should be fully straightened, and your arm should be directed straight up toward the ceiling with your elbow and wrist situated vertically over your shoulder.
    2. To transfer your leg drive into pushing the kettlebell upward in an explosive manner, you should perform steps 4 and 5 as a continuous movement.
    3. While your forearm starts slightly angled in the front rack position, it should otherwise remain essentially in a vertical position with your elbow stacked under your wrist throughout the press.
    4. Throughout the exercise, keep your lower back near a neutral position, like when you are normally standing upright, as you avoid excessively arching your lower back.
    5. Regardless of whether you lifted your heels up off the ground after extending your legs during the leg drive phase, your heels should be flat on the ground with the rest of your feet at the end of the pressing phase.
5. Lower the kettlebell in a controlled manner as you let your elbow bend while descending and arcing forward toward the front rack position.
6. As you approach the end of the lowering phase, shallowly bend your knees and hips as you did during step 3 (the dip phase) to help control the weight until you have returned to the starting position.
    1. Finish with your wrist in front of your shoulder, palm facing in toward your side, and elbow bent slightly in front of your ribcage.
    2. While keeping it vertical throughout most of the lowering phase, allow your forearm to angle slightly inward at the end, resulting in your straight wrist being slightly closer to your midline than your elbow.
7. After you have fully lowered the weight, extend your knees and hips to stand upright out of the dip position before initiating your next rep.
8. Alternate between steps 2-7 until you have completed your set and are ready to repeat the exercise with your other side.
9. Following your last rep, set the kettlebell down in the opposite manner to how you lifted it into the front rack position when setting up.
    1. If you initially cleaned the kettlebell up, you can let the kettlebell fall forward as you swing your arm down while straightening your elbow and hinging at your hips to absorb the force of the lowering phase.
    2. If you initially curled the kettlebell up with assistance from your free hand, you can similarly use your free hand to help guide the kettlebell down while letting your working arm’s elbow straighten in a controlled manner.
10. Transfer the kettlebell to your other side before repeating the exercise with that side.
## Description
While developing explosive overhead pressing strength and engaging the [quads](../Muscles/Quadriceps%20Femoris%201b95c6f170d88058a905d88715b5e628.md) to generate leg drive, this exercise can train your [front delts](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Anterior%20Head%201905c6f170d8805da59fc8f9dc0a59e4.md), [triceps](../Muscles/Triceps%20Brachii%201b95c6f170d88032be38d4f3e73c9e4c.md), [lateral delts](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Lateral%20Head%201905c6f170d8804b9b6ef12253eec774.md), [serratus anterior](../Muscles/Serratus%20Anterior%201955c6f170d880a8b8b9e712f2ec58e0.md), [traps](../Muscles/Trapezius%201b95c6f170d880bebf89c759b592e81f.md), and [supraspinatus](../Muscles/Supraspinatus%201905c6f170d880efb440c1614caf1c97.md).

    4. If you are not experienced with holding a kettlebell in the front rack position and/or you are using a rather heavy weight, it is normal to experience some discomfort from the kettlebell pressing into your forearm, but the appropriate position should not feel painful.
6. Reverse the movement by guiding the kettlebell back down in the opposite manner to how you cleaned it. Let the kettlebell fall forward as you swing your arm down while straightening your elbow and hinging at your hips to absorb the force of the lowering phase.
    1. Like when setting up, sit your hips back while allowing your knees to bend naturally and keeping your back flat to control the downward swing with your hip muscles.
    2. Let your palm rotate so that it finishes facing diagonally back toward you, as the base of your thumb is closer to you than your little finger.
7. Alternate between 4-6 until you have completed your set and are ready to set the kettlebell down
    1. As an alternative to transitioning continuously from one rep directly into the next, you have the option of setting the kettlebell back down onto the ground and resetting between reps. This approach can help with learning the technique if you find it difficult to transition fluidly between reps.
## Description
This exercise can develop explosive hip extension strength while dynamically training your [gluteus maximus](../Muscles/Gluteus%20Maximus%201bb5c6f170d8805380e7c611cd051f9f.md), [hamstrings](../Muscles/Biarticular%20Hamstrings%201bd5c6f170d8802cacc4e4bbc2a290cb.md), and [adductor magnus](../Muscles/Adductor%20Magnus%201b95c6f170d880518436f037bd6a822d.md).

## Setting up
1. Adjust each pulley from a dual cable station to its lowest height, connect a D-handle attachment to each cable, and select your desired weight with the loading pin of each stack.
    1. A dual cable station that can situate the two pulleys no further apart than your wingspan is ideal to use for this variation.
    2. A dual cable station that has its pulleys rather far apart from each other (often with a long upper beam connecting each end of the station) is not as practical to use. With this type of equipment, the [single arm cross-body cable Y-raise](Single%20arm%20cross-body%20cable%20Y-raise%202aa5c6f170d88015886fdf8eb2580e76.md) may be preferable.
2. Stand just in front of one pulley while facing in the direction of its weight stack.
3. Squat down, and grasp its handle with the arm on the side that is further away from the opposite pulley.
    1. For instance, if the opposite pulley is on your left side, grasp the cable in front of you with your right arm
4. Grasp the opposite cable with your free hand, and stand upright centered in between the pulleys.
    1. Your left arm should now be holding the cable on your left side, while your right arm is holding the cable on your right side.
5. Pivot your body to face the opposite direction while stepping over one cable and allowing the cables to cross over behind your back.
    1. With your back facing in the direction of the weight stacks, your left arm should now be holding the cable on your right side, while your right arm is holding the cable on your left side.
6. Take a step forward into a staggered stance with one foot further in front than the other, and your lead knee slightly bent.
    1. Your shoulders should be mildly in front of the pulleys rather than being directly between them, resulting in the cables pulling diagonally backward but mostly inward.
    2. In this staggered stance, you should feel stable and balanced.
7. Assume a “proud chest” posture rather than slumping your shoulders forward. Allow the cables to pull your arms in toward your sides with your elbows straight and palms facing the pulleys if they are not already in this position.
    1. Due to the diagonal line of pull from the cables, your wrists should be slightly behind your shoulders in the starting position.
## Exercise technique
1. In a smooth arcing motion, sweep your arms diagonally upward, outward, and mildly forward away from the pulleys.
    1. Finish with your wrists near shoulder height as your arms are angled outward and slightly forward.
    2. While you raise your arms through shoulder motion and allow your shoulder blades to move naturally, the rest of your body should remain stationary as you keep your elbows straight.
2. Reverse the movement in a controlled manner by lowering your arms in toward your sides and allowing them to move mildly back toward the pulleys.
    1. Strive to finish with your wrists near your buttocks as your arms are directed down toward the ground.
    2. While you do not need to perform an extremely slow lowering phase, avoid letting the cables abruptly yank your arms downward.
3. Alternate between steps 1 and 2 until you have completed your set.
## Description
This exercise can effectively develop your [lateral delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Lateral%20Head%201905c6f170d8804b9b6ef12253eec774.md), [front delt](../Muscles/Deltoid%20Anterior%20Head%201905c6f170d8805da59fc8f9dc0a59e4.md), and [supraspinatus](../Muscles/Supraspinatus%201905c6f170d880efb440c1614caf1c97.md), which are assisted by your [upper trap](../Muscles/Upper%20Trapezius%201925c6f170d880009e2cf04b5b29b467.md).
